A.label: The Arts
A.notes: Use all A* codes for: specialist and general adult titles, including both highly illustrated and more text-based works. For a hobby or recreational approach. Prefer: a WF* code as the main subject and supplement with A* code(s) where appropriate. Use all A* codes with: other subject categories and qualifiers as appropriate, in particular STYLE 6*, plus PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers

ABC.label: Conservation, restoration and care of artworks
ABC.notes: Use with: other A* codes for works about the conservation, preservation, renovation, restoration or care of any type of art, including buildings, structures, sculptures, photos, paintings, decorative arts, etc

ABK.label: Forgery, falsification and theft of artworks

ABQ.label: Art: financial aspects
ABQ.notes: Also class here: art sales and auctioneering, funding, patronage and sponsorship, curated sales, the Crypto art NFT market, the blockchain art market, art as a financial investment or speculation, commercial value of art, the business of art

AF.label: The Arts: art forms
AF.notes: Use for: works on the fine, visual and applied arts. Use all AF* codes with: the relevant AG* code(s), AGA for History of art and artworks, AGZ for specialist works about technique, and STYLE Qualifiers 6* as appropriate. Prefer: WF* codes as the main subject for more amateur, hobby or recreational approaches

AFC.label: Paintings and painting
AFC.notes: Also class here: painting or paintings in general, or in any medium with no more specific category below. Use all AFC* codes for: works about a painting or paintings, by individuals or groups, including the history of particular paintings, or a particular style of painting. Use with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate, AGA for History of artworks, AGB for monographs of painters, AGZ for specialist works about technique, etc. Prefer: WF* codes as the main subject for more amateur, hobby or recreational approaches

AFCC.label: Paintings and painting in watercolours or pastels

AFCL.label: Paintings and painting in oils
AFCL.notes: Also class here: acrylic paintings and painting

AFCM.label: Murals and wall paintings
AFCM.notes: Also class here: trompe l’oeil, frescos, ceiling paintings, muralism, marouflage

AFF.label: Drawing and drawings
AFF.notes: Also class here: sketches. Use all AFF* codes for: works about a drawing or drawings, by individual artists or groups, including the history of particular drawings, or a particular style or technique of drawing. Use with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate, AGA for History of artworks, AGB for monographs of artists, AGZ for specialist works about technique. Prefer: WF* codes as the main subject for more amateur, hobby or recreational approaches

AFFC.label: Drawing and drawings in pencil, charcoal, crayon or pastel
AFFC.notes: Also class here: graphite, chalk, conté

AFFK.label: Drawing and drawings in pen or brush and ink

AFH.label: Prints and printmaking
AFH.notes: Also class here: etchings, silk screens, screenprints, woodcuts, lithographs, line engravings, aquatints, dry point, mezzotints, monotypes, woodblocks

AFJ.label: Other graphic or visual art forms
AFJ.notes: Also class here: collage, photomontage. Use for: general works or art forms that do not have a specific code in AFC*, AFF* or AFH*

AFJY.label: Body art and tattoos
AFJY.notes: Also class here: body piercing, body painting as art. Use with: AFKP for performance art

AFK.label: Non-graphic and electronic art forms
AFK.notes: Use for: general works on non-graphic forms of art, or art using forms not listed below, including newer forms of media

AFKB.label: Sculpture
AFKB.notes: Also class here: statues, figurines, monumental sculpture. Use for: works about three-dimensional art made in any material, and for works about the art form, or associated traditions and techniques

AFKC.label: Carvings, masks, reliefs
AFKC.notes: Also class here: petroglyphs, small-scale and monumental carvings, stone carvings, carved visual motifs, gargoyles, grotesques, chimera, mascaron, sculpted rock reliefs. Use for: both the technique and works about specific carved objects or carved designs in any material

AFKG.label: Precious metal, precious stones and jewellery: artworks and design
AFKG.notes: Also class here: goldsmithing and silversmithing, Fabergé, arts using jewels and precious gems or metals, Toreutics, etc

AFKN.label: Installation art
AFKN.notes: Also class here: land art, site-specific art, environmental art

AFKV.label: Digital, video and new media arts
AFKV.notes: Also class here: computer, electronic, holographic, virtual, cyborg, interactive, internet, generative, telematic, sound and evolutionary arts, crypto art, video game art, software art, internet aesthetics in the arts, digital visual arts, synthetic media, AI-generated media as art, crypto arts, crypto artists, deepfakes as artworks, artificial intelligence art, algorithmic art. Use for: all works about any of the arts using digital technologies

AFP.label: Ceramics, mosaic and glass: artworks
AFP.notes: Also class here: pottery (including porcelain, bone china, earthenware, terracotta, stoneware, bisque), stained glass, enamelled or painted glass, overglaze decoration, tiles, or enamelwork as artworks

AFT.label: Decorative arts
AFT.notes: Also class here: ornament, ornamental motifs, decorative details, patterns or shapes, faux painting or finishing, decorative metalwork, repoussé, chasing, embossing, metal-engraving techniques, lacquerware, wallpapers and other decorative arts. Use for: works that look at the subject from a fine arts or history of art perspective, or aimed at a more professional, technical or skilled audience

AFW.label: Textile arts and artworks
AFW.notes: Also class here: carpets, kilims, rugs, quilts, tapestries, appliqué techniques, wall-hangings, weavings, knitting, patchwork, embroidery, beadwork, quillwork, featherwork, feltwork, ribbon work, and other textiles or textile embellishments as art. Use for: works about any arts or crafts that use plant, animal or synthetic fibres to construct practical, decorative, utilitarian, ceremonial, or conceptual objects or artworks

AG.label: The visual, decorative or fine arts: treatments and subjects
AG.notes: Use all AG* codes for: works on the fine, visual and applied arts and for the arts of specific cultures, societies, groups, peoples, places, movements, etc. Use all AG* codes with: the relevant AB*, AF*, AG*, AJ*, AK*, AM*, AT*, AV* code(s) and also STYLE 6*, PLACE 1*, INTEREST 5* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

AGA.label: History of art
AGA.notes: Use for: History of specific art movements, periods of arts, or the history of the arts of specific cultures, societies, groups, peoples, places, etc. Use with: other Arts codes A* and also STYLE 6*, PLACE 1*, INTEREST 5* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

AGB.label: Individual artists, art monographs
AGB.notes: Use for: works on both individual artists and named ateliers, collectives, studios or workshops that produced under a single artist’s name. Use with: AGC for catalogues of exhibitions dedicated to a single artist

AGC.label: Exhibition catalogues and specific collections
AGC.notes: Use for: publications that are linked to either a temporary exhibition or the catalogues of permanent collections such as art galleries, museums or individual collectors. Use with: other A* codes to indicate Art form and a PLACE 1* Qualifiers if it is the catalogue of a permanent location such as a specific gallery or museum

AGH.label: Human figures depicted in the arts
AGH.notes: Also class here: figure painting or drawing, illustrations of human anatomy for artists, anatomical drawing, or any art that depicts the human or parts of the human body. Use with: AGZ for techniques of drawing, life drawing techniques. Use all AGH* codes with: AF*, AJ* AK* AT* codes as appropriate

AGHF.label: Portraits and self-portraiture in the arts

AGHN.label: Nudes depicted in the arts
AGHN.notes: Also class here: Naked or unclothed human bodies or figures in any art form

AGHX.label: Erotic art / Erotica in the arts

AGK.label: Small-scale, secular and domestic scenes in the arts
AGK.notes: Also class here: ‘genre’ subjects, everyday scenes and events in art

AGN.label: Nature in the arts
AGN.notes: Also class here: Bird-and-flower painting, the natural world, depicted in visual, decorative or fine art forms. Use for: any depiction of nature in any artistic form or tradition. Use all AG* codes with: AKLB for illustrations, or PS* for art that has or was originally for, a scientific purpose, with AJ* codes for nature or wildlife photography, AF* codes for works about nature, the natural world in any of the art forms, with WN* codes, if appropriate, to give more detail of type of nature

AGNA.label: Animals in the arts
AGNA.notes: Also class here: animal painters, wildlife art, birds, insects, fish in art. Use for: any depiction of fauna in any artistic form or tradition. Use with: AKLB for illustration, or PS* for art that has or was originally for, a scientific purpose, or AJ* for animal photography

AGNB.label: Botanical arts
AGNB.notes: Also class here: botanical illustration, plant illustrations, flower paintings. Use for: any kind of artistic, accurate representation of trees, flowers or plants depicted in any art form or tradition. Use with: PST for works about botanical art that has a scientific purpose, often works that have text about the plants, or reproductions of historic botanical works, or with AKLB for works about botanical art as examples of the art of illustration

AGNL.label: Landscapes / seascapes in the arts
AGNL.notes: Also class here: skyscapes, cloudscapes, riverscapes, river scenes, landscape art, veduta, cityscapes, townscapes, moonscapes, waterscapes, inscapes, Weltlandschaft (world landscape), Shan shui, natural landscapes, scenery, vistas depicted in the arts. Use for: works about types of ‘scapes’ in visual arts, or individual examples

AGNS.label: Still life
AGNS.notes: Also class here: vanitas, nature morte, memento mori. Use for: depictions of small scale scenes of mostly inanimate objects both natural and human-made, essentially, the subject matter of a still life painting, photo, sculpture or other art form is anything that does not move or is dead

AGP.label: Human made objects depicted in the arts
AGP.notes: Also class here: buildings, machines, transport, cityscapes, townscapes or any object made or created by humans depicted in any art form or tradition

AGR.label: Religious and ceremonial arts
AGR.notes: Also class here: sacred or ritual art, icons, votive images. Use for: works about artistic imagery using religious inspiration or motifs, artistic representation of figures, patterns, shapes, calligraphy etc for spiritual or religious purposes. Use with: QR* codes or INTEREST 5PG* or 5PB* qualifiers to denote a particular religion as appropriate and with other A* codes for works on particular types of art

AGT.label: Public art
AGT.notes: Use for: works on art in any media that were planned and executed with the intention of being staged in the public realm, often outside and accessible to all, either permanent or temporary, and which may be specially commissioned for a site or unofficial or unauthorised

AGTS.label: Urban arts
AGTS.notes: Also class here: guerrilla art, graffiti art, flyposting, sticker art, yarn bombing, street installations, urban styles etc. Use for: works about visual or applied art forms in urban areas, inspired by urban lifestyles or environment and in the public space

AGZ.label: The Arts: techniques and principles
AGZ.notes: Use for: textbooks, advanced level and specialised works on techniques, perspective etc. Use with: appropriate AF* or AK* codes to indicate the art form, for example AFF for drawing techniques. Prefer: WF* codes as the main subject for more amateur, hobby or recreational approaches

AGZC.label: Colours and colour theory
AGZC.notes: Also class here: colour science in art. Use with: P* or T* codes for more scientific or technical works

AJ.label: Photography and photographs
AJ.notes: Also class here: Photographic arts. Use all AJ* codes with: AGN* for nature and wildlife photography, AGNL for landscape photography, AKT* for fashion photography, AV* codes for photography of musicians, concerts etc, AM* codes for photography of architecture, buildings, structures, monuments, etc

AJC.label: Photographs: collections
AJC.notes: Also class here: Group shows, collections from named photographic studios or specify groups of photographers who worked together. Use for: works that are or are about collections or curated selections of photos usually with a common theme or principle or representing the collection of a museum, gallery, agency or collector. Use with: AG* codes for specific treatments or subjects or other codes indicating the theme as appropriate

AJCD.label: Individual photographers
AJCD.notes: Also class here: photographic monographs. Use for: works on both individual photographers and named studios or collectives that produced under a single name. Use with: AGC for catalogues of exhibitions dedicated to a single photographer

AJCP.label: Photography: portraits and self-portraiture
AJCP.notes: Use for: works that present an individual or individuals and groups through photos, including selfies and individual models, as well as works on portrait photography. Use with: AJTF for works on the practical techniques of portrait photography

AJF.label: Photojournalism and documentary photography
AJF.notes: Also class here: photographic reportage, social documentary and street photography, event and celebrity photography, photo essays

AJT.label: Photographic equipment and techniques: general
AJT.notes: Also class here: cameras, lenses, film, darkroom techniques and photo processing, retouching and digital manipulation, principles of colour, composition, etc

AJTA.label: Camera-specific manuals
AJTA.notes: Use for: any publication about a specific camera type or brand

AJTF.label: Photography: subject-specific techniques and principles
AJTF.notes: Also class here: aerial, drone, studio, street, landscape, nature and wildlife, portrait, underwater photography, micro- and astrophotography techniques and guides. Use for: works on composition, etc

AJTR.label: Monochrome photography
AJTR.notes: Also class here: greyscale monochrome, black-and-white, sepia, cyanotype, brown monochrome photography. Use with: AJTV for monochrome techniques in film / video

AJTS.label: Light and lighting
AJTS.notes: Also class here: flash photography, use of natural or artificial light or lighting. Use with: AJTV for lighting techniques in film / video or with AT* codes for lighting techniques or lighting design in the performing arts

AK.label: Design, Industrial and commercial arts, illustration
AK.notes: Use all AK* codes for: works that look at the subject from a fine arts or history of art perspective, or aimed at a professional, technical or skilled audience. Use with: STYLE 6*, PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate. Prefer: WF* codes as the main subject for more amateur, hobby or recreational approaches

AKB.label: Individual designers or design groups
AKB.notes: Also class here: design agencies, brands, companies, firms or houses as well as named individuals. Use with: other subject codes to indicate what field of design as appropriate, e.g. AKT for fashion designers, plus AKX for historical approaches, ATT for costume designers, ATDH for set designers, ATS for makeup designers, AKC for graphic designers, etc

AKD.label: Typography and lettering
AKD.notes: Also class here: typefaces, font design and fonts, sign painting, shufa, shodo, khatt and other forms of calligraphy as an art

AKH.label: Book design and Bookbinding
AKH.notes: Also class here: cover design, fine binding, paper marbling, etc as arts. Use for: works on the arts of designing and creating books

AKHM.label: Manuscripts and illumination
AKHM.notes: Also class here: miniatures, illuminated or painted manuscripts, scrolls and codices

AKLB.label: Illustration
AKLB.notes: Also class here: book illustrations and information graphics as an art. Use for: works on illustration as an art form as well as illustration, both contemporary and historical, used for scientific, technical, narrative and other purposes

AKLC.label: Comic book and cartoon artwork
AKLC.notes: Use for: Collections of art from individual or multiple illustrators, or from multiple or particular comic book or cartoon series or from a shared fictional world, universe or series. Use all AKLC* codes with: X* subject codes to indicate the form of the comic book involved, with AGZ for specialist works about the techniques of drawing comic book art or characters, with AKX for histories of comic book art. Prefer: WF* codes as the main subject for more amateur, hobby or recreational approaches or UGL for more technical digital illustration

AKLC1.label: Graphic novel and Manga artwork
AKLC1.notes: Also class here: artwork from any East Asian comic book style, manga, manhwa, manhua, international styles, or from graphic novels. Use for: Collections of art from individual or multiple illustrators, or from multiple or particular series from a shared fictional world, universe or series. Use with: X* subject codes to indicate the form of the artwork involved

AKLF.label: Computer game art
AKLF.notes: Also class here: Collections of art from individual or multiple computer game designers or illustrators, or from multiple or particular video game world, universe or series. Use for: works on artistic aspects of game design, artwork, graphics, video game art, etc

AKP.label: Product design
AKP.notes: Also class here: universal or accessible design for products, Industrial design, designing everyday objects, Design for all, designing for accessibility, transgenerational design, usable design, inclusive design, regenerative design for products. Use for: works about product design in general, including associated trade or brand names, about design of an individual product or types of products, about functionality and safety, sustainable design of products etc. Use with: other subject codes for works on specific areas of design

AKT.label: Fashion and textile design
AKT.notes: Use for: fashion styles and trends in fashion design, general and reference works, works about specific items of clothing, illustrated works about fashion etc. Use all AKT* codes with: AKB for individual fashion designers, with AKX for history of fashion, plus STYLE 6*, PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate, with AJC* for photographic collections or fashion photography, with AGZ for practical techniques for fashion students and designers. Prefer: WJF as the main subject code for works aimed at a general audience about how to dress, guides to looking stylish, practical tips etc

AKTF.label: Fashion and textile design: accessories
AKTF.notes: Also class here: millinery, cordwainer, glove making, fashion and style in bags, hats, shoes, sneakers and other accessories. Use for: works, usually illustrated, that look at aspects of the design, or the aesthetics of different accessories in fashion or costume

AKTR.label: National or regional costume / textiles
AKTR.notes: Also class here: folk, ethnic and traditional costume, traditional garments, national dress, traditional textiles or cloth associated with particular groups or regions, etc. Use for: works that look at costumes of the past as well as contemporary costume. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers codes as appropriate

AKX.label: History of design
AKX.notes: Use with: other AK* and also STYLE 6*, PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

AM.label: Architecture
AM.notes: Use all AM* codes with: STYLE 6*, PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate, with TNKR or ABC for works about adaptive reuse, repurposing, restoration or conservation of buildings and structures, with other TNK* codes for topics that also concern more technical works on building and construction, from an architectural point of view, for example, TNKA for accessibility or universal and inclusive design aspects of architectural projects

AMC.label: Architectural structure and design
AMC.notes: Also class here: architectural drawings, sections, elevations, architectural renderings, floor plans. Use for: works that look at the subject from an architectural perspective. Use with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate. Prefer: TN* codes for works that look at the technical nature of building and construction

AMCD.label: Architectural details, components and motifs
AMCD.notes: Use for: works that examine the individual elements of a building or structure, e.g. windows, doors, roof design, ornamentation etc

AMCM.label: Materials in architecture
AMCM.notes: Use for: works, often highly illustrated, that look at structures specifically from the point of view of the materials they are made from, such as concrete, brick, steel, glass, wood etc. Prefer: TN* codes for more technical, structural engineering approaches

AMCR.label: Environmentally-friendly and sustainable architecture and design
AMCR.notes: Also class here: low-impact, sustainable and energy-efficient or energy-neutral architecture, building and interior design and technologies, arcology, green buildings, ecodesign and environmental design, biophilic and biomimetic architecture, plans for sustainable homes, carbon-neutral building techniques, practical guides to materials, green building projects, passive building design, regenerative development and design, environmentally conscious design, eco-design, Economic and Social Sustainable Design, “green” design, etc. Use with: RNU for works about sustainability and TNK* codes for works about sustainable building and construction, 5YS* qualifiers if work falls into one of the UN SDG goals

AMG.label: Architecture: public, commercial and industrial buildings
AMG.notes: Also class here: agricultural, industrial, commercial and civic buildings, such as, concert halls, arenas, stadia, memorials and monuments, hospitals, lighthouses, libraries, museums, galleries, exhibition spaces, stations, airports, hotels, spas, factories, warehouses, offices, shops, stores etc. Use for: works on buildings which have a primary function other than residential or domestic, and which are usually accessible to large groups of people. Use with: AMR as appropriate

AMK.label: Architecture: residential and domestic buildings
AMK.notes: Also class here: private homes, houses, apartments, flats, lofts, cottages, villas. Use for: works on house design, or about residential dwellings, both contemporary and historical, that can either be purpose built or converted structures. Use with: AMR interior design as appropriate

AMKH.label: Architecture: small-scale domestic buildings
AMKH.notes: Also class here: works on cabins, huts, sheds, tree houses, follies, tiny houses, summerhouses, outhouses, boathouses etc. Use for: works about smaller domestic, but not necessarily residential, buildings and structures, often connected with leisure, holidays, recreation or pleasure

AMKS.label: Architecture: palaces, stately homes and mansions

AMN.label: Architecture: religious buildings
AMN.notes: Also class here: architectural aspects of abbeys, cathedrals, churches, mosques, synagogues, temples and other religious buildings or structures

AMR.label: Architecture: interior design
AMR.notes: Use for: works that look at the subject as a decorative art, often presented in well illustrated editions and aimed at a more professional or skilled audience, including studies of interior architecture and design, lighting design, residential, commercial or other interior design specialisations. Use with: AKB for individual interior designers. Prefer: WJK as a main subject code for more amateur and domestic approaches

AMV.label: Landscape architecture and design
AMV.notes: Also class here: Landscape architects, sustainable landscape architecture, environmental designers, green space design

AMVD.label: City and town planning: architectural aspects
AMVD.notes: Also class here: architectural aspects of municipal, urban or civic planning, smart cities, public spaces, the built environment, urban green spaces, parks, playgrounds, urban furniture, urban architecture, urban land management, etc

AMX.label: History of architecture
AMX.notes: Use with: STYLE 6*, PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

AT.label: Performing arts
AT.notes: Use all AT* codes for: works about any aspect of the performing arts, particular performances or performers. Use all AT* codes with: STYLE 6*, PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

ATA.label: Performing arts: events / competitions / performances
ATA.notes: Use for: guides, listings or other works about any performing arts events or competition, either individual or various, such as film, theatre, comedy, television, music or dance festivals, concerts, gigs, performances, events, guides to carnivals, to costume play events, etc. Use with: other A* codes and qualifiers as appropriate, for example, with AV* codes for music festivals, or AT* for performing arts events

ATC.label: Individual actors and performers
ATC.notes: Also class here: media personalities, presenters. Use with: relevant AT* code to indicate whether specifically theatre, film, TV, radio etc

ATD.label: Theatre studies
ATD.notes: Also class here: studies of the dramatic arts, dramaturgy, performance studies, theatrology

ATDC.label: Acting techniques
ATDC.notes: Also class here: monologues, audition material, advice and techniques, voice acting, voice techniques, acting methods, acting for camera, improvisation techniques, movement techniques for actors etc

ATDF.label: Theatre direction and production
ATDF.notes: Also class here: theatre directors, directing plays, guides for putting on a play or performance, stage management, works about the organisation and coordination of a performance or theatrical production

ATDH.label: Theatre: technical and background skills
ATDH.notes: Also class here: stagecraft, wardrobe, costume, hair and makeup, lighting design and production, scenery and props, stage, set and scenic design and creation, special effects, theatrical sound design and production

ATDS.label: Theatre management
ATDS.notes: Also class here: theatre administration, being a theatre manager or producer

ATF.label: Films, cinema
ATF.notes: Use all ATF* codes for: performing arts aspects only, both for the traditional big screen and made-for-TV movies or for long-form films made for new media, including streaming, on demand or other services (but excluding episodic presentations)

ATFA.label: Film history, theory or criticism
ATFA.notes: Use for: works on national cinemas, history or critiques of individual films, film studios, movie franchises, film reception theory, film studies, film theories. Use with: other ATF* codes for particular aspects and with qualifiers as appropriate

ATFN.label: Film: styles and genres
ATFN.notes: Use for: works about specific styles or genres of cinema. Use with: ATM* codes or other ATF* codes to describe the specific style or genre of film, as appropriate

ATFR.label: Documentary films
ATFR.notes: Use for: works on short or long form documentaries, for documentary film making for the big and small screen, works on scripted, largely factual programming

ATFV.label: Animated films and animation
ATFV.notes: Use for: works about animated films or shorts. Use with: AGZ for techniques of animation

ATFV1.label: Anime
ATFV1.notes: Use for: Japanese style animated films

ATFX.label: Filmmaking and production: technical and background skills
ATFX.notes: Also class here: cinematography, editing, lighting, scenery, costume, special effects, artwork and design, makeup and hair, props, casting

ATJ.label: Television
ATJ.notes: Use all ATJ* codes for: performing arts aspects only, both for traditional television or for new media, including streaming, on demand or other forms of consuming small screen entertainment (including episodic presentations)

ATJS.label: Television: styles and genres
ATJS.notes: Also class here: works on series, soap operas, plays for TV, situation comedies, made for TV shows etc both live-action and animated, fiction and non-fiction, dramas, documentaries, news and current affairs etc. Use for: works about any particular genre or style of television or small screen entertainment. Use with: ATM* codes or other AT* codes to describe the specific style or genre, as appropriate

ATJS1.label: Television: reality shows
ATJS1.notes: Also class here: talent shows, reality competition or game shows, documentary-style reality shows, structured-reality shows, dating shows, improvement shows, talk shows, etc. Use for: works that examine aspects of reality TV or specific shows or types of reality TV or people who participate in reality shows, on TV, streaming services, online media, etc. Use with: DNBF for biographies of reality performers, with AV* codes for specific kinds of reality music shows, etc

ATJX.label: Television production: technical and background skills
ATJX.notes: Also class here: television camerawork, editing, lighting, scenery, costume, special effects, art and design, makeup and hair, props, casting

ATL.label: Radio / podcasts
ATL.notes: Use all ATL* codes for: performing arts aspects only, both for traditional radio or for new media, including streaming, on demand or other forms of consuming audio content

ATLD.label: Radio plays, scripts and performances
ATLD.notes: Also class here: radio drama, audio theatre, spoken word only performances

ATM.label: Performing arts genres: film, television, radio, and theatre
ATM.notes: Use for: the performing arts aspects of these genres only. Use with: other AT* codes to indicate that a work is about a particular genre of film, TV show, audio performance, stage production or with AVLM for works about musical films. Prefer: F* codes for fictionalised works in particular genres, including tie-ins

ATMB.label: Performing arts genres: Action, adventure, crime and thrillers
ATMB.notes: Also class here: works about martial arts, disaster, mysteries, suspense, gangster, heist, spy, espionage, film noir, westerns, action-based war films, shows, programmes or series

ATMC.label: Performing arts genres: Comedy and humour
ATMC.notes: Also class here: romantic comedies, romcoms, humorous infotainment. Use for: works about humour-based or light-hearted films, shows, programmes or series. Use with: ATJS for works about TV sitcoms

ATMF.label: Performing arts genres: Drama
ATMF.notes: Also class here: romance, everyday life, or realistic drama. Use for: works about films, shows, programmes or series. Use with: ATJS for works about TV soap operas or dramatic series, or with ATN for web series or web shows

ATMH.label: Performing arts genres: Historical
ATMH.notes: Also class here: period drama, peplums, historical biographies, historical epic films, samurai cinema, etc. Use for: works on films, shows, programmes or series where the historical period is one of the most important aspects

ATMN.label: Performing arts genres: Science fiction, fantasy and horror

ATMP.label: Performing arts genres: Superhero and comic book inspired
ATMP.notes: Use for: works about films, shows, programmes or series inspired by comic book characters or stories

ATN.label: Internet and digital media: arts and performance
ATN.notes: Also class here: all aspects of Internet as media channel, especially for material that originates online; internet celebrities, bloggers and blogging, vloggers, podcasts etc

ATQ.label: Dance
ATQ.notes: Use for: general works on techniques, studies, reference etc. Use with: JBC* for cultural studies aspects or academic works as appropriate. Use all ATQ* codes with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate

ATQV.label: Dancers / choreographers
ATQV.notes: Also class here: dance troupes, dance groups, companies

ATR.label: Performing arts: directing or directors
ATR.notes: Use for: works about the techniques and art of directing in different types of performing arts, or works about particular directors. Use with: other AT* codes for directing in particular performing arts

ATS.label: Performing arts: makeup
ATS.notes: Also class here: special effects makeup, SFX makeup, prosthetic makeup, hair design, professional and media makeup artistry, stage and theatrical makeup, professional works for makeup artists, cosplay makeup. Use with: other AT* codes for works for specific performance arts or with other A* codes if the work is about makeup art for fashion, photography or with 4CP* or other EDUCATIONAL 4* qualifiers for vocational titles

ATT.label: Performing arts: costume / props
ATT.notes: Also class here: designing and making costumes or props, costume play or cosplay, fancy dress. Use with: other AT* codes for works for specific performance arts or with 4CP* or other EDUCATIONAL 4* qualifiers for vocational titles

ATV.label: Performing arts: production, producing and business aspects
ATV.notes: Use for: works about the techniques and practices of producing or managing in the performing arts, or the techniques and practical advice on managing the business and financial aspects of a production, including the budgeting and scheduling, the finding and development of material, fund raising, managing pre-production, post-production, marketing, distribution and other skills related to producing a performing art. Use with: other AT* codes

ATX.label: Other performing arts
ATX.notes: Also class here: mime, Noh, street theatre, variety shows, music hall, cabaret, juggling, ventriloquism, pantomime, storytelling and storytellers as performers, etc. Use for: Any form of performing art, performance or related performers that does not have a more precise code

ATXB.label: Drag culture and performance
ATXB.notes: Also class here: drag artists, drag balls, drag queens, drag kings

ATXC.label: Circus and circus skills
ATXC.notes: Also class here: clowns, funambulism, acrobatics

ATXD.label: Comedy and stand-up
ATXD.notes: Also class here: Improvisational comedy, impressionists, alternative comedy, sketch comedy, comedians

ATXF.label: Conjuring and magic
ATXF.notes: Also class here: illusions, prestidigitation, card tricks, magicians as performers

ATY.label: History of Performing Arts
ATY.notes: Use with: other AT* codes as appropriate

ATZ.label: Film, television, radio and performing arts: companion works
ATZ.notes: Use for: non-fiction style, companion works to TV series, films, shows, franchises, etc. These are typically uncritical, such as a compendium of characters, or places, or guides to the objects, machines, vehicles, weapons, props, costumes (even if these are purely fictional) or a guide to the making of, or art of a series. Use with: other AT* codes as appropriate. Prefer: FYV or FZ for tie-in versions of novels, novelisations or novels inspired by a particular film, series, show or franchise

AV.label: Music
AV.notes: Use all AV* codes with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers to indicate the specific style or genre of music, PLACE 1* Qualifiers if specific to a particular region and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers if historical

AVA.label: Theory of music and musicology
AVA.notes: Also class here: works on music theory, music analysis, psychology of music, theories of solfège, counterpoint, harmony, melodies, intervals, scales and modes, motifs, cadenzas, refrains, ethnomusicology, aural or ear training, etc

AVD.label: Discographies and buyer’s guides
AVD.notes: Also class here: Guides to both live and recorded musical performances, or buyer’s guides to musical recordings, vintage and collectable recordings, guide to vinyl records, guides to collectable album covers

AVL.label: Music: styles and genres
AVL.notes: Use all AVL* codes with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers to indicate the specific style or genre of music, PLACE 1* Qualifiers if specific to a particular region and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers if historical

AVLA.label: Art music, orchestral and formal music
AVLA.notes: Also class here: works on classical music traditions from different cultures, such as ‘Western Classical music’, Indian Classical Music, Chamber music, concertos, symphonies, sonatas, compositions for voice and instrument such as art songs, Lieder. Use with: other AV* codes, STYLE 6* Qualifiers to indicate the specific style or genre of music, PLACE 1* Qualifiers if specific to a particular region and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers if historical

AVLC.label: Choral music
AVLC.notes: Also class here: choral music of any period and tradition. music for choirs. Use with: AVLK for religious choral music, such as, Gregorian or Ambrosian chant, or other AV* codes, with STYLE 6* Qualifiers to indicate the specific style or genre of music, PLACE 1* Qualifiers if specific to a particular region and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers if historical

AVLF.label: Opera
AVLF.notes: Also class here: comic opera, operetta, Opéra comique, sainete, Singspiel, Zarzuela, etc

AVLK.label: Sacred and religious music
AVLK.notes: Also class here: spirituals, hymns, choir music, oratorios, prayer set to music, religious chanting, liturgical music, sacred or ritual dance. Use for: works on music associated with, or used in, sacred rituals or religious observance. Use with: QR* codes and 5PG* and 6* STYLE Qualifiers as appropriate

AVLM.label: Music of film and stage
AVLM.notes: Also class here: works on musicals, film scores, musical theatre, show tunes, works on the soundtracks of music from film, TV or stage

AVLP.label: Popular music
AVLP.notes: Also class here: Jazz, Rock, Pop, Soul, Rap, Latin, Blues, Easy listening, Country, Reggae music and all their associated variations. Use for: all forms of popular music, as distinct from art music and traditional music. Use with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers to indicate the style or genre of popular music

AVLT.label: Traditional and folk music
AVLT.notes: Also class here: sea songs and shanties, traditional song cycles, drinking songs, sports songs, war or anti-war songs, protest songs, songs based on oral traditions, etc. Use for: works about songs and tunes which have often been performed, by custom, over a long period (usually several generations). They are most often folk songs, country dance or similar types of music, often associated with the folklore, traditions or cultural heritage of a region. Use with: PLACE 1* and STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate

AVLW.label: Global or regional music styles
AVLW.notes: Also class here: ‘World music’, worldbeat, global or world fusion. Use for: works about music that is a blend of two or more different styles or cultural traditions or works about music that do not fit into one of the other music categories, or works that examine any form of music from particular groups, by geographical region, by shared language and culture, by shared socio-economic status, by shared identity, etc. Use with: PLACE 1*, LANGUAGE 2*, TIME PERIOD 3* and 5* INTEREST Qualifiers as appropriate

AVLX.label: Electronic music
AVLX.notes: Use for: works on all forms of music produced using electronic musical instruments, digital instruments or circuitry-based music technology

AVM.label: History of music
AVM.notes: Use with: STYLE 6*, PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

AVP.label: Musicians, singers, bands and groups
AVP.notes: Also class here: conductors, orchestras and other musical or singing ensembles or individuals, brass bands, pop groups, jazz musicians, classical musicians, etc. Use with: other AV* codes and STYLE 6* qualifiers to indicate genres of music associated with musician, with DNBF for biographies of individual musicians or bands

AVQ.label: Musical scores, lyrics and libretti
AVQ.notes: Also class here: sheet music, scores for voices, ensembles, groups, choirs, orchestras, bands etc. Use with: AVR* codes to indicate if the music is for a particular type of instrument and other AV* and STYLE 6* Qualifiers to indicate genre of music

AVQS.label: Songbooks
AVQS.notes: Also class here: songs for easy piano, guitar, or other instruments and voices, etc. Use with: other AV* and STYLE 6* Qualifiers to indicate style of music

AVR.label: Musical instruments
AVR.notes: Use for: works about a particular instrument or their related historical and territorial forms. Use all AVR* codes with: AVQ* for musical scores for specific instruments, AVP for works on bands or ensembles or musicians associated with a particular instrument type, AVL* codes for particular styles of music associated with instruments, AVS for works on learning how to play an instrument, and STYLE 6* or PLACE 1* Qualifiers if appropriate

AVRG.label: Keyboard instruments
AVRG.notes: Also class here: harpsichord, organ, accordion, celesta, clavichord, electronic keyboards. Use for: general works on keyboard instruments or scores for keyboard instruments or types of keyboard instrument, from any musical culture or tradition, where there is no more specific code. Use with: AVQ* for musical scores, AVL* and STYLE 6* Qualifiers if work is about a specific style of music associated with keyboard instruments

AVRJ.label: Percussion instruments
AVRJ.notes: Also class here: drums, bodhrans, bells, cymbals, gongs, xylophones, glockenspiel, bongos, marimbas, vibraphones, tambourine, castanet, maracas, timpani. Use for: general works on percussion instruments or scores for percussion instruments or types of percussion instrument, from any musical culture or tradition, where there is no more specific code. Use with: AVQ* for musical scores, AVL* and STYLE 6* Qualifiers if work is about a specific style of music associated with percussion instruments

AVRL.label: String instruments
AVRL.notes: Also class here: sitars, setar, mandolins, bouzouki, mandola, samisen, sanxian, pipa, balalaika, charangos, etc. Use for: general works on stringed instruments or scores for string instrument ensembles, or types of string instrument, from any musical culture or tradition, where there is no more specific code. Use with: AVQ* for musical scores, AVL* and STYLE 6* Qualifiers if work is about a specific style of music associated with string instruments

AVRL1.label: Guitar
AVRL1.notes: Also class here: classical guitar, acoustic guitar, electric guitar, bass guitar, steel guitar, Guitarra de golpe, guitarrón mexicano, jarana, etc

AVRL2.label: Plucked instruments
AVRL2.notes: Also class here: harps, Celtic harp, lyres, zithers, dulcimers

AVRL3.label: Violin and violin family instruments
AVRL3.notes: Also class here: cello, viola, double bass, fiddle, alto violin, viola de gamba, bowed string instruments

AVRN.label: Wind instruments
AVRN.notes: Use for: general works on wind instruments or scores for wind instrument ensembles or types of wind instrument, from any musical culture or tradition, where there is no more specific code. Use with: AVQ* for musical scores, AVL* and STYLE 6* Qualifiers if work is about a specific style of music associated with wind instruments

AVRN1.label: Brass instruments
AVRN1.notes: Also class here: euphoniums, tubas, flugelhorn, sousaphone, bugle, horns, trumpets, cornets, trombones, etc

AVRN2.label: Woodwind instruments
AVRN2.notes: Also class here: reed instruments, all types of flutes, piccolo, bagpipes, cor anglais, contrabassoon, bassoons, clarinets, oboes, recorders, saxophones, etc

AVRS.label: Electronic musical instruments
AVRS.notes: Also class here: theremins, synthesizers, ondes martenots

AVS.label: Techniques of music / music tutorials / teaching of music
AVS.notes: Also class here: learning an instrument; self study tutorials and books for or about the teaching of music, the techniques of conducting

AVSA.label: Singing: techniques
AVSA.notes: Also class here: learning to sing, the voice as a musical instrument, vocal techniques or song types for choirs or choral voices, solo voices, duets or trios of voices, male or female voices, vocal ensembles, etc. Use with: AVQ* for scores for voice and with AVR* for vocal scores or voice plus instrument, AVL* for specific genres or 6* STYLE qualifiers for particular styles of music associated with the singing

AVSD.label: Music composition
AVSD.notes: Also class here: orchestration, musical arrangement, transposition, songwriting

AVX.label: Music recording and reproduction
AVX.notes: Use for: works about the recording and reproduction of music and sound, both general works and practical approaches. Use with: the appropriate codes from T* or U* for more technical works

C.label: Language and Linguistics
C.notes: Use all C* codes for: specialist and general adult titles. DO NOT USE: code ‘C’ itself, but select specific categories from section C*. Use all C* codes with: other subject categories and qualifiers where appropriate, in particular LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers plus PLACE 1*, TIME PERIOD 3* and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers

CB.label: Language: reference and general
CB.notes: Use all CB* codes with: LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers as appropriate

CBD.label: Dictionaries
CBD.notes: Also class here: Glossaries, monolingual dictionaries, picture dictionaries, visual dictionaries, lexicons. Use with: LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers as appropriate

CBDX.label: Bilingual and multilingual dictionaries
CBDX.notes: Also class here: bilingual or multilingual visual or illustrated dictionaries, unidirectional or bidirectional bilingual dictionaries. Use with: LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers as appropriate

CBF.label: Thesauri / conceptual dictionaries
CBF.notes: Also class here: thesaurus, dictionaries of synonyms, ideographic or ideological dictionaries. Use with: LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers as appropriate

CBG.label: Usage and grammar guides
CBG.notes: Use with: LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers as appropriate

CBM.label: Languages: revitalisation / revival
CBM.notes: Also class here: language revival, reversing language shifts, preservation of endangered languages. Use for: works about preserving languages, revitalising languages, protecting languages, reviving languages, teaching languages that are endangered, extinct or in decline, language as intangible cultural heritage. Use with: LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers plus PLACE 1*, and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate, and with JB* or DS* codes for cultural or literary revivals associated with a revival of a language revivals and NH* codes for historical revivals

CBP.label: Speaking in public: advice and guides
CBP.notes: Use for: general guides to public speaking, example speeches and quotes, preparing or giving presentations. Use with: WJW for wedding and best man speeches or with KJP for business presentations

CBV.label: Creative writing and creative writing guides

CBVS.label: Screenwriting techniques
CBVS.notes: Also class here: Writing for TV, for film, movie scripts, screenplays

CBW.label: Writing and editing guides
CBW.notes: Also class here: general guides as well as journalist style guides, technical writing, letter writing guides, guides to proofreading, handwriting, composition, academic writing, writing research papers, theses, dissertations, scholarly writing, etc

CBX.label: Language: history and general works
CBX.notes: Use for: more general or popular works on language. Prefer: CF* for more scientific or academic studies

CF.label: Linguistics
CF.notes: Also class here: the scientific study of language. Use for: more academic and specialist works. Use all CF* codes with: other subject codes to describe works about different aspects of language and LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers as appropriate

CFB.label: Sociolinguistics
CFB.notes: Also class here: Identity and language learning, language and Identity, linguistic anthropology, sociocultural linguistics, study of the sociological aspects of language, dialectology, gender-inclusive language, gender-neutral language. Use with: JHB* for Sociology of language, JBSF* for works about gender in language

CFC.label: Literacy (Theories of reading and writing)
CFC.notes: Also class here: skills, theories and topics relating to literacy, alphabetical literacy, functional illiteracy, social and cultural aspects of reading and writing, multiliteracy

CFD.label: Psycholinguistics and cognitive linguistics
CFD.notes: Also class here: neurolinguistics, psychology of language

CFDM.label: Bilingualism and multilingualism
CFDM.notes: Also class here: plurilingualism, code-switching, language alternation

CFF.label: Historical and comparative linguistics
CFF.notes: Also class here: etymology, language family studies

CFFD.label: Dialect, slang and jargon
CFFD.notes: Use with: CB* codes for dictionaries etc as well as PLACE 1* and LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers as appropriate

CFG.label: Semantics, discourse analysis, stylistics
CFG.notes: Also class here: pragmatics, lexicology, rhetoric

CFK.label: Grammar, syntax and morphology
CFK.notes: Also class here: Grammatical gender, order of words, sentence construction

CFL.label: Palaeography
CFL.notes: Use for: works on the study or analysis of historic writings and writing systems, the historicity of manuscripts and texts, deciphering and dating of historical manuscripts, including the analysis of historic handwriting

CFLA.label: Writing systems, alphabets, scripts
CFLA.notes: Also class here: Grammatology, Hieroglyphs, Cuneiform, Runes, different writing systems, such as abjad, abugida, alphabetical, ideographic, logographic, pictographic and syllabic systems. Use for: works about different scripts, ways of writing, character sets. Use with: LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers plus PLACE 1*, and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers for works about learning particular alphabets, scripts, character sets, etc

CFN.label: Philology
CFN.notes: Also class here: Cognitive philology, Classical Philology. Use for: the study of language in oral and written historical sources, or the study of literary texts as well as oral and written records, the establishment of their authenticity and their original form, and the determination of their meaning, the study of language preserved in written sources, the study of the structure, historical development, and relationships of a language or languages

CFP.label: Translation and language interpretation
CFP.notes: Also class here: translation studies, interpreting studies, translation theory, translation criticism, language localisation, internationalisation and localisation of language, simultaneous interpreting, consecutive interpreting

CFZ.label: Sign languages, Braille and other linguistic communication

CJ.label: Language teaching and learning
CJ.notes: Use all CJ* codes for: all material for or about teaching or learning of a language or languages. Use with: LANGUAGE 2* and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate and: JN* codes for different aspects of language education. Prefer: YPC* or YRD* codes for language material aimed at children or teenagers

CJAB.label: Language teaching and learning: first or native languages
CJAB.notes: Use for: all material for or about the teaching or learning of a first language or languages

CJAD.label: Language teaching and learning: second or additional languages
CJAD.notes: Use for: all material for or about the teaching or learning of, or in, an additional language or languages

CJB.label: Language teaching and learning material and coursework

CJBC.label: Language teaching and learning material and coursework: culture / civilisation
CJBC.notes: Use for: language learning material that presents different aspects of places where a language is spoken, to teach language skills at different levels. Use with: PLACE 1*, LANGUAGE 2* and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate

CJBG.label: Language learning: grammar, vocabulary and pronunciation
CJBG.notes: Also class here: verbs, nouns, adjectives, conjunctions, phrasal verbs, tenses, idioms etc

CJBR.label: Language readers
CJBR.notes: Use for: purpose-written or simplified versions of texts written for language learners. These are usually graded by language level and breadth of vocabulary. Use with: LANGUAGE 2* and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate and other secondary subject codes to indicate what subject or genre they are, for example with F* codes for fiction

CJBT.label: Language self-study
CJBT.notes: Use for: language learning material designed for self-learning. Use with: LANGUAGE 2* and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate, for example 4L

CJC.label: Language learning: specific skills
CJC.notes: Use with: LANGUAGE 2* and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate

CJCK.label: Language learning: speaking skills
CJCK.notes: Use with: LANGUAGE 2* and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate

CJCL.label: Language learning: listening skills
CJCL.notes: Use with: LANGUAGE 2* and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate

CJCR.label: Language learning: reading skills
CJCR.notes: Use with: LANGUAGE 2* and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate

CJCW.label: Language learning: writing skills
CJCW.notes: Also class here: learning scripts, writing systems, alphabets, composition, etc. Use with: LANGUAGE 2* and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate

CJP.label: Language learning for specific purposes
CJP.notes: Use with: other secondary subject codes to indicate specific purpose or type of language and LANGUAGE 2* & EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate

CJPD.label: Language learning for business, professional and vocational
CJPD.notes: Use with: other secondary subject codes, as appropriate, to give specific purpose and indicate type of language, for example with KJ* for Business, and LANGUAGE 2* and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate

CJPG.label: Language learning for academic, technical and scientific purposes
CJPG.notes: Use with: other secondary subject codes, as appropriate, to give specific purpose and indicate type of language, for example with P* for science and LANGUAGE 2* and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate

D.label: Biography, Literature and Literary studies
D.notes: Use all D* codes for: specialist and general adult titles. DO NOT USE: code ‘D’ itself, but select specific categories from section D*. Use all D* codes with: other subject categories and qualifiers where appropriate, in particular STYLE 6*, PLACE 1*, LANGUAGE 2*, TIME PERIOD 3* or INTEREST 5* Qualifiers

DB.label: Ancient, classical and medieval texts
DB.notes: Also class here: texts from the European Renaissance, Indian epics or Kavya and other texts from Ancient India, classic texts from Ancient or Imperial China, Mesoamerican Codices, or any other classic texts from any culture or tradition. Use all DB* codes for: texts, including annotated versions, written in an early, ancient or classical language or an old or archaic form of a modern language, and not typically readable by a modern non-academic reader. Prefer: the relevant subject codes, for example F* for fiction or DC* for poetry, DD* for plays, N* for History, QD* for Philosophy, etc, as the main subject, if used with DB* codes for works that could be read by a modern reader (e.g. modern translations of these texts or texts originally written in an understandable form of a contemporary language)

DBS.label: Ancient Sagas and epics
DBS.notes: Use for: the texts of classical or medieval sagas and epics, in the original language, an annotated version or a modern translation. Prefer: DC* plus 6EH for more recent Epic poetry

DBSG.label: Ancient Greek and Roman literature
DBSG.notes: Use for: the texts of classical epics, prose, verse or plays, including versions of traditional myths and legends, written by Classical Greek, Hellenic or Latin authors, in the original language, an annotated version or a modern translation

DBSN.label: Icelandic and Old Norse sagas
DBSN.notes: Use for: the texts of Icelandic and Old Norse sagas in the original language, an annotated version or a modern translation

DC.label: Poetry / Poems
DC.notes: Use all DC* codes for: publications using any poetic device or in any verse form, including free verse, fixed verse, blank verse, and poems written in prose form or mixing prose and verse, such as prose poetry or rhymed prose. Use with: DNBL for biographies of poets. Use all DC* codes with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate, or with FX* codes or other subject codes to indicate the main theme of the poetry or poems. Prefer: YDP for poetry and verse for children or teenagers

DCA.label: Classic poetry / poems
DCA.notes: Use for: poetry, poems or poetic works widely regarded or presented as ‘classic’ and typically, but not necessarily, published and in print for several decades. Use with: DCF or DCQ and DB* as appropriate

DCC.label: Modern and contemporary poetry / poems
DCC.notes: Use with: DCF or DCQ or DCR* as appropriate

DCF.label: Poetry / poems by individual poets
DCF.notes: Use with: DCA or DCC or DCR* as appropriate

DCQ.label: Poetry anthologies (various poets)
DCQ.notes: Also class here: anthologies of poems by genre or by tradition. Use with: DCA or DCC or DCR* or FX* as appropriate; for anthologies by theme use with other subject codes; for anthologies by locality use with 5T* Literature of a country, territory or region Qualifiers only to indicate national context where significant, e.g. an anthology of the poetry of Australia or the poetry of Mexico; and use with TIME PERIOD 3* qualifiers for an anthology of a specific period, e.g. the Poetry of the 17th century; and use with LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers only with poetry anthologies where the language of the poems is a key part of the content, e.g. an anthology of Anglo-Saxon poetry in both Anglo-Saxon and a modern translation, meant to be used for improving understanding of Anglo-Saxon

DCR.label: Poetry / poems by form or style
DCR.notes: Use for: collections of poetry by single or multiple poets, where the form is one of the major aspects for classification or search. Use DCR with: 6* STYLE qualifiers for forms and styles that do not have a unique DCR* code. Use all DCR* codes with: other DC* or DB* codes as appropriate

DCRB.label: Poetry / poems by form or style: Haiku

DCRC.label: Poetry / poems by form or style: Tanka

DCRG.label: Poetry / poems by form or style: Ghazal

DCRH.label: Poetry / poems by form or style: Calligram

DCRL.label: Poetry / poems by form or style: Limerick

DCRS.label: Poetry / poems by form or style: Sonnet

DD.label: Plays, playscripts, drama
DD.notes: Also class here: theatre scripts, scripts for musical theatre, for pantomimes, or for any dramatic performance. Use all DD* codes for: any work of drama originally intended for theatrical performance, anthologies of plays or dramatic works by individual or various writers. Use all DD* codes with: PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3*, STYLE 6* Qualifiers where these aspects are particularly pertinent and significant; appropriate codes, including FX* codes, may be added after DD* codes to indicate specific central themes or topics in drama and theatre. DO NOT USE: Qualifiers to indicate when or where the work was published

DDA.label: Classic plays / drama
DDA.notes: Use for: plays, drama or dramatic works widely regarded or presented as ‘classic’ and typically, but not necessarily, published and in print for several decades

DDL.label: Comedic plays
DDL.notes: Also class here: farce, entremés. Use for: different traditions of comedic theatre

DDT.label: Tragic plays
DDT.notes: Also class here: tragedies, revenge tragedy

DH.label: Oral literature
DH.notes: Also class here: stories from oral tradition, such as creation or origin stories, founding myths, founding stories, national epics or myths, global folk epics, ethnogenesis, oral histories. Use for: narrative texts, often at the origin of oral literature, about the origins, creation or founding of a people, a place, a dynasty, a country, a city, or epics, stories and narratives that are an integral part of the worldview of a particular people, or stories that are part of the common history of a particular group. DH can be used for works in the original language, an annotated version, a translation or a modern version or retelling

DN.label: Biography and non-fiction prose
DN.notes: Also class here: life-writing. Use all DN* codes with: another specific subject code where possible and appropriate, to give more detail of the main topic of the work, e.g. SFH Golf with DNBS or JW* with DNP for reportage from military conflicts, if appropriate

DNB.label: Biography: general
DNB.notes: Also class here: general biographical works where there is no more precise code or the person is known in multiple areas. Use with: other subject codes, if appropriate, to give detail of what type of biography, for example, the biography of a famous chef, use with WBB, for the biography of a cancer survivor use with VFJB3, with 5P* qualifiers for biographies of a person associated with a particular social or cultural background that is explored in the biography

DNBA.label: Autobiography: general
DNBA.notes: Also class here: general autobiographical works where there is no more precise code or the person is known in multiple areas. Use with: other subject codes, if appropriate, to give detail of what type of autobiography, with 5P* qualifiers for autobiographies of a person associated with a particular social or cultural background that is explored in the autobiography

DNBB.label: Biography: business and industry
DNBB.notes: Also class here: biographical works about business leaders, CEOs, industrialists, entrepreneurs, company founders, innovators, financiers, etc. Use with: K* or T* codes, if appropriate, to give detail of what type of business or industry

DNBF.label: Biography: arts and entertainment
DNBF.notes: Also class here: biographical works about those in the arts or in entertainment or associated media. Use with: other codes to give detail of what type of biography, for example, ATC and ATF for biographies of film actors, or ATJ for TV personalities, or AVP for musicians, AGB for artists, AKT and AKB for fashion designers, ATJS1 for reality TV celebrities, etc

DNBG.label: Biography: social media / internet celebrities
DNBG.notes: Also class here: biographical works about social media influencers, internet celebrities or stars, vloggers, micro-celebrities, net idols, or others who have acquired or developed their fame and notability via the internet, etc

DNBH.label: Biography: historical, political and military
DNBH.notes: Also class here: biographical works about Presidents, Prime or First ministers, heads of state, political leaders, politicians, political activists, holders of political office, military figures, or figures from history. Use with: other codes to give detail of what type of biography, for example, use with: TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers and N* codes for historical biographies or JW* or NHW* codes for military biographies, or JP* codes for political biographies

DNBL.label: Biography: writers
DNBL.notes: Also class here: literary biography, biographies of novelists, poets, playwrights, journalists etc. Use with: other subject codes, if appropriate, to give detail of what type of biography

DNBL1.label: Autobiography: writers
DNBL1.notes: Also class here: literary autobiography, autobiographies of novelists, poets, playwrights, journalists etc

DNBM.label: Biography: philosophy and social sciences
DNBM.notes: Also class here: biographical works about philosophers, great thinkers, academics, lawyers, judges, historians, psychologists, economists, sociologists, geographers or those associated with any of the social sciences or humanities, including Law. Use with: other subject codes, if appropriate, to give detail of what type of biography, for example, with JM* for a psychologist or KC for an economist, or CF for linguists, etc

DNBP.label: Biography: adventurers and explorers
DNBP.notes: Also class here: biographical works about travellers, voyagers, wanderers, etc. Use with: other subject codes, if appropriate, to give detail of what type of biography

DNBR.label: Biography: royalty
DNBR.notes: Also class here: biographical works about empresses, emperors, queens, kings, princesses, princes, sovereigns, monarchs, royal families or dynasties or others who are considered royal. Use with: PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers and N* codes for historical biographies, or JPHL codes for biographies about royals who are heads of state, etc

DNBS.label: Biography: sport
DNBS.notes: Also class here: biographical works about those associated with sports of any type. Use with: S* codes to indicate what area of sport the person or group is associated with

DNBT.label: Biography: science, technology and medicine
DNBT.notes: Also class here: biographical works about those associated with any of the sciences, or technology or medicine. Use with: other subject codes, if appropriate, to give detail of what type of biography, for example, with PB for biographies of mathematicians, PN for chemists, TN* for engineers, MBD for a biography of a medical professional, etc

DNBX.label: Biography: religious and spiritual
DNBX.notes: Also class here: biographical works about individuals or groups associated with a particular, faith, religion, belief system or spirituality. Use with: other subject codes, if appropriate, to give detail of what type of biography, for example, with QRMB1 for a biography of the Pope, or a QRJ* code for a biography of a rabbi, etc

DNBZ.label: Collected biographies
DNBZ.notes: Also class here: Collected obituaries, eulogies, collected biographical notices, collected lives, collected profiles of people, collected life stories or life histories, collected biographical essays from different domains, group biographies, etc. Use for: biographies of several people in single volume. Use with: appropriate DNB* code indicating area where possible

DNC.label: Memoirs
DNC.notes: Also class here: Personal accounts, anecdotes or recollections of the subject‘s own real-life story. Use for: Memoirs are typically less structured and less encompassing than entire autobiographies, and are often about part of a life (e.g. childhood, a politician’s time in office) rather than one’s whole life. Use with: an autobiography code from the DNB* sequence above to indicate area where possible

DND.label: Published diaries, letters and journals
DND.notes: Use for: works where diary or journal entries, or letters, are collected, including collected correspondence between more than one person, rather than the work being written specifically as an autobiography or memoir, or for works that are collections of things originally published on the internet or as modern, digital versions of journals or diaries such as a personal blog, or a series of emails. Use with: an autobiography code from the DNB* sequence above to indicate area where appropriate. DO NOT USE for: stationery, blank diaries, guided journals - always Prefer: WZ* codes for these

DNG.label: Animal life stories
DNG.notes: Also class here: biographies of specific animals, such as performing animals, racehorses, rescue animals etc

DNL.label: Essays
DNL.notes: Also class here: Collections of essays or individual essays. Use for: essays or causeries on literary subjects, essays on observations of daily life, recollections, and reflections of the author on different topics, essays as criticism or learned arguments, or political musings. Use with: other subject codes to classify collections of essays on a specific subject, e.g. essays on philosophy, economics, science, critiques, politics and society, etc

DNP.label: Reportage, journalism or collected columns
DNP.notes: Use for: works that are usually written in a journalistic style and that were either previously published in a news medium or published as original works. Use with: other appropriate subject codes to indicate the particular subject, for example with JP* codes for political or KC* codes for economic reportage or use on its own for more general works

DNPB.label: Interviews / discussions
DNPB.notes: Use for: works that are collections of interviews, or are presented as an interview, conversation or discussion between two or more people, or works that are recordings or podcasts of discussions, chats, interviews, debates, commentaries, etc

DNS.label: Speeches
DNS.notes: Use for: collections of transcribed speeches. Use with: other code indicating subject where appropriate

DNT.label: Anthologies
DNT.notes: Use for: collections of literary works, usually chosen by the compiler, for example, a collection of short stories, novellas, or excerpts either by different authors or the same author, or around a particular topic or theme, collected posthumous writings from a literary estate, Nachlass. Use with: other code indicating subject or literary form where appropriate, for example, with F* codes for anthologies of works of fiction, DB* for anthologies of literature, XQ* for anthologies of comics, etc. Prefer: DCQ for anthologies of poetry

DNX.label: True stories / true accounts of events
DNX.notes: Also class here: first person true stories or personal accounts of specific events. Use all DNX* codes for: popular accounts of actual events written in a narrative or journalistic style, or for works where people talk about a specific event or episode from their own lived experience. Use with: other subject codes to give detail of the topic as appropriate

DNXC.label: True crime
DNXC.notes: Use for: true accounts about real crimes, criminal acts, criminals, criminal organisations. Use with: JKV* codes to add more specific details of types of crime, for example, for a popular true crime account of criminal gangs, use with JKVM, or for a true crime account of a criminal fraud, use with JKVK, for biographies of criminals, outlaws, gangsters etc, with DNB, JBFK2 for true accounts of sexual assault, JPVR1 for political abduction or assassination, JKVN1 for kidnapping or hostage taking, NH* codes or 3* TIME PERIOD qualifiers for historical crime, etc

DNXC2.label: True crime: cold cases / long-unsolved crimes
DNXC2.notes: Also class here: accounts of crimes that were never solved by official investigations and that remain officially open or unsolved. Use with: other codes, especially JK* codes to indicate type of crime

DNXC3.label: True crime: serial killers and murderers
DNXC3.notes: Also class here: accounts of mass murders, killing sprees, mass shootings, poisonings, stabbings, etc

DNXH.label: True stories of discovery
DNXH.notes: Use for: discovery of a historical or scientific nature

DNXP.label: True stories of heroism, endurance and survival
DNXP.notes: Use for: primarily physical ordeals arising from misadventure, conflict, disasters etc

DNXR.label: True stories of survival of abuse and injustice
DNXR.notes: Also class here: Survivors’ stories, ‘misery memoirs’. Use for: physical or emotional ordeals arising from deliberate mistreatment, miscarriages of justice, victims of crime, etc. Prefer: DNXC for objective or criminal’s view of criminal activity

DNXZ.label: Erotic confessions and true stories
DNXZ.notes: Also class here: sexual diaries or journals, erotica. Use for: True and real-life accounts and stories relating to sex, sexual practices, sexual encounters, erotic episodes or other true accounts of aspects of human sexuality. Use with: 5PRD for true stories about BDSM or other erotic subcultures and with INTEREST Qualifier 5X as appropriate

DS.label: Literature: history and criticism
DS.notes: Use all DS* codes with: other subject codes for literary criticism of specific genres, for example with XR* for Comics criticism or Graphic Narrative Studies, or FL for science fiction studies, with 5T* Qualifiers for works about the literature of a particular place and with LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers to indicate the language of the literature in question, e.g. work about the Literature of Australia in English, 2ACB & 5T-AU-A or the Literature of Mexico in Spanish, 2ADS & 5TK-MX-A, or the literature of Finland in Swedish, 2ACSW & 5TD-FA-A

DSA.label: Literary theory
DSA.notes: Also class here: Reception theory, reader-response criticism, reception analysis, critical theory, aestheticism, African-American literary theory, American pragmatism, cognitive literary theory, Cambridge criticism, deconstruction, feminist literary criticism, ecocriticism, formalism, Marxist literary criticism, narratology, new criticism, new historicism, post-structuralism, psychoanalytic literary criticism, realist, Russian formalism

DSBB.label: Literary studies: ancient, classical and medieval
DSBB.notes: Also class here: Classical reception studies, studies of medieval literature. Use with: DB* or other subject codes as appropriate

DSC.label: Literary studies: poetry and poets
DSC.notes: Use for: critical books on poetry or individual poets and also for general books that talk about poems or poetry, including the appreciation of poetry

DSK.label: Literary studies: fiction, novelists and prose writers

DSM.label: Comparative literature
DSM.notes: Also class here: Comparative literature studies, transnational literature studies, World Literature studies, studies of literature across languages, borders or cultures

DSRC.label: Literary companions, book reviews and guides

DSY.label: Children’s and teenage literature studies: general

DSYC.label: Children’s and teenage book reviews and guides

F.label: Fiction
F.notes: Use all F* codes for: fictional stories, narratives or works of literature published as novels, novellas, short stories or in any other form. DO NOT USE: code ‘F’ itself, but select specific categories from section F*. Use all F* codes with: other subject categories and qualifiers where appropriate, in particular PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers where these aspects are particularly pertinent and significant. N.B. F* codes may be used with appropriate non-fiction categories to indicate key settings or topics of the narrative, but for all adult fiction the primary category must be an F* code. FX* codes may be used to indicate a strong underlying theme. Also use with 5H*, 5J*, 5L* or 5P* qualifiers when these represent a significant topic or part of the appeal of the narrative. FY* codes may be used to indicate special features of a fiction title

FB.label: Fiction: literary and general non-genre
FB.notes: Also class here: Literary fiction. Use for: works of literary and general non-genre fiction where either the date is unknown or where neither ‘classic’ nor ‘contemporary’ are applicable. Use all FB* codes with: FX* or FY* codes to give greater detail about themes or features where applicable. FB* codes may be used as the main code with genre fiction codes where a literary novel is also considered to be a significant example of the genre. Prefer: FBA or FBC wherever appropriate, and prefer a genre fiction code as the main subject when this is more appropriate

FBA.label: Modern and contemporary fiction: literary and general
FBA.notes: Also class here: Contemporary literary fiction. Use for: works of literary and non-genre fiction first published in the last few decades. Use with: FX* or FY* codes to give greater detail about themes or features where applicable

FBAN.label: Street fiction / urban fiction
FBAN.notes: Also class here: street lit, hip-hop fiction, ‘gritty drama’. Use for: stories, usually set in urban, inner-city enclaves, that are often dark, focusing on the underside of city life

FBC.label: Classic fiction: literary and general
FBC.notes: Also class here: Classic literary fiction. Use for: works of literary and general non-genre fiction widely regarded or presented as ‘classic’ and typically but not necessarily published and in print for several decades. Prefer: ‘classic’ headings for genre fiction where available

FC.label: Biographical fiction / autobiographical fiction
FC.notes: Also class here: fictional life writing, autobiographical stories, autofiction. Use for: highly fictionalised accounts of the lives of real people (including fictionalised autobiographies) or where an author is using fictionalised versions of real life memories or experiences from their own life as an integral and major part of the narrative or story. Use with: FV as appropriate

FD.label: Speculative fiction
FD.notes: Use for: works of fiction that speculate about different realities from the actual recognisable world, or other worlds or universes, using elements of science, supernatural, paranormal, futuristic or other imaginative elements that are not part of everyday reality as a major theme of the story. Use all FD* codes with: other F* codes as appropriate, with 6JM - Indigenous Futurisms - for Indigenous speculative fiction, with other 5* INTEREST and 6* STYLE qualifiers for particular types of speculative fiction

FDB.label: Dystopian and utopian fiction
FDB.notes: Use for: any fiction set in an ideal or utopian society, or a dysfunctional or degraded society. Use with: FL* or other F* codes as appropriate

FDK.label: Alternative history fiction
FDK.notes: Also class here: Uchronia. Use for: any work of speculative fiction, set in an imagined version of our world that might have emerged had key historical events happened differently e.g. outcome of WW2, or alternate history in which one or more historical events have occurred but are resolved differently than in actual history. Use with: FLG or other FL* codes for alternate history as science fiction stories that feature the tropes of time travel between histories, the psychic awareness of the existence of an alternative universe, by the inhabitants of a given universe; and time travel that divides history into various timestreams, cross-time stories, rival parallel time worlds, with FMH codes for historical fantasy based on an alternate history or historical divergences

FDM.label: Black Speculative fiction
FDM.notes: Use with: FL* for Black Science Fiction, or FK* or FM* or FN* codes as appropriate, with 6AR for Afrofuturism (African-American / Black American/ African diaspora speculative fiction), or with 6AS Africanfuturism (African speculative fiction) or with other subject codes or qualifiers as appropriate

FDV.label: Metaphysical / philosophical fiction
FDV.notes: Use for: fiction that explores, or is based on, some form of philosophy or system of thought, fiction where a significant portion of the content is devoted to the sort of questions normally addressed in philosophy

FF.label: Crime and / or mystery fiction
FF.notes: Use all FF* codes for: Stories about crimes, or mysteries to be solved, locked room mysteries, whodunits, heists and capers novels, crime novels, detective stories, murder mysteries, cold cases, unsolved crimes, etc. Use all FF* codes with: other codes for different types of crime fiction that do not have a unique code, for example, with PLACE 1* qualifiers for regional crime fiction, FK* for horror crime fiction, FL* for science fiction crime

FFC.label: Classic crime and mystery fiction
FFC.notes: Also class here: Classic whodunit stories. Use for: works of crime fiction widely regarded or presented as ‘classic’ and typically, but not necessarily, published and in print for several decades

FFD.label: Crime and mystery: private investigator / amateur detectives
FFD.notes: Also class here: Amateur sleuths, religious sleuths, private investigators, silver-haired sleuths, accidental detectives. Use for: stories where the main investigator is not an official police or judicial investigator

FFH.label: Historical crime and mysteries
