Use for: works about the movement of individuals or groups from one socio-economic group to another, or the ability to do this, or government policies to facilitate social mobility, or works about the maintenance and continuation of existing social relations, the opposite of social mobility. Use with: JBSA and 5PD* qualifiers as appropriate

JBFU.label: Animals and society / Animal rights - issues and debates
JBFU.notes: Also class here: works that look at debates around topics like animal rights, vivisection and experimentation on animals, hunting and other blood sports, animal welfare, the use of animals for food, as resources, or as commodities, keeping animals as pets, human impact on the animal world, debates on speciesism, and treatment of animals based on religious doctrines

JBFV.label: Ethical issues, topics and debates
JBFV.notes: Use with: other categories to indicate works that treat a subject as an ethical debate, or ethical or moral dilemmas and where there is no specific JBFV* code

JBFV1.label: Ethical issues, topics and debates: reproductive health, abortion and birth control
JBFV1.notes: Also class here: debates on the access to birth control, debates about abortion and abortion services, family planning, reproductive rights, access to information about reproductive health, provision for women of sexual and reproductive healthcare and information, access to family planning

JBFV2.label: Ethical issues: capital punishment
JBFV2.notes: Also class here: the death penalty

JBFV3.label: Ethical issues: censorship / freedom of expression
JBFV3.notes: Also class here: debates around freedom of speech, censorship vs security, censorship in schools, universities and libraries, book banning and banned books, debates on limitations or restrictions to freedom of speech, freedom to protest, or works that look at government, institutions or corporations restricting freedom expressions through laws, manipulation or control of information, scapegoating marginalised groups or minorities to restrict freedoms, etc

JBFV4.label: Ethical issues: euthanasia and right to die
JBFV4.notes: Also class here: assisted suicide, assisted death. Use with: LNT for legal aspects

JBFV5.label: Ethical issues: scientific, technological and medical developments
JBFV5.notes: Also class here: Ethical challenges, debates, issues or dilemmas linked to, or the Impact on societies and culture of, things like artificial intelligence, social technology, surveillance society, mass data collection, medical advances, etc

JBFV6.label: Ethical issues and debates: Competing or conflicting rights
JBFV6.notes: Also class here: Value pluralism, ethical pluralism, moral pluralism. Use for: works that examine debates about when the rights of an individual or group conflict with the rights of another individual or group, or to situations where citizens’ constitutional and legal rights clash, such as debates of religious freedom versus secular freedoms, free speech versus protection from hate speech or protection of privacy, collective identity rights versus individual identity freedoms, minority versus majority rights, paradox of tolerance, balance of individual rights vs collective rights, the right to protest vs the rights or needs of state or individual security, etc

JBFW.label: Sex and sexuality, social aspects
JBFW.notes: Also class here: Sex and sexuality studies, sexual cultures. Use for: general interest works on sex and society, works on social and cultural aspects of sexual and reproductive health, pornography and the sex industry, sex work and prostitution, or works that look at questions about human sexuality in particular societies, general works about how humans experience and express themselves sexually, cultural or societal attitudes towards or norms and controls around human sexuality, repression and criminalisation of sexuality, attitudes to contraception, attitudes to education and information about sex in society, etc

JBFX.label: Social attitudes
JBFX.notes: Also class here: political correctness, societal attitudes, changing attitudes, individual or collective attitudes. Use for: general works about social, political and moral attitudes in societies. Use with: other categories for attitudes towards particular subjects or groups

JBG.label: Popular beliefs
JBG.notes: Also class here: popular piety, historical superstitions, popular religion. Use with: NHTB for works looking at historical aspects of popular beliefs, or with VXQ* codes for works about particular popular beliefs about the paranormal, or unexplained phenomena, or mysteries

JBGB.label: Folklore studies / Study of myth
JBGB.notes: Use for: non-fiction studies of traditional stories or material, verbal or customary folklore; folkloristics, studies of folk religions or traditions, studies of urban and contemporary myths and legends; studies of the origins of myths, fairy tales, tall stories, paranormal tales, supernatural beings, old wives’ tales, popular superstitions etc; specialist works about the origin of the stories of things like Atlantis, the Holy Grail, the Hidden Folk, the Bermuda Triangle, the Green Man, the bogeyman etc. Prefer: QR* codes for the spiritual or religious aspects of mythology or VX* codes for more popular approaches or FN* codes for the stories themselves

JBGX.label: Conspiracy theories
JBGX.notes: Also class here: hoaxes, cover ups, denialism, etc. Use for: works that examine conspiracy theories in general, or the reasons for their existence, or look at individual theories, or set out arguments for or against a particular theory

JBS.label: Social groups, communities and identities
JBS.notes: Also class here: general works on social groups, groups with shared identities, works that look at aspects of social units with commonalities (communities), or different forms of studies of communities and their development, or works on compounded identities (intersectionality), works that look at personal or collective identities, Social stratification, general works about intersectionality or particular theories or schools of thought or research about intersectionality, or works that look how individuals’ various social and political identities result in unique combinations of discrimination and privilege. Use all JBS* codes with: other codes for specific topics, such as JBFA for discrimination, JP* codes for works on identity politics, NHTB for social history, FX* for novels and INTEREST 5* Qualifiers as appropriate

JBSA.label: Social classes
JBSA.notes: Also class here: class conflict, social stratification, socio-economic groups. Use for: works that examine class, a particular class, characteristics and distinctions of that class, interaction between different strata of society, perceptions and prejudices about particular classes. Use with: 5PD* Qualifiers to indicate works about particular socio-economic groups, with JBFQ for works about movement from one social class to another

JBSB.label: Indigenous reservation / reserve communities or equivalents
JBSB.notes: Also class here: Reservation life, Rez Lit. Use for: works that look at Indigenous groups living on reservations, reserves or equivalents, on land set aside for First Nations under Treaties, Land governed by Native American Tribal Nations, Indigenous territory or Indigenous land, Native Community Lands. Use with: F* codes for fiction where the main theme is about life on a reservation or similar communities

JBSC.label: Rural communities / rural life
JBSC.notes: Also class here: small settlements in rural areas, people living in the countryside, semi-rural areas, isolated communities, farming communities, country life, rural studies, people living and working in rural areas. Use with: F* codes for rural fiction

JBSD.label: Urban communities / city life
JBSD.notes: Also class here: urban studies, life in the city, inner cities, city and town dwellers. Use for: any works on aspects of life or issues in urban or semi-urban settings and the associated communities. Use with: other subject codes for effects on urban communities or studies of things like urban decay, gentrification, commuters, urban regeneration and urban communities

JBSD1.label: Suburban communities / suburban life
JBSD1.notes: Also class here: suburban lifestyles, suburbia, commuter belt communities, dormitory towns, exurbs, outskirts of metropolitan areas, people who live or work in suburban areas, studies of suburban mentalities or attitudes. Use with: F* codes for suburban fiction, or fiction where the main theme is about suburban life

JBSE.label: Small town communities / small town life
JBSE.notes: Also class here: small town life, people who live and work in small towns, studies of small town mentalities or attitudes. Use with: F* codes for small town fiction, or fiction where the main theme is about small town life

JBSF.label: Gender studies, gender groups
JBSF.notes: Use for: works that examine social roles based on the sex of the person (gender role) or personal identification of one’s own gender based on an internal awareness (gender identity), as well as works that look at sex (based on the anatomy of an individual’s reproductive system, and secondary sex characteristics), including intersex people. Use all JBSF* codes with: other subject codes that explore gender topics in particular areas, e.g. with MB* for works that examine gender or sex differences in medicine, or JB* for works about gender in culture, JBFA for works on gender equality or gender-based discrimination, or F* codes for fiction where the main theme is gender, etc

JBSF1.label: Gender studies: women and girls
JBSF1.notes: Also class here: Women’s studies. Use with: other subject codes when a work is primarily about women or girls, such as JBFA for discrimination based on gender or sexism or misogyny, NHTB for women’s history, JBFK* or JKVN for works that look at violence or violent crimes against women, JM* for psychology titles, VF* codes for advice on different health and wellbeing topics for women, or with DS* codes for literary studies or theory, or other subject codes as appropriate

JBSF11.label: Feminism and feminist theory
JBSF11.notes: Also class here: Women’s liberation movement, First-wave, Second-wave, Third-wave and Fourth-wave feminism, Radical feminism, Intersectional feminism, Neo-feminism, Post-feminism, Analytical feminism, Individualist feminism, Liberal or mainstream feminism, Materialist feminism, Social feminism, Post-structural feminism, Feminist separatism, Neo feminism, Post feminism, Afro-feminism, Black feminism, Indigenous feminism, Use for: general works on feminism or about particular feminist movements, theories or schools of thought. Use with: other codes for different types of feminism, such as RNA for ecofeminism, JPFB for Anarcha-feminism, QRM for Christian feminism, QRP for Islamic feminism, JPFC for Marxist Feminism, QD* for feminist topics in philosophy, JBSF3 for Transfeminism, QRVG for Feminist theology

JBSF2.label: Gender studies: men and boys
JBSF2.notes: Also class here: Men’s studies, topics around masculinity. Use with: other subject codes when a work is primarily about men or boys

JBSF3.label: Gender studies: ‘trans’, transgender people and gender variance
JBSF3.notes: Also class here: transsexual, transgender, gender non-conforming, non-binary, genderqueer, gender minority, two spirit, third gender etc. Use for: works that look at those whose gender is different (wholly or partially) from that assigned to them at birth, or gender variance in cultures which have established more than two genders. Use with: JBFA for issues around discrimination and transphobia / transmisia, JBFK* or JKVN for works that look at anti-trans violence or hate crimes, VF* codes for advice on different health and well being topics, etc plus 5PT Qualifier, as appropriate

JBSJ.label: LGBTQIA+ Studies / topics
JBSJ.notes: Also class here: queer studies, sexual diversity studies, gay and lesbian studies, gender, sexual, and romantic minorities studies, queer theory. Use for: studies of sexuality, sexual orientation and associated identity-based groups or cultures. Use with: other codes for specific LGBTQIA+ topics, e.g. JBFA for homophobia / homomisia or issues around discrimination or NHTB for LGBTQ+ history, or JBFK* or JKVN for works that look at Anti-LGBTQ+ violence or hate crimes, VF* codes for advice on different topics, etc. plus 5P* INTEREST Qualifiers, as appropriate

JBSJ2.label: LGBTQIA+ topics: coming out
JBSJ2.notes: Use for: works that examine, or give advice about, an LGBTQIA+ person‘s process of, or journey to, recognition, personal acceptance and disclosure to others of their sexual orientation or gender identity. Use with: other subject codes and 5P* qualifiers as appropriate

JBSL.label: Ethnic studies / Ethnicity
JBSL.notes: Also class here: Diaspora studies. Use for: works about the study of the histories, experiences, cultures, and issues of ethnic groups or groups who share a common cultural heritage. Use with: other subject codes for interdisciplinary studies and PLACE 1* and 5PB* values from INTEREST 5* Qualifiers, as appropriate or other J* or N* codes for topics like ethnic violence or conflict, debates on multiculturalism in specific domains, such as migration, JHMC for Ethnography or Ethnology

JBSL1.label: Ethnic groups and multicultural studies
JBSL1.notes: Also class here: race relations, ethnic minorities, multiculturalism, pluriculturalism, polyethnicity. Use for: works on social and cultural topics linked to multicultural societies, or works that look at particular ethnic groups, or cultural groups. Use with: PLACE 1* and INTEREST 5P* as appropriate and with LANGUAGE 2* qualifiers for studies of groups linked by a common language

JBSL11.label: Indigenous peoples / Indigeneity
JBSL11.notes: Also class here: Indigenous Studies. Use with: other subject codes for works about Indigenous peoples

JBSL13.label: Mixed heritage / Multiracial groups or people
JBSL13.notes: Also class here: bicultural, multicultural, mixed-race, biracial, multiracial, multiethnic groups or people

JBSP.label: Age groups and generations
JBSP.notes: Use for: works that look at different generations, or topics, issues, problems for different generations or generational misunderstandings or conflicts, intergenerational or multigenerational topics, etc. Use all JBSP* codes with: other subject codes for works that look the generational or age groups aspects of a topic, for example JHB* for sociological approaches to topics around aging

JBSP1.label: Age groups: children
JBSP1.notes: Also class here: Childhood studies, children’s studies

JBSP2.label: Age groups: adolescents
JBSP2.notes: Use for: works about teenagers, youths. Use with: with other subject codes for works that look at youth culture or topics that relate to young people, for example JPVH for works about Youth Rights or Rights of Young people, JBFK* for works about youth or teenage violence

JBSP3.label: Age groups: adults
JBSP3.notes: Use for: works about adulthood, works that look at or are studies of adults or aspects of adulthood

JBSP4.label: Age groups: the elderly / old age
JBSP4.notes: Use for: works about seniors, elders, pensioners, older retirees

JBSP9.label: Future generations
JBSP9.notes: Use for: works that examine hypothetical groups of people as yet unborn, works that look at Intergenerational equity for future generations. Use with: L* codes for works looking at the legal rights of future generations, or with other relevant codes looking at philosophical, religious, environmental, economic, political topics relating to future generations

JBSR.label: Social groups: religious groups and communities
JBSR.notes: Use with: 5PG* values from INTEREST 5* Qualifiers and QR* codes as appropriate

JBSW.label: Social groups: alternative lifestyles / subcultures
JBSW.notes: Use for: groups associated with lifestyles that are diverse in regards to the mainstream or perceived to be outside the cultural norms, for example, counterculture movements, alternative movements, groups who are marginalised because they are perceived as not being part of the “normal”, underground movements, antiestablishment groups, Bohemian cultures and lifestyles, subcultures associated with fandoms

JBSY.label: Social groups: clubs and societies
JBSY.notes: Also class here: voluntary association or ‘elective affinities’, how and why people join and associate themselves with specific groups, such as fan clubs, fan groups, sport supporters groups, youth organisations, common interest associations, learned societies, professional associations, etc

JH.label: Sociology and anthropology
JH.notes: Use all JH* codes for: textbooks or academic and specialist works. Use with: other J* codes indicating specific topics where appropriate

JHB.label: Sociology
JHB.notes: Use with: other subject categories for works that are about the sociology of something, sociological studies, applied sociology, or a sociological approach to a topic, when there is no more specific code for that topic, for example for military sociology use with JW* codes, for fiscal sociology use with KFFD, for rural sociology use with JBSC, for sociology of religion and belief systems use with QR*, LAQ for Sociology of law, ATF for sociology of film, JBC* for Sociology of culture, JN* codes for Sociology of Education, etc

JHBK.label: Sociology: family, kinship and relationships
JHBK.notes: Also class here: human development and family sciences. Use for: works about family structures; relationships within families, social networks, peer-groups, friendships; sociology of physical and emotional relationships with other people; social control or conformity within groups or families; co-dependency in families; works that look at how people develop physically, emotionally and socially within the context of family and society; different types of traditional and non-traditional family structures; works about found family or family of choice; extended families or kinship, works that look at different types of kinship including things like ancestors, ancestry, forebears, descents, kinship relationship, bonds of kinship, extended kinship groups or communities, structures based on kinship

JHBL.label: Sociology: work and labour
JHBL.notes: Also class here: sociology of employment / unemployment, labour studies, industrial sociology

JHBZ.label: Sociology: death and dying
JHBZ.notes: Use for: works that examine the relationships between society and death, dying and grief; how societies deal with the end of life and with death; attitudes and taboos around mortality, death and dying; customs, ceremonies and traditions around funerals, death or the dead; how societies deal with grief, bereavement and mourning and the bereaved; death literacy

JHM.label: Anthropology
JHM.notes: Also class here: Anthropological studies. Use with: other subject categories for works that are about the anthropology of something, when there is no more specific code for that topic, for example, with CF* for linguistic anthropology, PSXE for biological anthropology, NK* for Archaeological anthropology

JHMC.label: Social and cultural anthropology
JHMC.notes: Also class here: ethnography, kinship and family, Institutional anthropology, sociocultural anthropology, Culture Theory. Use with: other J* codes for different specialities in anthropology

JK.label: Social services and welfare, criminology
JK.notes: Use all JK* codes with: 4TM for revision and study guides, 4CP for vocational or professional qualifications, 4Z* for specific national qualifications

JKS.label: Social welfare, social policy and social services
JKS.notes: Also class here: human services, social care, social security policy, social care research, provision of and access to welfare, social care and healthcare, the social aspects of the policies, provision of, or access to social welfare, social care or health services, healthcare, health education

JKSB.label: Welfare and benefit systems
JKSB.notes: Also class here: welfare state, state or official provisions of welfare benefits, policies about welfare benefits, types of welfare benefits and systems, social policies linked to welfare, social protections

JKSB1.label: Child welfare and youth services
JKSB1.notes: Also class here: child protection and safeguarding, social work services aimed at support of vulnerable / under-privileged youths in society

JKSG.label: Care of the elderly
JKSG.notes: Also class here: elder abuse, maltreatment and neglect, institutions for the care of older people. Use for: social care aspect, community and government policies and associated professions or roles

JKSL.label: Care of people with specific needs
JKSL.notes: Also class here: care of people with visible or hidden disabilities, people with physical and sensory impairments, care of neurodivergent persons with additional needs. Use for: social care aspect, community and government policies and associated professions or roles. Use with: 5PM* qualifiers as appropriate

JKSM.label: Care of people with mental health conditions
JKSM.notes: Use for: social care aspect, community and government policies and associated professions or roles. Use with: 5PM* qualifiers as appropriate

JKSN1.label: Charities, voluntary services and philanthropy
JKSN1.notes: Also class here: Volunteering, charitable giving and organisations, humanitarian, secular or religious charities, voluntary sector, civic sector or social sector

JKSR.label: Aid and relief programmes
JKSR.notes: Also class here: works on international and foreign aid or assistance, humanitarian aid, secular or religious aid and relief programmes, disaster relief. Use for: domestic and international programmes, either short term or long term aid programmes, relief initiatives, emergency programmes, etc

JKSW.label: Emergency services
JKSW.notes: Also class here: works on uniformed or public protective and emergency services, first responders, emergency planning, provisions of emergency and protective services, etc

JKSW3.label: Ambulance and rescue services
JKSW3.notes: Also class here: air and sea rescue services, mountain rescue, lifeboat services, paramedics, air ambulance services, specialist disaster rescue services, search and rescue services, etc. Use for: non-medical works about paramedical and equivalent emergency services

JKV.label: Crime and criminology
JKV.notes: Also class here: Crime studies. Use all JKV* codes with: other J* codes for different aspects of crime in the social sciences, NH* codes for historical studies, DNXC for journalistic style accounts of actual crimes, or with FF* codes for fictional accounts of particular types of crime

JKVC.label: Causes and prevention of crime
JKVC.notes: Also class here: surveillance, anti-terrorism measures, protection of the public from crime, policies around prevention and causes of crime, Social control theory

JKVF.label: Criminal investigation and detection
JKVF.notes: Also class here: Policing methods, police operations, covert operations, criminal intelligence gathering, sting operations, undercover law enforcement, investigative practices

JKVF1.label: Forensic science
JKVF1.notes: Use with: UY or UX* for computer or digital forensic science

JKVJ.label: Street crime
JKVJ.notes: Also class here: mugging, pickpocketing, vandalism, knife crime, gun crime

JKVK.label: Corporate crime / white-collar crime
JKVK.notes: Also class here: financial crimes, fraud, scams, embezzlement, bribery and corruption, cybercrimes, money laundering, counterfeiting, credit card fraud, tax evasion, bank or insurance scams, Con-men, Ponzi schemes, insider trading, copyright infringement, identity theft, forgery, call centre fraud, internet scammers, etc

JKVM.label: Organized crime
JKVM.notes: Also class here: criminal gangs, mafia, bandits or banditry, modern piracy, the mob, mobsters, the Mafia, Crime syndicates, the criminal underworld, organised crime networks. Use with: J* codes for works about organised crime and specific topics, like drug or human trafficking

JKVN.label: Violent crimes
JKVN.notes: Also class here: violent felonies, murder, unlawful killings, torture, assault, honour crimes, rape and crimes of sexual violence, assassination, mass shootings, stabbings, robbery or extortion with violence, mob violence, looting, arson, rioting, vigilante violence, or any other crime of a violent nature. Use for: works that examine different aspects of different types of violent crime. Use with: DNXC* codes for journalistic style accounts of actual violent crimes, or with: JBS* codes or INTEREST 5* qualifiers for works about violent crimes against specific groups

JKVN1.label: Abduction, kidnapping, hijacking
JKVN1.notes: Also class here: Hostages, hostage taking, missing person crimes. Use for: works that look at crimes that involve the kidnap or forceful removal of individuals or groups, or the forceful or unlawful detention of a person or persons against their will, outside official state run prisons, how these are dealt with. Use with: DNXC* for true crime accounts

JKVP.label: Penology and punishment
JKVP.notes: Also class here: prisons, penitentiaries, penal systems and theories, restorative justice, community service, retributive justice, correctional studies, participatory justice, transformative justice, prison reform, prisoners or detainees, sentencing disparity, etc

JKVQ.label: Offenders / Criminals
JKVQ.notes: Also class here: Lawbreakers, outlaws, felons, crooks. Use for: works about the people who break the law or commit a crime

JKVQ1.label: Rehabilitation of offenders
JKVQ1.notes: Also class here: Restorative justice, reintegration of ex-offenders, support for prisoners after prison, care and post-prison support, support for the formerly incarcerated, ex-felons, recidivism

JKVV.label: Victimology and victims of crime
JKVV.notes: Also class here: victim’s rights, victim-offender mediation, victim assistance, victim support

JM.label: Psychology
JM.notes: Use all JM* codes for: academic, specialist and professional level works. Use with: MKM* for Clinical psychology and psychotherapy approaches or MKL* for psychiatry. Prefer: VS* codes for practical advice for the general reader

JMA.label: Psychological theory, systems, schools and viewpoints
JMA.notes: Also class here: Therapies, therapeutic approaches

JMAF.label: Psychoanalytical and Freudian psychology
JMAF.notes: Also class here: psychoanalysis, Adlerian therapy, Individual psychology

JMAL.label: Behaviourism, Behavioural theory
JMAL.notes: Also class here: Behavioural therapy, Behavioural psychology,

JMAN.label: Humanistic psychology
JMAN.notes: Also class here: Humanistic therapy, Person-centred therapy, Gestalt therapy, existential therapy, solution-focused therapy, transactional analysis

JMAP.label: Positive psychology
JMAP.notes: Also class here: the psychology, science or theory of happiness, mental well-being, psychology of positivity, psychology of having a meaningful life

JMB.label: Psychological methodology
JMB.notes: Use for: works about different methods used in psychology

JMBT.label: Psychological testing and measurement
JMBT.notes: Also class here: psychometrics, psychological assessments

JMC.label: Child, developmental and lifespan psychology
JMC.notes: Also class here: attachment theory, psychological development, social emotional development

JME.label: Psychosocial studies
JME.notes: Also class here: Psychosocial risk factors or hazards, psychosocial health. Use for: works that look at the interaction of mental health, social health, emotional health and spiritual wellbeing

JMF.label: Couple and Family psychology
JMF.notes: Also class here: Family therapy, couples therapy, relationship therapy. Use for : works that look at psychology that is focused on the emotions, thoughts, and behaviour of individuals, couples, and families in relationships and in the broader environment in which they function

JMG.label: Psychology of gender
JMG.notes: Also class here: works that look at gender dysphoria, gender incongruence, works that look at psychological aspects or topics related to gender or gender identity. Use for: studies of the social, cultural, behavioural, and psychological factors that are associated with being male, female, or other gender identities, or works that explore the relationship between gender identity and gender expression, or look at the role of gender in shaping a persons behaviours, feelings or ways of thinking

JMHC.label: Interpersonal communication and skills
JMHC.notes: Also class here: psychology of communication, both verbal and non-verbal, body language

JMJ.label: Occupational and industrial psychology
JMJ.notes: Also class here: Industrial and organizational psychology, I-O psychology, psychology of work lives, psychological approaches to understand and optimize the effectiveness, health, and well-being of both organizations and individuals in a work or professional environment

JMN.label: Applied psychology
JMN.notes: Also class here: Counselling psychology, media psychology, environmental psychology, traffic psychology, political psychology. Use for: works about the use of psychological methods and findings of scientific psychology to solve practical problems of human behaviour and experience. Use with: other codes for area of application

JMR.label: Cognition and cognitive psychology
JMR.notes: Also class here: cognitive neuroscience, psychological works on learning, cognitive processes, such as memory and memory loss, intelligence, reasoning, perception, language, metacognition, cognitive control, working memory, long-term memory, Cognitive therapies

JMS.label: Psychology: the self, ego, identity, personality
JMS.notes: Also class here: Personality psychology, Personality theories, personality types, personality traits, extraversion and introversion, conscientiousness, agreeableness, neuroticism, openness to experience, development of personality. Use for: works that study personality and all its variations in individuals

JMT.label: Psychology: states of consciousness
JMT.notes: Also class here: psychological works on conscious and unconscious mind; sleep and dreams; altered states of mind, hypnosis, drug-induced, etc

JMX.label: Parapsychological studies
JMX.notes: Also class here: parapsychology. Use for: specialist (professional and academic) works or studies. Prefer: VX* categories for more popular, general works

JN.label: Education / Educational sciences / Pedagogy
JN.notes: Also class here: Education studies. Use all JN* codes for: works about education as a practice or subject. Use with: GP* codes for different types of research in education. Prefer: YP* codes for schoolbooks or educational material for pupils in pre-tertiary education

JNA.label: Philosophy and theory of education
JNA.notes: Also class here: educational philosophies, educational perennialism, educational essentialism, critical pedagogy, democratic education, critical thinking in education, learning styles theories, non-formal and informal learning theories, etc

JNAM.label: Moral and social purpose of education
JNAM.notes: Use for: works supporting the theories behind education focussed particularly on themes connected to society and behaviour in it

JNAS.label: Progressive education
JNAS.notes: Also class here: Montessori education, Waldorf or Steiner education. Use for: works about the theory or principles of pedagogical theories labelled as progressive, in comparison to more traditional curricula and theories. Use with: other JN* codes as appropriate

JNB.label: History of education
JNB.notes: Also class here: history of specific schools, colleges, as well as general history

JNC.label: Educational psychology
JNC.notes: Also class here: Educational psychology, works for educational psychologists, scientific study of human learning and learning processes, works about the psychological problems that can arise during teaching and training

JND.label: Educational systems and structures
JND.notes: Also class here: formal education, informal or non-formal education. Use for: general works about the systems or structures of education, comparative education, different types of educational systems or structures. Use with: GP* codes for different types of research

JNDC.label: Education: comparative studies
JNDC.notes: Use with: other JN* codes and PLACE 1* Qualifiers for comparisons between different education systems or comparative education studies, GP* codes for different types of research in comparative education

JNDH.label: Education: examinations and assessment
JNDH.notes: Also class here: testing, evaluations, measuring students

JNE.label: Social pedagogy
JNE.notes: Use for: works about social pedagogy as a field of study

JNF.label: Educational strategies and policy
JNF.notes: Also class here: government, regional, local educational teaching or learning strategies and policies, educational reforms, communication strategies for educational institutions, school policies, policies on admissions, selection, catchment areas, international education strategies, etc

JNFC.label: Counselling and care of students
JNFC.notes: Also class here: pastoral care, student affairs, student life, student welfare issues, absence, truancy, discipline, safety and security of students and in educational establishments, child protection in schools, emergency drills and practices, crisis management, academic development advice, welfare of exchange or international students, student exchange programs, school wellbeing strategies, relations and communication with parents or carers, pupil and student safeguarding, school safety etc

JNFK.label: Educational strategies and policy: inclusion
JNFK.notes: Also class here: works about diversity, inclusivity, equity, equality, accessibility, social mobility in education; or works that look at exclusion or those excluded from education; or works about access to education for the disadvantaged, or low-income groups, migrants, strategies to deal with prejudices and discrimination, equal access to education for girls and women, training for all educational personnel in inclusivity, support and resources for school leadership for inclusive education, works that identify barriers to education and policies for removing these. Use for: both formulating policy and practical applications. Use with: 5YS-UN-D as appropriate

JNFN.label: Education: relations with parents, communities or organisations
JNFN.notes: Also class here: Parent, carer and home participation in student or pupil education and development, relations and communications between schools or teachers and parents, carers or legal guardians, parental or carer volunteering and in-school activities, help with learning at home, teachers and schools involving parents in supporting their children’s academic learning, school-home and home-school communication, joint decision-making, schools helping parents or carer get children prepared for entering school. Use for: works about schools and community relations, engagement and outreach with communities, strategies and policies for dealing with hostility or pressure from external individuals and bodies or communities on educational institutions, the role of educational institutions in their communities, collaborating with the community, how educational institutions deal with external bodies, funding bodies, government or state bodies, private corporations etc

JNG.label: Early childhood care and education
JNG.notes: Use for: works aimed at professionals dealing with childcare or general works on subject

JNH.label: Home schooling / home education
JNH.notes: Also class here: elective home education, unschooling, worldschooling. Use for: works about forms of education for school aged children either at home or other places other than a school

JNK.label: Educational administration and organization
JNK.notes: Also class here: school governance, boards of education, head teachers, superintendents, principals or other leadership or administrative roles, or general works about the administration or organizations in educational institutions, parent-teacher associations or organizations, non-teaching and support staff, management of education and educational institutions

JNKG.label: Funding of education and student finance

JNKH.label: Teaching staff / Educators
JNKH.notes: Also class here: teachers, teaching assistants, educator roles, professors, classroom assistants, instructors, working conditions and practices for teaching staff, policies and strategies for safety, wellbeing and welfare of staff, anti-bullying and harassment policies,

JNLB.label: Primary and middle schools
JNLB.notes: Also class here: elementary, preparatory, infant and junior schools

JNLC.label: Secondary schools
JNLC.notes: Also class here: senior and high schools

JNLP.label: Independent schools, private education
JNLP.notes: Also class here: Charter schools, Academy trusts, Private schools. Use for: schools that receives government funding but that operate independently of the established state school system or schools that not administered or funded by government, but are financed by fees or private sector funds

JNLQ.label: Residential educational institutions
JNLQ.notes: Also class here: boarding schools, seminaries, military schools or academies, residential schools or any educational institutions that also have pupils living and staying in the educational faculty

JNLV.label: Outdoor schools / education
JNLV.notes: Also class here: adventure education, outdoor learning, forest schools. Use for: organized learning that takes place in the outdoors

JNM.label: Higher education, tertiary education
JNM.notes: Also class here: all advanced and post-secondary education, including institutions offering vocational, technical or non-degree courses as well as universities

JNMT.label: Teacher training
JNMT.notes: Also class here: professional development of educators, continuous learning, in-service training

JNP.label: Adult education, continuous learning
JNP.notes: Also class here: lifelong learning, popular education, community education, ‘Bildung’. Use for: works about education or training of adult learners that are neither university nor vocational training

JNQ.label: Open learning, distance education
JNQ.notes: Also class here: online learning, remote or blended learning

JNRV.label: Industrial or vocational training
JNRV.notes: Use for: works on industrial / vocational training, professional development and education as a subject. Prefer: YPW* or other subjects codes, such as T*, and the appropriate 4CP* Qualifiers for teaching material and coursework for teaching vocational subjects

JNS.label: Teaching of students with different educational needs
JNS.notes: Also class here: special education, mixed classes of students with different cultural or linguistic backgrounds, mixed classes with pupils from different socioeconomic backgrounds, techniques and advice for teaching different types of group, communication and learning techniques, etc. Use all JNS* codes with: 5P* Qualifiers for works about teaching to specific groups with specific or special needs

JNSC.label: Teaching of students with physical impairments or disabilities
JNSC.notes: Use for: teaching of students with impaired hearing or vision, or any physical condition giving rise to specific educational needs. Use with: 5PM* codes as appropriate

JNSG.label: Teaching of students with learning difficulties or disorders
JNSG.notes: Use for: teaching of students with learning difficulties or disorders such as dyslexia, dyscalculia, dysgraphia, communication disorders or any other specific learning difficulties (or learning disabilities in USA) giving rise to specific educational needs

JNSL.label: Teaching of students with social, emotional or behavioural difficulties or disorders

JNSP.label: Teaching of gifted or talented students

JNSR.label: Remedial education and teaching
JNSR.notes: Also class here: developmental education, compensatory education

JNSV.label: Education of bilingual or multilingual students
JNSV.notes: Also class here: works looking at the theory of education through a secondary language, education in mixed language classes, works about the education of pupils who speak another language, but where the language teaching itself is not the focus of the education, works about bilingual or bicultural education, plurilingual education, pluricultural education, language immersion

JNT.label: Teaching skills and techniques
JNT.notes: Also class here: classroom control, coaching and mentoring, lesson planning, tutoring, behavioural management, classroom management, team teaching, co-teaching, differentiated Instruction, culturally relevant teaching techniques, responsive teaching skills, collaborative teaching skills and methods

JNTC.label: Competence development
JNTC.notes: Also class here: competency-based education and training, competency learning, social and emotional learning, teaching problem solving, analytical, creative or critical thinking skills. Use for: works that examine the practical approach to developing competencies and concrete skills in education or training or works that examine theories or techniques for helping learners develop skills to manage emotions, resolve conflicts, and make responsible decisions

JNTR.label: Play-based learning
JNTR.notes: Use for: works that examine the theories or approaches to using play and activity to teach and learn

JNTS.label: Teaching of reading, writing and numeracy
JNTS.notes: Also class here: phonics approach, linguistic method, multisensory learning approach, reading aloud, dialogic reading. Use for: works about the theory or different approaches of learning or teaching the basic skills, or that look at how education can improve, measure, promote or otherwise enhance literacy, reading, writing or numeracy skills and motivate interest in these skills at all ages

JNU.label: Teaching of a specific subject
JNU.notes: Use all JNU* codes for: works that are about how an educator can teach a specific subject. Use with: the code for the subject taught, for example, YP* for works that look at how to teach a subject at primary or secondary school level, or with another subject code, if the topic is how to teach adults a certain subject. If JNU is used with YP* codes then it should also use a 4* EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE Qualifier and JNU should be designated as the Main Subject code

JNUM.label: Teachers’ classroom resources and material
JNUM.notes: Also class here: interactive resources, teachers’ editions of textbooks, learning materials and teaching aids etc. Use with: the code for the subject taught, for example, YP* for teachers materials for use at primary or secondary school level, or with other subject codes if the work is teachers material for teaching adults, and use with 4*EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE Qualifiers to indicate level as appropriate and JNUM should be designated as the Main Subject code

JNUM1.label: Lesson plans
JNUM1.notes: Use with: the code for the subject taught, using YP* Educational codes where appropriate

JNV.label: Educational equipment and technology, computer-aided learning (CAL)
JNV.notes: Also class here: media technology in classroom, Learning management systems, virtual or online learning, e-learning, remote, blended or hybrid learning, EdTech courseware, educational software, virtual whiteboards, etc. Use for: works about using digital technologies in class and for learning

JNW.label: Extra-curricular activities
JNW.notes: Also class here: field trips, school trips, sporting and community activities, events, performances, playtime/mealtime, after-school activities, school clubs etc

JPF.label: Political ideologies and movements
JPF.notes: Use for: works on different parts of the political spectrum, or political ideologies or movements that do not have more precise codes. Use all JPF* codes for: works on political rhetoric, political strategies, political groupings, individuals or general works associated with a particular approach to politics or part of the political spectrum and use in combination as appropriate

JPFA.label: Green politics / ecopolitics / environmentalism
JPFA.notes: Also class here: green movements, activist organisations

JPFC.label: Far-left political ideologies and movements
JPFC.notes: Also class here: Communism, Marxism-Leninism, Trotskyism, Maoism, extreme-left, radical left, hard left, democratic socialists, populist socialists, social populists, left-wing populism, far-left-wing nationalism, far-left politics and political parties or movements

JPFF.label: Left-of-centre democratic ideologies and movements
JPFF.notes: Also class here: social democracy, socialism, socialist ideologies and movements, Centre-left politics and political parties or movements

JPFK.label: Centrist democratic ideologies and movements
JPFK.notes: Also class here: Communitarianism, Centrism, Liberalism, liberal ideologies and movements, economic liberalism, social liberalism, cultural liberalism, democratic liberalism, progressivism, centrist politics and political parties or movements. Use with: other JPF* codes if work is associated with other ideologies

JPFL.label: Libertarianism and libertarian ideologies and movements
JPFL.notes: Use with: other JPF* codes if work is associated with other ideologies, such as left-wing libertarianism, right-wing libertarianism, etc

JPFM.label: Right-of-centre democratic ideologies and movements
JPFM.notes: Also class here: Christian Democracy, centre-right politics and political parties or movements

JPFN.label: Nationalism and nationalist ideologies and movements
JPFN.notes: Also class here: ethnic nationalism, language nationalism, nationalist or nativist movements, national populism, national revivals or national awakenings. Use for: works that examine any form of nationalism. Use with: NH* codes for history titles and INTEREST 5* Qualifiers as appropriate

JPFN2.label: Pan-nationalism
JPFN2.notes: Use for: works about specific forms of nationalism that look beyond traditional boundaries of basic national identities, in order to create a ‘higher’ pan-national (all-inclusive) identity, based on various common denominators. Use with: NH* codes for history titles and INTEREST 5* Qualifiers as appropriate

JPFP.label: Populism / populist ideologies and movements
JPFP.notes: Use with: other JPF* codes if work is associated with other ideologies, such as left-wing-populism, right-wing populism, religious populism, national populism, social populism, etc

JPFQ.label: Far-right political ideologies and movements
JPFQ.notes: Also class here: Fascism and neo-fascism, Nazism and neo-Nazism, ultra-nationalism, extreme right, alt right, hard right, radical right, Palaeoconservatism, nativism, right-wing populism, far-right-wing nationalism, far-right conservative political movements based on religious ideologies and movements, far-right politics and political parties or movements

JPFR.label: Religious and theocratic ideologies and movements
JPFR.notes: Also class here: Theocracy, religious political parties. Use for: works about religion used as a source of political ideology, identity or action. Use with: QR* codes to indicate particular religion as appropriate, with other JP* codes for particular religious inspired political ideologies, movements or structures

JPFT.label: Conservatism / conservative ideologies and movements
JPFT.notes: Also class here: Conservative thought, social conservatism, fiscal conservatism, economic conservatism, cultural conservatism, liberal conservatism, national conservatism, traditionalist conservatism, religious conservatism, authoritarian conservatism, left-wing conservatism, right-wing conservatism, etc. Use with: other JPF* codes if work is associated with other ideologies or political movements

JPH.label: Political structure and processes
JPH.notes: Also class here: Politics structures, systems, general works about political systems, or structures. Use all JPH* codes with: N* codes for historical looks at different political structures or processes

JPHC.label: Constitution: government and the state
JPHC.notes: Also class here: studies of the branches of government, the role of the executive, role of legislatures, how government works, how constitutions define government, the state, branches of government

JPHF.label: Elections and referenda / suffrage
JPHF.notes: Also class here: psephology, voting systems, right to vote, electoral districts, electoral map. Use for: works both on the study of, as well as on specific elections or referendums, studies of voting behaviour, types of electoral and voting practices, voting and electoral systems. Use with: JPZ for works about electoral corruption, fraud, gerrymandering, political manipulation of electoral districts or electoral lists, for works about specific elections, votes or referendums, referenda. Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers

JPHL.label: Political leaders and leadership
JPHL.notes: Also class here: heads of government, presidents, prime or first ministers, party leaders. Use for: works that examine significant politicians, the role of political leaders, heads of state or leaders of the executive, or works about leaders or leadership in politics

JPHR.label: Political structures / systems: monarchies
JPHR.notes: Also class here: monarchy as a form of government, constitutional monarchy, parliamentary monarchy, democratic monarchy, elective monarchy, hereditary monarchy, absolute monarchy, federal monarchy, emirates or other form of monarchies, Royal systems of government, Royalty and its role in government or state. Use with: N* codes for works of history about monarchy

JPHT.label: Political structures / systems: republics
JPHT.notes: Also class here: republics as a form of government, including constitutional republics, democratic republics, federal republics, Islamic republics, parliamentary republics, presidential republics, people’s republics, socialist republics or any other republican form of government. Use with: N* codes for works of history about republics

JPHV.label: Political structures / systems: democracy
JPHV.notes: Also class here: Democratic systems, direct democracy, liberal democracy, representative democracy, social democracy

JPHX.label: Political structures / systems: autocracy, totalitarianism and dictatorship
JPHX.notes: Also class here: authoritarianism, tyranny, absolutism, civilian dictatorships, military dictatorships, autocratic or oligarchic authoritarian forms of government, one-party systems, military rule

JPL.label: Political parties and party platforms
JPL.notes: Use for: works that look at individual or multiple political parties, or examine particular party platforms or programs. Use with: JPF* codes for works about a particular party on the political spectrum

JPN.label: Indigenous people: governance and politics
JPN.notes: Also class here: works on policies, government, administration, assemblies, sovereignty, nationhood, Reserves or Reservations, First Nation Bands, Tribal Councils, First Nations government, Native American tribal nations, Native American sovereignty, Native Community Lands, Indigenous Territories, Terra Indígena, Territorio indigena, etc. Use for: works about the politics of or form of governance used by diverse Indigenous peoples around the globe, or the relationships between Indigenous forms of governance and other entities, such as States, Federal governments etc, or relationships with legal entities and legal systems, Treaties, etc

JPP.label: Public administration / Public policy
JPP.notes: Use for: works about the creation, discussions and the implementation of public policy or policies, of domestic policy, of social policy. Use with: JPQB or JPRB as appropriate and other codes for policies in particular areas

JPQB.label: Central / national / federal government policies
JPQB.notes: Also class here: public policy, domestic policies, social policies, etc. Use with: other J* or other subjects codes for area of policy, and JPP for the administration or implementation of the policies

JPR.label: Regional, state and other local government
JPR.notes: Use for: any government within a country that is not municipal or city based (these are within scope of JPT)

JPRB.label: Regional, state and other local government policies
JPRB.notes: Use for: public, social or domestic policy of any government within a country that is not municipal or city based (these are within scope of JPT). Use with: other J* or other subjects codes for area of policy, and JPP for the administration or implementation of the policies

JPS.label: International relations
JPS.notes: Also class here: International politics, foreign policy

JPSF.label: Arms negotiation and control
JPSF.notes: Also class here: arms race, arms stockpiling, disarmament

JPSH.label: Espionage and secret services
JPSH.notes: Also class here: surveillance, counterintelligence, spying, military intelligence

JPSL.label: Geopolitics
JPSL.notes: Also class here: Political borders, frontiers, borderland studies, effects of geography on international relations and politics, frozen conflicts, territorial disputes, international and regional boundaries

JPSL1.label: Neo-colonialism / Neo-imperialism
JPSL1.notes: Also class here: works that look at contemporary or historical examples of neo-colonial or neo-imperial debates or new colonial or new imperial powers / countries, or old empires or countries who are reverting colonial or imperial control or influence, contemporary empire building or contemporary imperialism. Use with: KCS* for economic studies, NHTQ for historical studies, JW* for wars and military operations linked to neo-imperialism or neo-colonialism and with 1* PLACE qualifiers as appropriate

JPSN.label: International institutions / intergovernmental organizations
JPSN.notes: Also class here: UN and UN agencies, EU institutions, intergovernmental and non-governmental organizations (IGOs and NGOs) etc. Use with: 1QF* values from PLACE 1* Qualifiers as appropriate

JPT.label: Municipal / city government
JPT.notes: Use for: city regions (e.g. Greater London or the Bay Area), metropolitan areas or key subdivisions of urban areas such as boroughs

JPV.label: Political control and freedoms
JPV.notes: Also class here: political propaganda, political censorship, freedom of the press, political autonomy. Use for: works about the freedom from unreasonable constraints on political action or speech, the positive exercise of rights, capacities and possibilities for action and the exercise of social or group rights, the exercise of political control to limit political freedoms

JPVC.label: Civics and citizenship
JPVC.notes: Also class here: digital citizenship, political participation, citizens‘ assemblies or conventions, notions of being citizens, obligations, duties, rights and responsibilities linked to civic society, becoming a citizen, loss of citizenship, statelessness, etc

JPVH.label: Human rights, civil rights
JPVH.notes: Also class here: works that look at freedom of speech, of information, of worship; land rights, civil and political rights, economic, social and cultural rights, civil liberties, the abuse of or repression of human rights, conflicts and debates about rights and liberties in societies, dealing with legacies of human rights abuses, individual rights vs collective rights, competing rights, etc. Use with: GTU for works on transitional justice

JPVR1.label: Political abduction, imprisonment, ‘Disappearance’ and assassination
JPVR1.notes: Use for: works about forced abduction, kidnapping, hostage taking, unlawful detention, extrajudicial punishments, imprisonment, or unlawful killings, judicial murder or targeted killings used as a form of political oppression, the ‘Disappeared’ in various societies, the search for the people or their bodies, missing people, etc. Use with: LBBR or LNDC for legal aspects or NH* codes for historical material

JPW.label: Political activism / Political engagement
JPW.notes: Also class here: activists, social activism. Use with: DNB* codes for biographies of activists

JPWB.label: Public affairs / Lobbying
JPWB.notes: Use for: works about the interaction with and influencing of public bodies, agencies, governments, public administrations, politicians, etc by third party organisations, public relations firms, specialist lobby groups, trade bodies, business, etc in regards to legislation, regulation, policies, taxation, etc

JPWG.label: Pressure groups, protest movements and non-violent action
JPWG.notes: Also class here: demonstrations, civil disobedience, peaceful resistance, active defiance of authority, direct action, activist campaigns, passive resistance, social movements, political protests, student protests, student activism. Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate and NH* codes for historical protests, movements or groups

JPWL.label: Terrorism, armed struggle
JPWL.notes: Also class here: political assassination, terrorist tactics or methods such as stabbings, shootings, bombings, targeted or random attacks, vehicles as a weapon, sabotage, cyberterrorism, bioterrorism, suicide attacks, environmental terrorism, death squads, clandestine cells, lone wolf terrorists and types of terrorism or terrorists, such as state terrorism, state-sponsored terrorism, ideological terrorism, religious terrorism, domestic terrorism, terror groups or organisations, designated terrorist groups, responses to terrorism, counter-terrorism, online radicalisation, etc

JPWS.label: Armed conflict
JPWS.notes: Also class here: uprisings, armed skirmishes, flashpoints, outbreaks of organized violence short of full-scale war

JPZ.label: Corruption in politics, government and society
JPZ.notes: Also class here: government and public sector corruption, judicial and police corruption, bribery and corruption as part of everyday life in society etc

JWA.label: Theory of warfare and military science
JWA.notes: Use with: RG* codes for Military Geography topics

JWCD.label: Land forces and warfare
JWCD.notes: Also class here: armies, infantry, ground warfare and operations. Use with: NHW* for military history, JWMV and either TRC* or WG* for works about particular types of land combat vehicle, such as tanks or other armoured fighting vehicles, etc

JWCG.label: Irregular or guerrilla forces and warfare
JWCG.notes: Also class here: armed resistance movements, insurgents, foreign fighters. Use for: works about non-regular military forces who fight for political, economic, ideological or religious reasons. Use with: NHW* codes as appropriate and PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

JWCK.label: Naval forces and warfare
JWCK.notes: Also class here: navies, naval operations, surface warfare, submarine or underwater warfare, blue-water navies, riverine navy, amphibious warfare, amphibious operations, amphibious landings, etc. Use with: NHW* for military history or NHTM for maritime history, JWMV and either WGG* for works about military ships or TRL* for technical works about navies etc

JWCM.label: Air forces and warfare
JWCM.notes: Also class here: aerial warfare, aerial operations, aerial reconnaissance, air combat, airborne forces, parachute operations, airstrikes, strategic bombing, anti-aircraft warfare, missiles, military unmanned aerial vehicles or drones, etc. Use with: NHW* for military history, JWMV and either TRP for more technical works about military aviation, or WGM for works about particular types of aircraft

JWCS.label: Special and elite forces
JWCS.notes: Also class here: special operations forces

JWD.label: Information warfare / Cyberwarfare
JWD.notes: Also class here: AI arms and warfare, military artificial intelligence, cyberattacks, cyberweapons, cyber sabotage, cyberdefence, iWar, electronic warfare, virtual war, command and control warfare, Fifth Dimension Operation, information operations, digital battlespace, etc

JWJ.label: Military administration
JWJ.notes: Also class here: personnel issues, discipline, procurement, funding etc

JWK.label: Military and defence strategy
JWK.notes: Also class here: military tactics, civil defence, national security policies

JWLF.label: Battles / military campaigns
JWLF.notes: Also class here: Military campaign strategies, tactics and plans, military operations, strategic goals, the conduct of a military campaign, operational level of war. Prefer: NHWR* codes for specific and historic wars, military campaigns or battles

JWM.label: Weapons and equipment
JWM.notes: Use with: code from JWC* to indicate sector

JWMV.label: Military vehicles and transport of air, land and sea
JWMV.notes: Also class here: works on all kinds of military vehicles of air, land or sea, general works about vehicles, form of transport etc, used for military purposes. Use with: code from JWC* to indicate sector and WG* or TR* codes as appropriate, for example, with JWCM for Military aircraft, JWCK for Military and naval vessels and watercraft, JWCD for Armoured and military land vehicles

JWT.label: Military institutions
JWT.notes: Also class here: regiments, memorials, war cemeteries, rolls of honour, command centres, defence institutions, military academies, organisations for veterans or ex-combatants etc

JWXF.label: Arms trade
JWXF.notes: Also class here: Armaments, weapons industry

JWXJ.label: Non-combatants / impact of war on civil society
JWXJ.notes: Also class here: civilians, journalists, aid workers, combat medics, military chaplains, neutrals etc

JWXN.label: Mercenaries
JWXN.notes: Also class here: soldiers of fortune, private armies and private defence companies. Use for: works about soldiers who fight for money or personal gain

K.label: Economics, Finance, Business and Management
K.notes: Use all K* codes for: specialist (professional and academic) and general adult titles, but see also VS* codes for practical approaches to many topics. Use all K* codes with: other subject categories and qualifiers where appropriate in particular EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* qualifiers for vocational, professional or apprenticeship style education titles, 4TM for revision and study guides, 4CP for vocational or professional qualifications, 4Z* for specific national qualifications

KCA.label: Economic theory and philosophy
KCA.notes: Also class here: history of economic thought. Use with: TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

KCB.label: Macroeconomics
KCB.notes: Also class here: studies of the behaviour and performance of an economy as a whole or works that look at economy-wide phenomena or general economic factors such as inflation, price levels, national income, gross domestic product (GDP), changes in employment, interest rates, national productivity, economic growth, structural adjustments

KCBM.label: Monetary economics
KCBM.notes: Also class here: monetary policy, currency policy, money supply, monetarism, monetary systems, gold standard

KCC.label: Microeconomics
KCC.notes: Also class here: consumer activity, business decisions, etc

KCCD.label: Domestic or internal trade
KCCD.notes: Also class here: wholesale and retail trade. Use for: works on the economics of exchange of domestic goods within the boundaries of a country

KCF.label: Labour / income economics
KCF.notes: Also class here: wage and salary policy, pay policy, basic income, earnings, comprehensive income, income growth, income inequality, labour or jobs markets, economic works on employment and unemployment, the labour and non-labour force parts of the economy

KCLT.label: International trade and commerce
KCLT.notes: Also class here: International trade agreements, free trade and protectionism, economics of tariffs and quotas, subsidies, dumping, trade negotiations

KCS.label: Economic systems and structures
KCS.notes: Use for: works on systems such as transitional economies, traditional economies, participatory economics, barter economy, gift economy, etc

KCSA.label: Capitalism
KCSA.notes: Also class here: laissez-faire, market economies, free market, neoliberal economics, corporate capitalism, mercantilism, etc. Use for: works that look at capitalism as an economic model in all its variations

KCSD.label: Mixed economic systems
KCSD.notes: Also class here: social market economies, welfare economies, social corporatism, state-sponsored capitalism, distributed ownership models, etc

KCSG.label: Planned economic systems
KCSG.notes: Also class here: centrally-planned economies, command economies

KCST.label: Circular economic systems / Regenerative economics
KCST.notes: Also class here: Circularity models, regenerative economic theory, sustainable economic models, Doughnut economics. Use for: works about circular economic models based on repairing, remaking, reusing, redesigning goods and sustainable economic models aimed at eliminating waste and creating a continual use of resources

KCSV.label: Degrowth / post-growth economics
KCSV.notes: Also class here: Anti-consumerism, decoupling, degrowth, New Economy movement, ecological economics, solidarity economy, commons, degrowth, regenerative design, systems thinking and Buddhist economics

KCVG.label: Environmental economics
KCVG.notes: Also class here: green economy, green accounting, ecotaxation, environmental economic strategies and policies, economics of carbon emissions trading, green growth, green jobs, green recovery, sustainable development, environmental pricing, environmental tariffs, carbon pricing, carbon neutrality, creating a low-carbon economy, carbon offsetting, etc. Use for: works that explore aspects of how environmental policies impact economies, environmental economic strategies or challenges, market-based environmental policy instruments

KCVJ.label: Health economics
KCVJ.notes: Also class here: healthcare industry, medical industry, the economics of the healthcare and health of populations, economics of health prevention and education, etc

KCVM.label: Digital or internet economics
KCVM.notes: Also class here: sharing economy, platform economy, access economy, peer-to-peer economy, on-demand economy and other economic models associated with the online sector, digital technologies or networked technologies, digital subscription business models, software as a service

KCVP.label: Knowledge / Information / Data economics
KCVP.notes: Also class here: information economy, knowledge-based economy, intellectual capital, the economics around the collection, analysing and use of information and data

KCVQ.label: Service sector economics
KCVQ.notes: Also class here: the tertiary sector. Use for: works that look at the economics of the service sector, usually firms offering ‘intangible goods’ such as services, maintenance and repairs, training, consulting, advice, and affective labour in areas like entertainment, retail, insurance, tourism, banking, financial services, media, hospitality, teaching, caring and other services

KCX.label: Economic and financial crises and disasters

KCY.label: Popular economics
KCY.notes: Use for: highly accessible works for the general reader, that usually take a broad, generalist view of an economics topic, and may also be a simplified approach to that particular subject. DO NOT USE: for indicating a title that sells well or has been a bestseller or is popularly purchased title

KCZ.label: Economic history
KCZ.notes: Use with: NH* codes and PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

KF.label: Finance and accounting
KF.notes: Use all KF* codes for: academic, specialist and professional level works. Prefer: VS* codes for practical advice for the general reader

KFCM1.label: Auditing / Audits
KFCM1.notes: Also class here: internal and external audits

KFCM2.label: Valuation (finance)
KFCM2.notes: Use for: works that look at the metrics, techniques or processes for determining the present value of an asset or a company

KFCR.label: Financial reporting, financial statements
KFCR.notes: Also class here: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) and works on other recognised international or national standards

KFCT.label: Tax planning and compliance
KFCT.notes: Also class here: Tax avoidance. Use for: works that explain taxation for organisations, entities and individuals. Use with: LNU* codes for professional titles looking at rules or procedures for different types of tax, with KJV* for different types of organisation

KFCX.label: Accounting: study and revision guides
KFCX.notes: Also class here: revision or preparation for recognised international or national accountancy and bookkeeping qualifications, for example ACCA, CIMA or ICAEW etc. Use with: 4CP* codes as appropriate or 4Z* for specific national qualifications

KFF.label: Finance and the finance industry
KFF.notes: Use for: general works on finance, financial theories or works that deal with multiple aspects of finance or financial topics, or works on the financial services sector, financial institutions, financial companies, alternative financial services or the businesses that manage money or the international financial architecture or system. Use with: KCVQ for works about the economics of the financial service sector or KNS for works that look at financial services from a business or industrial studies perspective or other K* codes for finance in particular sectors

KFFC.label: Fundraising, grants, donations
KFFC.notes: Also class here: applying for grants, grant writing, donations, raising money for charities, NGOs, not-for-profits, political organisations, financial endowments, etc. Use with: KJVX for Not-for-profit fundraising

KFFD.label: Public finance and taxation
KFFD.notes: Also class here: sovereign wealth funds, social wealth fund, public finance management, fiscal policy, government revenues and expenditure, public debt, financing of government expenditures, government borrowing, government budgets, etc

KFFF.label: Financial technology (fintech)
KFFF.notes: Also class here: decentralized finance technologies, mobile banking tech, online trading, electronic trading platforms. Use for: works that look at the use or impact of new technologies in the financial services sector. Use with: other K* codes and U* codes for technical approaches, for example UNKD for use of blockchain, UYQ* for use of AI

KFFJ.label: Currency / Foreign exchange
KFFJ.notes: Also class here: currency trading, money markets, cryptocurrencies (from a finance / investment aspect), etc

KFFK.label: Banking
KFFK.notes: Also class here: different types of banks or banking businesses, the banking industry, central banks, reserve banks

KFFM.label: Investment and securities
KFFM.notes: Also class here: commodities, stocks and shares, bonds, futures, hedge funds, derivatives, options, fixed-income securities, equity investments, dividends, forward contracts, swaps, hedging investment management, investment markets, investment advice, investment services, divestment, portfolio management, investment analysis, guides to investing and trading, private equity investment, angel investing, equity crowdfunding, seed funding, bond valuation, debt and loan markets, debt instruments, venture capital

KFFS.label: Green finance / sustainable finance
KFFS.notes: Also class here: climate finance, green funds, green bonds, eco-investing, green investments, climate-related asset stranding, adaptation funding, fossil fuel divestment, climate related financial disclosures, ESG investments, TBL framework accounting. Use for: works that look at green, environmentally friendly, sustainable practices and approaches to finance, financial products, financial institutions, private and public investment; structured financial activity that has been created to ensure a better environmental outcome; ideas for changes to financial institutions to deal with environmental issues, etc. Use with: other K* codes for particular types of green finance

KFFT.label: Private wealth management
KFFT.notes: Also class here: wealth planning, family or multi-family offices, personal finance management, advice for families planning their assets across generations, or works for professionals who work in the wealth management area. Use with: KFCT or LNU* for specific works about tax planning, with L* for works aimed at private law professionals, with VSB for works that give more general advice aimed at a broader general readership

KFFX.label: Banking and finance: study and revision guides
KFFX.notes: Also class here: revision or preparation for recognised international or national banking, finance, insurance qualifications, for example IMC, CFA, FIA etc. Use with: 4CP* codes as appropriate or 4Z* for specific national qualifications

KJ.label: Business and Management
KJ.notes: Use all KJ* codes for: academic, specialist and professional level works. Prefer: VS* codes for practical advice for the general reader

KJBX.label: Business and management: study and revision guides
KJBX.notes: Also class here: revision or preparation for recognised international or national business or management qualifications. Use with: 4CP* codes as appropriate or 4Z* for specific national qualifications

KJC.label: Business strategy
KJC.notes: Also class here: business analysis, business intelligence, strategic planning

KJD.label: Business innovation
KJD.notes: Use for: works on business and the effect of new technologies, strategies, innovation in business

KJDD.label: Disruptive innovation
KJDD.notes: Use for: developments that create new markets and value networks, and typically disrupt and replace existing markets

KJE.label: E-commerce: business aspects
KJE.notes: Also class here: electronic commerce, internet commerce. Use for: works about the buying and selling of goods or services using the internet, and the transfer of money and data to execute these transactions

KJG.label: Business ethics and social responsibility
KJG.notes: Also class here: Advice on Corporate social responsibility (CSR), Environmental, Social, Ethical Corporate governance (ESG), Ten Principles of the UN Global Compact

KJH.label: Entrepreneurship / Start-ups
KJH.notes: Also class here: designing, launching, starting and developing a new business or venture, entrepreneurs and risk, emerging companies, unicorn companies, internal start-ups, early-stage companies. Use for: works that refer to starting a new business venture or company, or the first stages of running a new venture

KJJ.label: Business and the environment; sustainable approaches to business
KJJ.notes: Also class here: sustainability in the business world, creating or running a sustainable or green business or enterprise, advice for business world to achieve climate goals, works on business impact on the environment, digital sobriety in business, ESG (environmental, social and governance) designations, ratings or criteria, etc

KJL.label: Consultancy
KJL.notes: Also class here: getting or giving advice about running a business, including obtaining grants, subsidies, research funding

KJMB.label: Management: leadership and motivation
KJMB.notes: Also class here: management of change

KJMK.label: Knowledge management
KJMK.notes: Also class here: Knowledge audits, protection, retention of knowledge in an organisation. Use for: works that look at knowledge management techniques, applications and practices in organisations

KJMN.label: Business process / operations management
KJMN.notes: Also class here: business method management, business process engineering. Use for: works that look at all the tasks or processes that a business does, either by its personnel or by technology, to help it function and supply its product or service to its customers

KJMP.label: Project management
KJMP.notes: Also class here: Agile, Scrum, etc, project and programme management methodologies

KJMQ.label: Quality Assurance (QA) and Total Quality Management (TQM)

KJMV.label: Management of specific areas
KJMV.notes: Use with: other K* or other subject codes for management in specific specialist areas

KJMV2.label: Personnel and human resources management
KJMV2.notes: Also class here: recruitment, hiring, firing, training, coaching and mentoring employees, staff policies, managing remote workforces, managing payroll, guides to setting correct behaviour at the workplace, guidelines to codes of behaviour, discipline procedures, communication with workforce, protocols, etc

KJMV21.label: Performance management / appraisals
KJMV21.notes: Also class here: professional aptitude tests, performance testing, reviews and evaluations

KJMV22.label: Diversity, equality, equity and inclusion in the workplace
KJMV22.notes: Use for: works about social justice, equity, diversity, inclusivity and accessibility policies and strategies in the workplace, creating a diverse and inclusive workforce and professional environment, or works that examine inequality, exclusion, discrimination at work, or works that look at topics such as unconscious bias, positive discrimination, affirmative hiring practice, anti-discrimination and anti-harassment policies, creating a safe space at work, training around these topics in the workplace. Use with: JBFK4 for bullying or harassment in the workplace, or JBS* for policies around specific groups

KJMV3.label: IT and information systems management
KJMV3.notes: Also class here: data centre management, hardware asset management, software asset management, information management and policy, data infrastructure management, document management, information technology operations, technical support, software licensing, compliance audits, digital asset management strategy. Use for: business and management approaches. Prefer: U* codes for technical works

KJMV4.label: Management of assets: real estate, property and plant
KJMV4.notes: Also class here: management of physical assets, facilities management, infrastructure assets, enterprise asset management

KJP.label: Business communication, etiquette and presentation
KJP.notes: Also class here: techniques and skills for work presentations, work meetings, business etiquette and protocols, for in person, face-to-face business communication or remote, online or virtual communication, online meetings, online webinars or conferences. Use for: works on the norms of social behaviour in a workplace, protocols for doing business with others, the etiquettes and rules for working within a business and with colleagues, including time management, dress codes, interaction with your teams, use of work space, equipment, technology, manners in business, accepted and proper codes of behaviour, etiquette for online working and meetings, cross-cultural meeting etiquette etc. Use with: CBP for advice on public presentations, WJXC for workplace etiquette, VSC for guides to presentational skills, etc

KJR.label: Corporate governance: role and responsibilities of boards and directors
KJR.notes: Also class here: role and responsibilities of company secretary, etc

KJS.label: Sales and marketing
KJS.notes: Also class here: general works on selling techniques, sales skills

KJSG.label: Online marketing / Social media marketing
KJSG.notes: Also class here: use of social media and online resources to market products, web marketing, SEO techniques, the attention or experience economy, online newsletters, influencers, online recommendation engines, personalized marketing, individual marketing, digital marketing, viral marketing

KJSR.label: Marketing for change / Cause-related marketing
