KJSR.notes: Also class here: community-based marketing, social marketing, behaviour change marketing, purpose-driven marketing. Use for: works that look at how organisations, for-profit businesses or brands seek to both increase profits and to better society, in accordance with corporate social responsibility, or works that look at integrating marketing concepts with other approaches to social change, or the application of marketing principles to enable social transformation. Use with: JP* codes for works about using this in politics or government, KN* codes for works looking at different industry sectors , etc

KJST.label: Greenwashing and other forms of deceptive marketing
KJST.notes: Also class here: marketing spin, colourwashing, diversity washing, redwashing, whitewashing, woke washing, rainbow washing, pink washing, astroturfing, etc. Use for: works, often critical, that look at how companies, organisations, entities, governments political parties, celebrities, etc use causes or social justice topics for ‘window-dressing’ marketing purposes, public relations or deception purposes, with little or no real commitment to the actual cause behind this. LNUP.label: Personal tax
LNUP.notes: Also class here: personal income tax, capital gains tax, wealth tax

LNUS.label: Sales tax, tariffs and customs duties
LNUS.notes: Also class here: laws relating to value added taxes (VAT), systems of general sales taxes, rules and regulations relating to tariff codes or commodity codes, VAT codes and categories

LNUT.label: Trusts and estates taxation, gift tax
LNUT.notes: Also class here: inheritance taxes, death duties

LNUU.label: Real estate tax, property valuation
LNUU.notes: Also class here: land value taxes, millage tax, property taxes, stamp duty, transfer taxation

LNUV.label: Excise taxes and duties
LNUV.notes: Also class here: laws relating to charges levied on goods such as alcohol, fuel, tobacco

LNUW.label: Other transaction taxes
LNUW.notes: Also class here: financial transaction tax, securities transaction tax, currency transaction tax, Tobin tax, Spahn tax, Special Drawing Rights (SDR), bank transaction tax, automated payment transaction tax, etc

LNUY.label: Taxation procedure
LNUY.notes: Also class here: tax administration law, laws on tax procedure. Use for: works on the tax procedures that codify the relationship between the State and its taxpayers in order to define the rights and obligations of these two partners throughout the taxation process, including assessment, declaration, tax liability, collection and payment of taxes, judicial and administrative mechanisms available for resolving disputes, tax investigations, suppression of tax fraud, the anti-evasion measures, limitations and limits, etc

LNV.label: Law of torts, damages and compensation

LNVC.label: Negligence
LNVC.notes: Use for: both general and professional negligence

LNW.label: Law: wills, probate, succession, inheritance
LNW.notes: Also class here: works on laws dealing with passing on private property, titles, debts, rights and obligations upon the death of an individual, estate planning, succession regulations

LNWB.label: Private client law
LNWB.notes: Use for: works about aspects of the law for legal professionals who act for private individuals on legal matters such as wealth management, wills, trusts and probate, legal topics around preparing for inheritance of assets. Use with: other L* codes for particular specialities, such as LNUT for inheritance taxation

LNY.label: Cultural heritage law / Art and Culture law
LNY.notes: Also class here: Cultural property law, cultural patrimony law, laws relating to ownership, preservation, regulation or exploitation of tangible cultural heritage, such as art, antiquities, archives, architecture, treasure, paintings, sculptures, coins, manuscripts, monuments, archaeological sites, shipwrecks, underwater ruins, etc., laws relating to intangible cultural heritage assets, such as oral traditions, performing arts, rituals, intergenerational knowledge, etc, laws relating to natural heritage, natural sites with cultural or sacred aspects (physical, biological or geological formations), laws relating to heritage in the event of armed conflict. Use for: works about law, including domestic and foreign law, and multilateral treaties and conventions, that regulates and is applied to artists, fine art and cultural property, the protection and preservation of cultural heritage, the trade in, exploitation of cultural heritage, works about tradition-based products and services, works about Indigenous cultural rights, language rights, etc

LNZ.label: Primary sources of law
LNZ.notes: Use all LNZ* codes for: published copies of the texts of primary or original legal documents, such as Charters, Legal or Law Codes, Constitutions, Court rulings, judgements, or materials that state the actual laws, rules or regulations themselves. Use with: other L* codes for identifying sources and type of Law

LNZC.label: Sources of law: case law, precedent
LNZC.notes: Use for: works about judicial decisions deciding law, ‘judge made law’

LNZL.label: Sources of law: legislation
LNZL.notes: Also class here: material sources of law from institutions, or social groups, that are authorised to create laws, such as statutes, Acts of Parliament or legislatures, executive acts when recognised as source of laws, statutory instruments and other forms of delegated or secondary Legislation

LWF.label: Shariah law: four Schools of Fiqh

LWFA.label: Shariah law: Al-Shafi’i School of Fiqh

LWFB.label: Shariah law: Al-Hanbali School of Fiqh

LWFC.label: Shariah law: Al-Maaliki School of Fiqh

LWFD.label: Shariah law: Al-Hanafi School of Fiqh

LWK.label: Shariah law: key topics and practice

LWKH.label: Shariah law: inheritance and disposal of property

LWKL.label: Shariah law: economics and finance

LWKR.label: Shariah law: administration of justice (including penalties and apostasy)

LWKT3.label: Shariah law: Islamic rituals: prayer and funeral prayer

LX.label: Law: study and revision guides
LX.notes: Also class here: revision or preparation for recognised international or national legal qualifications or for law / legal exams. Use with: Other L* codes and PLACE 1* or EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate

M.label: Medicine and Nursing
M.notes: Also class here: the Health sciences, Healthcare. Use all M* codes for: academic, technical and specialist healthcare and medical material only. Use with: EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate. Prefer: V* codes for health topics aimed at a broad general adult audience

MB.label: Medicine / Healthcare: general issues / topics
MB.notes: Also class here: Health policies, general overviews of medicine and health topics

MBD.label: Medical profession
MBD.notes: Use for: general works about medical and clinical professions or working in medical professions, or being a particular kind of medical professional, such as a junior doctor, a physician, a resident or consultant. Use with: DNBT or DNC for biographies of medical staff, KCVJ for the economics of staffing, etc

MBDP.label: Doctor / patient relationship
MBDP.notes: Also class here: advice for medical practitioners, healthcare providers and medical professionals on relations, engagement and communications with patients, their families, their carers, etc

MBDS.label: Patient safety
MBDS.notes: Use for: professional and specialist works concerning procedures, safeguards, standards and training designed to ensure the safety and welfare of patients within healthcare systems

MBF.label: Medical and health informatics
MBF.notes: Also class here: artificial intelligence in healthcare, decision support machine learning in healthcare, healthcare or biomedical informatics, health information management, electronic health records, electronic medical records, healthcare information system, smart tech, clinical informatics, clinical research informatics. Use for: works that look at the design, development and application of computational or digital innovations, computer structures and algorithms to improve healthcare

MBG.label: Medical equipment, devices and techniques
MBG.notes: Use for: general works about hospital and medical devices, the use of medical equipment, techniques and equipment used in healthcare, guidance for healthcare technology and sterilisation professionals, etc. Use with: other M*, P*, T* or U* codes as appropriate and 4* qualifiers for educational or training material

MBGD.label: Implementation and management of medical equipment and healthcare technologies
MBGD.notes: Also class here: Healthcare technology management, Clinical Engineers, Biomedical equipment technicians, advanced medical technologies and equipment, specialist life support systems such as haemodialysis machines, artificial ventilators, perfusion, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Use for: works about specialist technologies and equipment used in medicine and healthcare settings, usually technologies that require specialist knowledge and training, guidance for advanced and specialised equipment for healthcare technology professionals, specialist healthcare engineers, or professional technicians, who work in hospitals or healthcare institutions, who support and advances patient care by applying engineering and managerial skills to healthcare technology, train and supervise biomedical equipment technicians (BMETs), serve as technological consultants. Use with: 4CP* and other 4* qualifiers for works aimed at professional certification and with other M*, P*, T* or U* codes as appropriate

MBGT.label: Telemedicine
MBGT.notes: Also class here: telehealth, mHealth, eHealth, video or electronic consultations, teletherapy. Use with: other M* codes to indicate the speciality as appropriate

MBN.label: Public health and preventive medicine
MBN.notes: Also class here: Healthcare promotion, Community healthcare, access to healthcare, public health policy, healthy communities, social medicine, Global health policies, Community Health policy, the science of health, health science

MBNC.label: Medical screening
MBNC.notes: Also class here: mass screening, high-risk or selective screening of populations or groups

MBND.label: Social medicine
MBND.notes: Use for: works that look at how social and economic conditions impact health, disease and the practice of medicine and then try to work out how what conditions lead to a healthier society

MBNF.label: Behavioural medicine
MBNF.notes: Use for: works that look at the integration of behavioural, psychosocial, and biomedical concepts to prevent, diagnose, and treat patients. Use with: other M* codes for interdisciplinary studies in particular medical domains

MBNH.label: Personal and public health / health education
MBNH.notes: Also class here: specialist and professional works on health education, patient education, training for health education specialists

MBNH2.label: Environmental factors
MBNH2.notes: Also class here: Environmental health, impact of environment on health, etc

MBNH3.label: Dietetics and nutrition
MBNH3.notes: Use for: medical and academic works on the relationship between diet, health and disease. Use with: PS or PND for works on food as medicine or nutrition in health care that are primarily aimed at academic, technical and specialist audiences

MBNH4.label: Birth control, contraception, family planning
MBNH4.notes: Also class here: sexual and reproductive health education and provision. Use with: VFX* codes for works aimed at a broader general audience

MBNH9.label: Health psychology
MBNH9.notes: Also class here: medical psychology. Use for: works that look at how biological, behavioural, social and psychological factors influence health and illness, or how psychological science can be used to promote health, prevent illness or improve health systems

MBNS.label: Epidemiology and Medical statistics
MBNS.notes: Also class here: works that deal with the collection, statistical analysis and applications of statistics and data to medicine and the health sciences or with the study of the incidence, distribution, and possible control of diseases (both epidemic and disease in general) and other non-disease, health-related conditions

MBP.label: Health systems and services
MBP.notes: Also class here: health administration, provision of healthcare facilities, works about hospitals, clinics as institutions. Use for: general works about healthcare systems, public and private healthcare systems, how healthcare systems are financed, works about secondary level healthcare services and institutions. Prefer: KCVJ for works that look at healthcare from a business or economic sector perspective

MBPA.label: Primary care medicine, primary health care

MBPN.label: Residential care / Long-Term Care Facilities
MBPN.notes: Also class here: elder care, convalescent homes, hospices, nursing homes, skilled nursing facilities (SNF), care homes, rest homes or intermediate care

MBR.label: Sciences in medicine and healthcare
MBR.notes: Use for: works about the use for other scientific disciplines in medicine and health care. Use with: 4* Educational purpose qualifiers for material aimed at university, vocational or professional education and with P* codes for works about using specific sciences in healthcare. Prefer: other M* codes for specific health sciences or specialities

MBS.label: Medical sociology
MBS.notes: Also class here: Health sociology, medical anthropology. Use for: works that look at the practical uses and applications of sociology in medicine and healthcare or works that study the social causes and consequences of health and illness

MF.label: Pre-clinical medicine: basic sciences
MF.notes: Also class here: Basic medical sciences. Use for: broad approaches and works about sciences needed for medicine or healthcare. Use with: 4* Educational purpose qualifiers for material aimed at university, vocational or professional education

MFG.label: Physiology
MFG.notes: Use for: medical titles on the study of how the human body works

MFGT.label: Electrophysiology
MFGT.notes: Also class here: electroencephalography, electrocardiogram, Electrocorticography, EEG, ECG, Electroneuronography

MFGV.label: Biomechanics, human kinetics
MFGV.notes: Also class here: exercise physiology, kinesiology, works aimed at professionals about human movement

MFKC.label: Reproductive medicine
MFKC.notes: Use for: works on the branch of medicine that specializes in fertility preservation, diagnosing and treating infertility, and other reproductive problems, or certain medical issues related to puberty, menopause, contraception, and certain sexual problems

MFKC1.label: Infertility and fertilization
MFKC1.notes: Also class here: assisted reproductive technology, IVF

MJCJ.label: Infectious and contagious diseases
MJCJ.notes: Also class here: transmissible / communicable diseases, epidemic diseases, viral, bacterial and parasitic infections, treatments and prevention

MJCJ1.label: Sexually transmitted infections / Venereal diseases
MJCJ1.notes: Also class here: STIs, STDs, syphilis, chlamydia, gonorrhoea, genital herpes, warts, trichomoniasis, etc

MJCJ2.label: Medicine: HIV/AIDS, retroviral diseases
MJCJ2.notes: Use for: medical works about human immunodeficiency virus infections and acquired immune deficiency syndrome

MJCJ3.label: Hospital-acquired infections
MJCJ3.notes: Also class here: nosocomial (healthcare-acquired) infections, iatrogenic infections

MJCJ4.label: Human coronaviruses
MJCJ4.notes: Also class here: severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS), severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, SARS‑CoV‑2 (COVID-19)

MJCL.label: Oncology
MJCL.notes: Use with: other M* codes for medical specialities relating to oncology and studies and treatments of cancer, for example, MJD for cardiovascular oncology, MKN for geriatric oncology, MKMT12 for psychiatric oncology or Psychosocial oncology, MKB for Palliative care, etc

MJCL1.label: Radiotherapy
MJCL1.notes: Also class here: Radiation therapy, radiation oncology, brachytherapy, external beam radiation therapy, radionuclide therapy, molecular radiotherapy

MJCL2.label: Chemotherapy / Pharmacotherapy
MJCL2.notes: Also class here: molecularly targeted therapy, Immunotherapy, biological therapy, Hormonal therapy in oncology

MJCM.label: Immunology
MJCM.notes: Also class here: immune system, disorders of human immunity, immunodeficiencies, autoimmunity, hypersensitivity, immune-mediated inflammatory disease, transplant rejection, immunotherapy

MJCM1.label: Medicine: Allergies
MJCM1.notes: Also class here: Anaphylaxis, hay fever (allergic rhinitis), food allergies. Use for: medical works about allergic diseases

MJD.label: Cardiovascular medicine
MJD.notes: Also class here: cardiology. Use for: works on the study of and related disorders of the heart and parts of the circulatory system, diagnosis and treatment of congenital heart defects, coronary artery disease, heart failure, valvular heart disease and cardiac electrophysiology

MJE.label: Musculoskeletal medicine
MJE.notes: Use for: works on the diagnosis and treatment of problems arising from the musculoskeletal system, including injuries and diseases affecting the muscles, bones and joints

MJF.label: Haematology
MJF.notes: Use for: works on the study of and related disorders or diseases related to the blood and the haematopoietic system, works on haemophilia, blood clots, thrombus, leukaemia, multiple myeloma, lymphoma, sickle cell disease and other diseases that affect the production of blood and its components

MJG.label: Endocrinology
MJG.notes: Use for: works on the study of and related disorders of the endocrine system, psychological or behavioural activities caused by hormones

MJGD.label: Medicine: Diabetes
MJGD.notes: Use for: medical works about Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes, Gestational diabetes mellitus, Maturity onset diabetes of the young (MODY)

MJH.label: Gastroenterology
MJH.notes: Use for: works on the study of and related disorders, diseases diagnosis and treatment of the human digestive system, the gastrointestinal tract, gastroenterological diseases

MJJ.label: Hepatology
MJJ.notes: Use for: works on the study of and related disorders, diagnosis and treatment of the liver, gallbladder, biliary tract, pancreas

MJK.label: Dermatology
MJK.notes: Use for: general works for medicine dealing with the skin, hair or nails, medical works on skin conditions, skin diseases, works for dermatologists, dermatopathology, trichology and trichoscopy

MJL.label: Respiratory medicine
MJL.notes: Also class here: pulmonology, pneumology, respirology, chest medicine, pulmonary medicine, thoracic medicine

MJM.label: Rheumatology
MJM.notes: Use for: works on diagnosis and therapy of rheumatic diseases, arthropathies or joint diseases, such as osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, connective tissue diseases

MJP.label: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
MJP.notes: Also class here: Ear, Nose and Throat, otolaryngology (head and neck surgery), Laryngology and Rhinology. Use with: MN* codes for works about surgical techniques

MJPD.label: Audiology and otology
MJPD.notes: Also class here: Neurotology. Use for: works on hearing, balance and related disorders, anatomy and physiology of the ear, inner ear, the vestibular sensory systems and the related diseases, diagnosis and treatments

MJQ.label: Ophthalmology
MJQ.notes: Also class here: ophthalmic, ocular or eye surgery. Use for: works on disorders of the eye, and the related diseases, diagnosis and treatments, specialist works for ophthalmologist. Use with: MN codes for works about surgical techniques relating to eye surgery

MJR.label: Renal medicine and nephrology
MJR.notes: Use for: medical works on the study of the kidneys, kidney medicine, kidney functions or renal physiology, or kidney disease or renal pathophysiology and the related diseases, diagnosis and treatments

MJS.label: Urology and urogenital medicine
MJS.notes: Also class here: male sexual dysfunction, medical works on the genitourinary system, or urogenital system, surgery or medical diseases of the male and female urinary tract and male reproductive organs

MKC.label: Gynaecology and obstetrics
MKC.notes: Use for: medical works about the health of the female reproductive system, or the field of study concentrated on pregnancy, childbirth and the postpartum period, OBGYN medicine

MKD.label: Paediatric medicine / child and adolescent medicine
MKD.notes: Use for: works about the medical care of infants, children, and adolescents, for works aimed at paediatricians, child health, adolescent health, young adult health. Use with: other M* codes for medical specialities relating to children and adolescents, for example, with MKL for child and adolescent psychiatry, MJCL for paediatric oncology, MKE for paediatric dentistry, etc, and with JBSP* codes and 5L* qualifiers to indicate the age group concerned

MKDN.label: Neonatal medicine
MKDN.notes: Also class here: Neonatology. Use for: works about the medical care of new-born infants, ill or premature new-borns

MKE.label: Dentistry and related oral medicines
MKE.notes: Also class here: Craniofacial, dental medicine, preventive, therapeutic and cosmetic dentistry, dental hygiene, stomatology, Oral mucosal abnormalities, oral pathologies. Use for: works about basic, general and clinical dentistry, medicine relating to the mouth and mouth diseases. Use with: MQC* for dental nursing, MBPM for Dental administration, etc

MKED.label: Orthodontics
MKED.notes: Also class here: dentofacial orthopaedics, orthodontia

MKEH.label: Dentistry specialities
MKEH.notes: Also class here: Prosthodontics, Endodontics, Periodontics, Paediatric dentistry, dental anaesthesiology

MKF.label: Pathology
MKF.notes: Use for: works about the study of the causes and effects of disease or injury, works on general pathology. Use with: MFG* for pathophysiology or physiopathology, use with other M* codes for other specialised areas of pathology

MKFK.label: Chronic diseases and conditions
MKFK.notes: Also class here: Chronic fatigue syndrome

MKFM.label: Medical microbiology and virology
MKFM.notes: Also class here: bacteriophage, phage therapy, antibiotics, antivirals, medical bacteriology

MKFM1.label: Medicine: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) / multiresistance
MKFM1.notes: Also class here: Antibacterial Resistance, antibiotic resistance, multiple drug resistance, superbugs, multidrug-resistant organisms, extensively drug-resistant (XDR), pandrug-resistant (PDR). Use with: PSG for non-medical microbiology

MKG.label: Pharmacology
MKG.notes: Also class here: Ethnopharmacology, Biopharmacology, medicinal plants and pharmacology, etc. Use for: works on basic, general and clinical pharmacology or for works on pharmaceutical science, the study of drugs and their actions on living systems or how they work in the body. Use with: other M* or P* codes as appropriate

MKGW.label: Psychopharmacology
MKGW.notes: Also class here: psychoactive drugs, psychopharmaceuticals, psychopharmacological substances. Use for: works about the study of drugs that affect mood, sensation, thinking, behaviour and cognition

MKJ.label: Neurology and clinical neurophysiology
MKJ.notes: Also class here: Peripheral neuropathy. Use for: works on neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, and diseases and disorders of the nervous system, or the diagnosis and treatment of all categories of conditions, disorders and disease involving the nervous system, the brain, the spinal cord, the central and the peripheral nerves. Use with: MKL* for Neuropsychiatry, with 5PM* qualifiers for specific neurodevelopmental disorders

MKJA.label: Autism Spectrum Disorder
MKJA.notes: Also class here: autistic spectrum disorder, Asperger’s Syndrome

MKJD.label: Alzheimer’s, dementia, Parkinson’s disease and other neurodegenerative diseases
MKJD.notes: Also class here: Neurocognitive disorders, cognitive disorders, major neurocognitive disorder, memory disorders, Parkinson’s disease

MKL.label: Psychiatry
MKL.notes: Also class here: works about psychiatric assessment, treatments, works for psychiatrists. Use with: other M* codes for specialities within psychiatry and with JBSP* and 5L* codes for psychiatry for specific age groups, child Psychiatry JBSP1, adolescent psychiatry JBSP2, MKN and JBSP4 for geriatric psychiatry, JBSP3 for general adult psychiatry, MKG or MKGW for psychiatric medicines or psychopharmaceuticals, with JMA* codes for relation to different schools in psychology, with MKZR for Addiction psychiatry, with MKJ for Neuropsychiatry or Clinical Neuropsychiatry

MKLD.label: Psychiatric and mental disorders
MKLD.notes: Also class here: Neuropsychiatric disorders, psychological trauma, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), clinical depression, obsessive compulsive disorder, (OCD), personality disorders, anxiety disorders, Bipolar and related disorders, Schizophrenia spectrum and other psychotic disorders, disruptive behaviour and dissocial disorders, depressive disorders, trauma- or stress-related disorders, dissociative disorders, mood disorders, substance use disorders, etc. Use for: specialised general works about the diagnosis, causes, treatments of mental, behavioural or psychiatric disorders or works about specific disorders

MKM.label: Clinical psychology
MKM.notes: Also class here: Psychopathology, assessment and treatment of psychopathologies. Use all MKM* codes with: other M* codes for uses of psychology in different medical specialities and with JM* codes as appropriate, and with JBS*, 5L* or 5P* codes for works about particular groups, use with JMM for Clinical neuropsychology

MKMT.label: Psychotherapy
MKMT.notes: Also class here: general works on psychotherapy, psychological therapy, talk therapy, or talking therapies, individual therapy. Use with: other M* codes for use of psychotherapies within different medical specialities and with JM* codes to indicate particular specialities

MKMT1.label: Psychotherapy: therapies or techniques
MKMT1.notes: Also class here: individual one-to-one therapy, integrative counselling, body psychotherapy. Use for: works about specific types of psychotherapy and therapies that do not have a more precise MKMT code. Use with: other M* codes or JM* codes as appropriate and 5L* or 5P* qualifiers if applicable

MKMT2.label: Psychotherapy: group
MKMT2.notes: Also class here: Group therapy, psychodynamic group therapy, co-therapy. Use for: works that look at form of psychotherapy when delivered in a group format, or any form of psychotherapy in which one or more therapists treat a small group of clients together as a group. Use with: other subject codes or qualifiers as appropriate

MKMT3.label: Psychotherapy: child and adolescent
MKMT3.notes: Use with: MKL* for child or adolescent psychiatry

MKMT4.label: Psychotherapy: couples and families
MKMT4.notes: Also class here: Relationship therapy, family counselling, family systems therapy, marriage or marital therapy, couples and family therapy, couples’ counselling, therapies that focus on families or couples in intimate relationships, relationship issues counselling

MKPB.label: Trauma and shock
MKPB.notes: Also class here: Traumatology, medical trauma. Use for: works on the treatment, diagnosis and management of shock or severe, acute physical injuries or wounds in emergency medicine. Use with: MKL*, MKMT*, MKZ* or JM* codes for works on psychological traumatology as appropriate

MKPL.label: Intensive care medicine
MKPL.notes: Also class here: critical care medicine

MKSG.label: Medical imaging: nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR / MRI)

MKW.label: Sports injuries and medicine
MKW.notes: Also class here: sport and exercise medicine. Use for: medical works about physical fitness and the treatment and prevention of injuries related to athletes, sports and exercise

MKZ.label: Therapy and therapeutics
MKZ.notes: Use for: general works on therapies or treatments used in different medical specialities or in general. Use with: other M* codes for works that look at therapies or treatments for a particular medical area

MKZD.label: Eating disorders and therapy
MKZD.notes: Also class here: works on therapies or treatments for eating disorders such as, anorexia nervosa, bulimia, binge eating disorder (BED), Avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID), Other specified feeding or eating disorder (OSFED)

MKZL.label: Speech and language disorders and therapy
MKZL.notes: Also class here: Speech-Language Pathology, all therapies associated with speech and language, use of Augmentative and Alternative Communication

MKZP.label: Psychosocial therapy / treatments
MKZP.notes: Also class here: Psychosocial interventions, psychoeducation, psychosocial rehabilitation, assertive community treatment, vocational rehabilitation, etc. Use for: works about therapies that are a mixture of different talk therapies or psychotherapy and social and vocational help, or works about psychological treatment designed to help an individual with emotional or behavioural disturbances adjust to situations that require social interaction with members of the family, work group, community, or any other social unit. Use with: other M* codes for use of psychosocial therapies in particular medical specialities, for example, with MJCL for Psychosocial oncology, psycho-oncology, or psychiatric oncology

MKZS.label: Sleep disorders and therapy
MKZS.notes: Also class here: Somnipathy and insomnia, sleep apnoea

MN.label: Surgery
MN.notes: Use for: general works on surgery. Use with: other M* codes for surgical specialities that do not have a unique MN* code, for example with MJQ for ophthalmic surgery, MJP for ENT surgery, MKD for paediatric surgery, MJS for Urological surgery, etc

MQ.label: Nursing and ancillary services
MQ.notes: Use for: works for healthcare professionals, allied professions or ancillary roles that do not have their own code, or for general works

MQC.label: Nursing

MQCL.label: Nursing specialties
MQCL.notes: Use with: other M* or JK* codes to indicate particular specialities when there is no more precise MQCL* code for works on nursing specialities

MQCL2.label: Intensive care nursing
MQCL2.notes: Also class here: critical care nursing

MQCL4.label: Geriatric nursing
MQCL4.notes: Also class here: gerontological nursing, nursing and care of elderly

MQCL6.label: Surgical nursing
MQCL6.notes: Also class here: Perioperative and theatre nursing

MQCL7.label: Nurse practitioner / Advanced Practice nursing and equivalents

MQCL8.label: Learning disability nursing / Special needs nursing

MQCL9.label: Terminal care nursing
MQCL9.notes: Also class here: Palliative nursing, end of life care

MQCW.label: Nursing sociology

MQCX.label: Community nursing

MQCX1.label: Home care / domiciliary care
MQCX1.notes: Also class here: home healthcare nursing, Private Duty Nursing, social care, in-home medical care, family support, home nursing, care in the community, End of life care at home, home palliative care. MQG.label: Medical assistants / Physicians’ assistants
MQG.notes: Also class here: clinical assistants, healthcare assistants, physicians’ associates. Use for: qualified healthcare professionals training or trained to assist doctors, physicians and other qualified medical professionals. Use with: other M* codes to indicate a speciality

MQP.label: Pharmacy / dispensing
MQP.notes: Also class here: Prescribing guidelines, Formulary, Pharmacopeia, guides to drugs and medication, information for pharmacists, administration of drugs, medication handbooks, dosage calculations

MQS.label: Physiotherapy
MQS.notes: Also class here: physical therapy, exercise prescription

MQT.label: Occupational therapy
MQT.notes: Also class here: Recreational Therapy, Horticultural therapy

MQTC.label: Creative therapy / Expressive therapies
MQTC.notes: Also class here: art, music, drama therapy, dance / movement therapy, bibliotherapy, play-based therapy, writing therapy

MQW.label: Biomedical engineering / Medical engineering
MQW.notes: Also class here: the medical aspects of bioinformatics, biomechanics, biomaterial, biomedical optics, tissue engineering, genetic engineering, neural engineering, pharmaceutical engineering, rehabilitation engineering and associated professionals. Use for: works that look at the application of engineering principles and design concepts to medicine and biology for healthcare purposes, or works that look at the management of current medical equipment in hospitals while adhering to relevant industry standards. Use with: other M*, P*, T* or U* codes as appropriate

MR.label: Medical study and revision guides and reference material

MRG.label: Medical study, exam preparation and revision guides
MRG.notes: Use with: PLACE 1* or EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers for medical exams, levels and qualifications as appropriate

MRP.label: Medical guidelines / Clinical guidelines
MRP.notes: Use with: relevant medical speciality category

MRT.label: Medical charts, colour atlases
MRT.notes: Also class here: anatomical charts, atlases and posters

MX.label: Complementary, integrated and alternative medicine and therapies

MXN.label: Animal-assisted therapy

MZC.label: Veterinary medicine: small animals

MZD.label: Veterinary medicine: large animals
MZD.notes: Also class here: veterinary medicine of domestic / farm animals

MZG.label: Veterinary medicine: exotic and zoo animals

N.label: History and Archaeology
N.notes: Use all N* codes for: specialist and general adult titles. DO NOT USE: code ‘N’ itself, but select specific categories from section N*. Use all N* codes with: other subject categories and qualifiers where appropriate, in particular PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers. A History work will usually need more than one subject category, from either History or non-History subjects to give greater detail, for example categories from Social Sciences (J*) with NHTB

NH.label: History
NH.notes: Use for: general history of broad topics, places etc. Use all NH* codes with: other subject codes to give more detail and also PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate. Prefer: ‘history of’ categories from within that subject where they exist, e.g. PDX History of science, QRAX history of Religion or KCZ Economic History

NHA.label: History: theory and methods
NHA.notes: Also class here: Historical method, historical research theories, Reception history, schools of historical thought, cyclical theories, Linear theories, Historical determinism, Exceptionalism, Historiometry, Historical Progressivism, Societal collapse, Sociocultural evolution, Comparative historical research, Historical materialism, Longue durée, Annales school, Great man theory, Interdisciplinary historical research

NHAP.label: Historical research: source documents
NHAP.notes: Use for: works about the subject, and also the historical documents published in contemporary or modern formats, usually as annotated versions of the original text or modern translations

NHB.label: General and world history
NHB.notes: Also class here: Universal history, global histories, transnational history, comparative histories, encyclopaedias, dictionaries or timelines of world history. Use for: works that take a truly global view of history and that do not fit into a more precise history category. Use with: an appropriate subject category for general or global history of specific topics. Prefer: ‘history of’ categories from within that subject where they exist

NHC.label: Ancient history
NHC.notes: Use for: works about ancient history according to the concept or notion of ‘ancient history’ as applied to the particular region and subject of the work. Use with: other NH* codes and relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHD.label: European history
NHD.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1D* or 1QB* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHDA.label: European history: the Romans
NHDA.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHDC.label: European history: the Celts
NHDC.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHDE.label: European history: the Vikings
NHDE.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHDG.label: European history: the Normans
NHDG.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHDJ.label: European history: medieval period, middle ages
NHDJ.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHDL.label: European history: Renaissance
NHDL.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHDN.label: European history: Reformation
NHDN.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHF.label: Asian history
NHF.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1F* or 1QB* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHG.label: Middle Eastern history
NHG.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1FB* or 1QB* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHH.label: African history
NHH.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1H* or 1QB* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHHA.label: African history: pre-colonial
NHHA.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1H* or 1QB* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHK.label: History of the Americas
NHK.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1K*, 1QB* or 1QP*, TIME PERIOD 3* and INTEREST 5P* Qualifiers as appropriate, and with other N* codes for histories of different topics in history or with other non-fiction subject codes for specialised histories within the Americas

NHKA.label: History of the Americas: pre-contacts
NHKA.notes: Also class here: pre-Columbian, pre-colonization, pre-invasion, pre-colonial, pre-Hispanic, pre-Cabraline histories of the Americas, archaeological stages of history, peopling of the Americas, history from oral transmission of knowledge or events. Use for: histories of regions or of the Indigenous peoples, groups, Nations or cultures in the Americas prior to being conquered, invaded, colonised or significantly influenced by Europeans or other non-Indigenous cultures. Use with: relevant PLACE 1K*, 1QB* or 1QP*, TIME PERIOD 3* and INTEREST 5P* Qualifiers as appropriate, and with other N* codes for histories of different topics in history or with other non-fiction subject codes for specialised histories within the Americas

NHM.label: Australasian and Pacific history
NHM.notes: Also class here: Histories of Oceania, Melanesia, Micronesia, Polynesia, etc. Use with: relevant PLACE 1M* or 1QB* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHQ.label: History of other geographical groupings and regions or specific cultures / societies / groups / peoples
NHQ.notes: Also class here: Antarctica, the Polar regions, isolated oceanic islands etc. Use for: works about areas not covered by other NH* codes or trans-continental or multi-location histories, or works that look at specific groupings of people, ethnic groups, cultural areas or regions, cultural groupings, socio- economic groups, language groups, minority communities, diaspora groups, that do not fit in with the geographical history subject codes. Use with: relevant PLACE 1*, LANGUAGE 2*, TIME PERIOD 3* and 5* INTEREST Qualifiers as appropriate

NHT.label: History: specific events and topics
NHT.notes: Use all NHT* codes with: regional NH* codes where possible and other subject codes to give more detail and also PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* and 5* INTEREST Qualifiers as appropriate

NHTB.label: Social and cultural history
NHTB.notes: Use with: other subject codes, especially J* codes, to indicate what branch of, or topic in, social or cultural history the work is about, for example, for labour history use with JHBL, or JBSF1 for women’s history, etc

NHTB1.label: Historical cross-cultural or intercultural interactions / encounters
NHTB1.notes: Also class here: Cross-cultural Exchanges in history. Use for: works that look at aspects of historical interactions between different cultures, groups, peoples or nations, when different cultures first encounter or come into contact, the influences of one culture on another, or historical interactions between different groups, such as traders or merchants encountering different groups, colonisers and colonised, explorers or settlers and Indigenous peoples, agricultural societies and hunter- gatherers, nomadic groups and settled communities, industrialised economies meeting non-industrialised cultures, monotheistic belief systems encountering alternative worldviews, impact of technological developments on different cultures, etc

NHTD.label: Oral history
NHTD.notes: Also class here: Oral transmission of histories, narratives, lessons and other knowledge of cultures, collections of transcribed or recorded oral narratives or personal testimonies to historical events, life in the past, oral stories that reflect the history of a particular culture, people, place, etc

NHTF.label: History: plagues, diseases, famines
NHTF.notes: Also class here: the Black Death, Bubonic Plague, Plague of Justinian, Spanish Flu, Cocoliztli epidemics, HIV/AIDS, Covid, Soviet Famine, Holodomor, Bengal Famine, European Potato Failure, or other historical outbreaks of particular diseases or famines. Use for: works about epidemics, pandemics, pestilence, infectious diseases, famines in history. Use with: JBFF for studies of the social impact on past societies

NHTK.label: Industrialisation and industrial history
NHTK.notes: Also class here: industrial or technological revolutions, impact of industrial or technological changes on society

NHTM.label: Maritime history
NHTM.notes: Also class here: nautical histories of seafaring, sailors, whaling, fishing, navigation, exploration, maritime trade, shipping, sea-related communities, navies, naval history, etc. Use for: any historical aspect of human interaction with or activity at sea. Use with: NHW* or JWCK for histories of naval warfare, WGG* codes for histories of types of vessels

NHTM1.label: Maritime history: Pirates / piracy
NHTM1.notes: Also class here: Privateers, corsairs, maritime smugglers, the Sea Peoples, pirate shipwrecks, commerce raiding, merchant raiding, buccaneers, sea borne raiders, Viking raiders. Use for: works about the history of illegal (at least at the time) or non-naval maritime criminality, criminals or groups

NHTP.label: Historical geography
NHTP.notes: Also class here: histories of borders, frontiers, boundaries, borderlands, histories of changing aspects the landscape, historical aspects of human geography. Use with: RGC* codes as appropriate

NHTP1.label: Historical maps and atlases
NHTP1.notes: Use for: works that present a history of a topic through maps – of any sort, including old maps or purpose drawn – as well as a standard atlas of history

NHTQ.label: Colonialism and imperialism
NHTQ.notes: Also class here: colonisation, studies of colonies or empires, New Imperialism, neo-colonialism, impacts of colonialism, colonisers and colonised, colonial settlements and settlers. Use with: NHW* codes for military history titles about colonial wars and conflicts, with JPS* for studies of new colonial or imperial powers

NHTR.label: National liberation and independence
NHTR.notes: Also class here: National revival movements, national awakenings. Use for: works about achieving independence, or histories of newly independent societies. Use with: NHW* codes for military history titles about wars of liberation and independence

NHTR1.label: Decolonisation and postcolonial studies
NHTR1.notes: Use for: works that look at the process of undoing colonialism, the end of colonial empires, continued indirect colonialism, cultural colonialism as well as works that look at the history after the colonising power is no longer in full, direct control

NHTS.label: Slavery, enslaved persons and abolition of slavery
NHTS.notes: Also class here: History of enslaved peoples or enslaved persons, the slave trade, chattel slavery, the emancipation of slaves, serfdom, bonded labour, lives of enslaved persons, the struggle and fights for abolition, the abolition of slavery and serfdom. Use for: works about any form or aspect of historical slavery in different societies, cultures or regions. Use with: DNB* or DNC codes for slave narratives or with NHTD for oral history of enslaved persons or with F* codes for stories about enslaved people

NHTT.label: Invasion, conquest and occupation
NHTT.notes: Use with: NHW* codes for military history titles about wars or conflicts linked to invasion, conquest or occupation

NHTV.label: Revolutions, uprisings, rebellions
NHTV.notes: Also class here: insurgencies, insurrections, violent attempts to change existing systems, Coups d’état, etc. Use with: NHW* codes for military history titles about wars or conflicts linked to revolution, uprisings, revolts, rebellions, etc

NHTW.label: Cold wars and proxy conflicts
NHTW.notes: Also class here: The Cold War, phoney wars. Use for: works that examine conflicts between nations that do not involve direct military action but are pursued primarily through economic and political actions, propaganda, espionage or proxy wars waged by surrogates

NHTX.label: Violence, intolerance and persecution in history
NHTX.notes: Also class here: Purges, pogroms, violent repression, cruelties, atrocities, massacres, lynchings, burnings, witch hunts, riots, mob violence, civil disorder, vigilante justice, feuds, etc. Use for: works that examine these themes in history, aspects of these topics or specific events in different societies, cultures or regions. Use with: 5P* qualifiers for works about historical violence, intolerance or persecution against or by specific groups

NHW.label: Military history
NHW.notes: Use all NHW* codes with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate, and other NH* codes for specific types of war, NHTQ for colonial wars, NHTR for wars of liberation, wars of independence, NHTT for military invasions, wars of conquest, military occupations, wars to seize territory, NHTV for wars of revolution, military uprisings, wars of rebellion, NHTW for proxy wars, etc, or with JW* codes for Military history approaches to these topics, or with QRAM9 for wars and conflicts based on religion or religious wars or holy wars

NHWA.label: Ancient warfare
NHWA.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHWD.label: Medieval warfare (predating gunpowder warfare)
NHWD.notes: Also class here: the Crusades, medieval siege warfare. Use for: works that look at warfare post-antiquity, usually periods of greater use of mounted cavalry, and technologies such as the stirrup, or heavily armoured knights or castles, but prior to modern technologies such as gunpowder warfare. Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHWF.label: Early modern warfare (including gunpowder warfare)
NHWF.notes: Use for: works that look at warfare in periods when gunpowder and associated armaments and techniques were developed and used. Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHWL.label: Modern warfare
NHWL.notes: Also class here: Contemporary methods and techniques of warfare, fourth-generation warfare, industrial warfare. Use for: works that look at periods of total war, war using industrial techniques, sophisticated technologies, conscript armies etc. Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHWR.label: Specific wars and military campaigns
NHWR.notes: Also class here: Specific military conflicts, operations, periods of combat. Use for: works that look at particular wars or campaigns (the name of the war is described in other metadata). Use with: other NH* codes for types of war, e.g. and relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate, e.g. for a military history title about the Thirty Years War in Europe, use with 1D and 3MGB-DE-B

NHWR1.label: Specific battles
NHWR1.notes: Also class here: Individual military engagements, battles, skirmishes or sieges. Use for: works that look at particular battles (the name of the battle is described in other metadata). Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHWR3.label: Civil wars
NHWR3.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHWR5.label: First World War
NHWR5.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHWR7.label: Second World War
NHWR7.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

NHWR9.label: Military history: post-WW2 conflicts
NHWR9.notes: Also class here: Contemporary and recent conflicts, ongoing armed conflicts, conflicts of the late 20th century, the 21st century, frozen conflicts, active conflicts, etc. Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate, e.g. for a title about the Iran-Iraq War use with 1FBN, 1FBQ and 3MPQX

NKD.label: Archaeology by period / region
NKD.notes: Use with: relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate, e.g. for Prehistoric archaeology, use with 3B* TIME PERIOD qualifiers or for Egyptology use with 1QBAE and 3* qualifiers

NKDS.label: Archaeological sites
NKDS.notes: Also class here: works about specific sites or digs

NKR.label: Underwater archaeology
NKR.notes: Also class here: maritime or marine archaeology

P.label: Mathematics and Science
P.notes: Use all P* codes for: mostly academic, technical and specialist titles and some general adult works. Qualifiers are mostly not required with P* codes. DO NOT USE: code ‘P’ itself, but select specific categories from section P*. Prefer: WN* codes for general interest adult titles where appropriate

PBKF.label: Functional analysis and transforms
PBKF.notes: Also class here: Fourier, Hilbert, Laplace, Z transforms

PD.label: Science: general issues
PD.notes: Use for: the natural sciences as well as general works on the different branches of science. Use with: other subject codes as appropriate

PDC.label: Scientific nomenclature and classification
PDC.notes: Use with: other P*, M*, T* for works about classification in different sciences or technologies, for example use with MJC for the classification of diseases or disorders (nosology)

PDG.label: Industrial applications of scientific research and technological innovation

PDJ.label: Regulation of science and experimentation
PDJ.notes: Use for: works on regulation, whether legal or directed by other bodies or authorities, aimed at scientists and practitioners. Use with: other P* code indicating area of science where appropriate

PDND.label: Microscopy
PDND.notes: Also class here: optical, electron, scanning probe microscopy, X-ray microscopy, ultraviolet and infrared microscopy, digital or virtual microscopy, etc

PDR.label: Impact of science and technology on society
PDR.notes: Use for: works that look that at impact that any science or technology has had or could have on society. Use with: NHTB for social history or other P* or T* or J* codes as appropriate

PDT.label: Nanosciences
PDT.notes: Use for: nanomaterials, nanomaterial synthesis, nanoparticle chemistry. Use with: other P* codes for applications of nanoscience in different scientific fields, or with M* codes for applications in medical sciences

PDZ.label: Popular science
PDZ.notes: Use all PDZ* codes for: highly accessible works for the general reader, that usually take a broad, generalist view of a science topic, and may also be a simplified approach to that particular subject. Use with: other P* code indicating area of science given popular treatment. DO NOT USE: for indicating a title that sells well or has been a bestseller or is popularly purchased title

PDZM.label: Popular and recreational mathematics
PDZM.notes: Use with: other PB* codes indicating the area of maths given popular treatment as appropriate

PGG.label: Astronomical observation: observatories, equipment and methods

PGM.label: Galaxies and stars
PGM.notes: Also class here: exoplanets, extrasolar planets

PGS.label: Solar system: the Sun and planets
PGS.notes: Also class here: the Moons of the different planets

PHFC.label: Condensed matter physics (liquid state and solid state physics)
PHFC.notes: Also class here: Physics of rigid matter or solids

PHJ.label: Optical physics
PHJ.notes: Also class here: optics and photonics

PHQ.label: Quantum physics (quantum mechanics and quantum field theory)

PHR.label: Relativity physics
PHR.notes: Also class here: physics of time

PHV.label: Applied physics
PHV.notes: Use with: other P* codes for applications of physics in specific domains

PNA.label: Periodic table of the Elements
PNA.notes: Also class here: the chemical elements, such as oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, helium, neon, iron, silicon, magnesium, potassium, sodium, sulphur, phosphorus, chlorine, calcium, the noble gases, alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, rare-earth elements, lanthanides, actinides, transition metals, metalloids, nonmetals, halogens, etc and periodic trends, periodic laws, the classification of the elements

PNB.label: Medicinal chemistry
PNB.notes: Also class here: drug discovery and design, drug development

PNC.label: Environmental chemistry

PSAD.label: Bioethics
PSAD.notes: Use for: issues surrounding the ethics of practices typically connected to new developments in biology and medicine

PSAF.label: Ecological science, the Biosphere
PSAF.notes: Use for: comprehensive scientific, objective and descriptive works on living organisms and their relationship with their environment

PSAJ.label: Evolution / Evolutionary biology
PSAJ.notes: Also class here: History of evolutionary thought, origin of life, mutation in DNA, genetic drift, gene flow, natural selection, biogeography, evolutionary developmental biology, evolutionary ecology, adaptive evolution, convergent evolution, divergent evolution, coevolution, macroevolution, microevolution, abiogenesis. Use with: other codes for subfields and specialised subjects in evolution

PSAK.label: Genetics (non-medical)
PSAK.notes: Also class here: DNA, Genome, RNA, transcriptome, genetic resources, genomics, epigenetics, DNA extraction, DNA sequencing, etc. Use with: NK* codes for Archaeogenetics, NH* codes for Genetic histories, PSXE for human evolution, PSAJ for evolutionary biology, or Population genetics, RBX for Palaeogenetics, etc

PSAN.label: Neurosciences

PSB.label: Biochemistry
PSB.notes: Also class here: biochemical immunology, non-medical toxicology, enzymology, lipids, biological chemistry, metabolism, biomolecules, proteins, etc

PSBD.label: Phytochemistry
PSBD.notes: Also class here: phytochemicals, plant biochemistry, pharmacognosy. Use with: MKG for works aimed at pharmacists

PSG.label: Microbiology (non-medical)
PSG.notes: Also class here: archaea, bacteria, chromista, oomycetes, water moulds, protistology, protist, slime mould, non-medical bacteriology, parasitology, virology, etc

PSQ.label: Mycology, fungi
PSQ.notes: Also class here: lichenology, mycorrhiza, lichens, fungus, mushrooms, toadstools, yeasts. Use for: works about fungi and works about human use of fungi, in medicine, food, fermentation, cultivation, etc

PSTJ.label: Conifers and gymnosperms
PSTJ.notes: Also class here: cycads, ginkgo and gnetophytes

PSV.label: Zoology and animal sciences
PSV.notes: Also class here: animal physiology, reproduction, pathology and diseases, animal ecology

PSVA.label: Zoology: invertebrates
PSVA.notes: Also class here: annelids (worms), Myriapoda, echinoderms (starfish, sea urchins), jellyfish

PSVA2.label: Insects (entomology)
PSVA2.notes: Also class here: caterpillars, butterflies and moths

PSVA4.label: Crustaceans (carcinology)
PSVA4.notes: Also class here: crabs, lobsters, crayfish, shrimp, krill, woodlice, barnacles, etc

PSVA6.label: Molluscs (malacology)
PSVA6.notes: Also class here: cephalopod, octopus, squid, gastropods, snails, slugs, bivalves, clams, oysters, cockles, mussels, scallops, etc

PSVA8.label: Arachnids (arachnology)
PSVA8.notes: Also class here: spiders, scorpions, ticks, mites, etc

PSVM2.label: Zoology: marine and freshwater mammals
PSVM2.notes: Also class here: Cetacea and Sirenia – whales, dolphins, sea cows, etc. Use for: aquatic and semiaquatic mammals

PSVM3.label: Zoology: primates (primatology)
PSVM3.notes: Also class here: lemurs, monkeys, apes

PSX.label: Human biology
PSX.notes: Use for: works about the human body or parts of the human body, or that look at human physiology or anatomy from a non-medical, human biology point of view, works on the human skeleton and bones, blood, muscles, tissues, the brain, the intestines, teeth, hair, human sex, etc

PSXE.label: Evolutionary anthropology / Human evolution
PSXE.notes: Also class here: early man, palaeoanthropology, Hominidae, human forebears and archaic humans, biological anthropology, physical anthropology, anthropogeny. Use with: 3A* or 3B* time period qualifiers if appropriate, with NK* for archaeological studies

Q.label: Philosophy and Religion
Q.notes: Also class here: Belief systems and worldviews. Use all Q* codes for: academic, specialist and general adult titles. DO NOT USE: code ‘Q’ itself, but select specific categories from section Q*. Use with: QRA* and QRV* codes should be used with other QR* codes to denote which particular religion

QDH.label: Philosophical traditions and schools of thought
QDH.notes: Also class here: History of Philosophy. Use all QDH* codes with: other Q* codes, relevant PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

QDHA.label: Ancient Greek and Roman philosophy
QDHA.notes: Also class here: Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, Pythagoras, Pre-Socratic and Hellenistic philosophy, Stoicism, Sophism, Cynicism, Epicureanism, etc. and associated schools of thought

QDHF.label: Medieval Western philosophy

QDHH.label: Humanist philosophy
QDHH.notes: Also class here: Renaissance humanism, Erasmus

QDHM.label: Western philosophy: Enlightenment
QDHM.notes: Also class here: Empiricism, Rationalism, Descartes to Kant

QDHP.label: African philosophy
QDHP.notes: Also class here: Africana philosophy and critical theory

QDHR.label: Western philosophy from c 1800
QDHR.notes: Also class here: Post-Kantian philosophy, Continental philosophy, Critical theory. Use for: works about either Modern (c 17th to early 20th century) or Contemporary (20th and 21st century) philosophy from the ‘Western’ tradition

QDHR1.label: Idealism
QDHR1.notes: Also class here: German idealism, subjective or objective idealism

QDHR3.label: Pragmatism
QDHR3.notes: Also class here: pragmatics, the Pragmatists

QDHR9.label: Analytical philosophy and Logical Positivism
QDHR9.notes: Also class here: Positivists, Neopositivism, Logical empiricism

QDTK.label: Philosophy: epistemology and theory of knowledge
QDTK.notes: Also class here: Epistemics, philosophical scepticism

QDTL.label: Philosophy: logic
QDTL.notes: Also class here: formal, informal or symbolic logic, Critical Thinking

QDTM.label: Philosophy of mind
QDTM.notes: Also class here: mind and body problem, dualism, monism, neurophilosophy, consciousness, Interactionism

QDTN.label: Philosophy: aesthetics
QDTN.notes: Also class here: debates about the nature of beauty and taste, the philosophy of art, aesthetic judgment, aesthetic universals

QDTQ.label: Ethics and moral philosophy
QDTQ.notes: Also class here: axiology, meta-ethics, normative ethics, applied ethics, concepts of right and wrong behaviour, deontological ethics, deontology, nature of good and evil, utilitarianism, consequentialism, ethical theory, ethics of care

QDTS1.label: Critical theory
QDTS1.notes: Also class here: the Frankfurt School. Use with: J* codes for sociological approaches or schools of thought

QDX.label: Popular philosophy
QDX.notes: Use for: accessible works for the general reader seeking to apply principles of philosophy to everyday life, or works that use ordinary language to explain philosophy to a broad general audience. Use with: other QD* codes for works that are easily accessible approaches to different topics in philosophy

QDXB.label: Popular philosophy: Meaning of life / finding sense in life
QDXB.notes: Also class here: 42. Use for: works that take philosophical principles or thought systems to help people make sense of or understand aspects of everyday life, or the significance of living or existence, usually in an accessible way and aimed at a general reader. Prefer: VSP* or VX* codes for the works that look at this topic from a practical psychological or spiritual approach

QR.label: Religion and beliefs
