QRA.label: Religion: general
QRA.notes: Also class here: Religious Studies, general works on religions, general reference works on religion. Use all QRA* codes with: other QR* code indicating religion concerned

QRAB.label: Philosophy of religion
QRAB.notes: Use for: works on philosophical examinations of the central themes and concepts involved in religious traditions or the nature of religion as a whole

QRAB1.label: Nature and existence of God and of the Divine
QRAB1.notes: Use for: works on belief in or questions about the existence of a supreme being, deities or other divinities, or that examine the divine nature of these or the nature of divinity itself

QRAB7.label: Religion: Sin / salvation
QRAB7.notes: Use for: works that examine religious concepts, discussions or topics of repentance, salvation, redemption, forgiveness or notions of sin and the consequences of sin

QRAB9.label: Religion: Eschatology
QRAB9.notes: Use for: works that examine religious concepts of the end of the world or the end times, notions concerned with death, judgement and the destiny of the human soul, or ultimate destiny of humanity. Use with: other QR* codes as appropriate for eschatological traditions in different religions

QRAC.label: Comparative religion
QRAC.notes: Use with: QRVG for Intercultural Theology or Comparative theology

QRAM.label: Religious issues and debates
QRAM.notes: Also class here: Apologetics, general works on debates in religion. Use all QRAM* codes with: other QR* code indicating religion concerned, or with QRAC if comparative

QRAM1.label: Religious ethics
QRAM1.notes: Use for: works that look at notions ethics in religion or of morality in religious belief, rules and laws based on religious doctrines, value frameworks regarding personal behaviour for religious adherents, notions of right and wrong based on religious values, notions of virtue and manners in religious traditions, etc

QRAM2.label: Religion and politics
QRAM2.notes: Also class here: political theology, advocacy theology, freedom of religion, freedom of conscience, religion and secularism, role of religion in politics, use of religion or religious beliefs for political ends, official state religions, use of religion to create laws and political structures, Separation of church and state, disestablishmentarianism, laïcité, Latin American liberation theology, Black theology, Black Liberation Theology, Liberation Theology, etc

QRAM9.label: Religious intolerance, persecution and conflict
QRAM9.notes: Use for: works about discrimination, intolerance, violence or persecution of, or within, a religion, by others with different beliefs. Use with: JBFA for issues of discrimination in societies based on religious identity, with JW* or NHW* codes for religious wars or conflicts linked to religious beliefs, with INTEREST 5* qualifiers for intolerance or persecution of particular groups, for example, with 5PGJ for religious antisemitism, 5PGP for Islamophobia

QRDF.label: Hinduism: sacred texts and revered writings
QRDF.notes: Use all QRDF* codes with: QRVC for critiques or examination of sacred texts

QRFF.label: Buddhism: sacred texts and revered writings
QRFF.notes: Use all QRFF* codes with: QRVC for critiques or examination of sacred texts

QRJB1.label: Orthodox Judaism
QRJB1.notes: Also class here: Haredi Judaism, Modern Orthodox Judaism, Hasidic Judaism

QRJF.label: Judaism: sacred texts and revered writings
QRJF.notes: Use all QRJF* codes with: QRVC for midrash, critiques or examination of sacred texts

QRJF1.label: Jewish texts: Tanakh, Torah, Nevi’im, Ketuvim
QRJF1.notes: Also class here: Hebrew Bible, Five Books of Moses, Mikra

QRJF5.label: Rabbinic literature
QRJF5.notes: Also class here: Mishnah, the Talmud

QRMB.label: Christian Churches, denominations, groups
QRMB.notes: Also class here: Ecclesiology, Church history, the notion of the universal Church or local church, Ecclesiastical history

QRMB1.label: Roman Catholicism, Roman Catholic Church
QRMB1.notes: Also class here: Eastern Catholic Churches, Eastern Rite, Maronite, Uniates, Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church, Syro-Malabar, Melkite Catholic, Chaldean Catholic, Armenian Catholic

QRMB2.label: Orthodox and Oriental Orthodox Churches
QRMB2.notes: Also class here: Greek, Russian, Coptic, Syrian Churches, etc

QRMB3.label: Protestantism and Protestant Churches
QRMB3.notes: Also class here: Moravians, Moravian Brethren, Hussite Church, general works on Protestantism or protestant churches, or works on Proto-Protestantism

QRMB31.label: Anglican and Episcopalian Churches
QRMB31.notes: Also class here: Church of England, Anglicanism, the Anglican Communion, etc

QRMB33.label: Calvinist, Reformed and Presbyterian Churches
QRMB33.notes: Also class here: United Reformed, Church of Scotland, Huguenots, Calvinism, Congregationalism, Congregational churches, United Church of Christ, etc

QRMB36.label: Pentecostal or Charismatic Churches
QRMB36.notes: Also class here: Pentecostalism, the Charismatic and Neo-charismatic Movements and associated churches

QRMB38.label: Anabaptism and Anabaptist Churches
QRMB38.notes: Also class here: Amish, Mennonites, Hutterites, Bruderhof Communities, Schwarzenau Brethren, River Brethren, Apostolic Christian Church, Neo-Anabaptism

QRMB39.label: Other Nonconformist and Evangelical Churches
QRMB39.notes: Also class here: Shakers (United Society of Believers), La Luz del Mundo, Iglesia ni Cristo and other Nontrinitarian denominations, other non-denominational Christian churches

QRMB5.label: Denominations of American origin
QRMB5.notes: Also class here: Adventists, Mormons (Latter Day Saints), Jehovah’s Witnesses, Christian Science, etc

QRMB8.label: Christian and quasi-Christian cults and sects

QRMF.label: Christianity: sacred texts and revered writings
QRMF.notes: Use for: canonical and non-canonical writings. Use all QRMF* codes with: QRVC for critiques, exegesis or examinations of texts. Prefer: the relevant QRMF code for versions of the texts themselves

QRMF1.label: Bibles
QRMF1.notes: Use for: Any version of the Bible itself. Use with: QRVC for critiques or examination of the Bible, Biblical Studies, Biblical Concordances and Commentaries

QRMF12.label: Old Testaments
QRMF12.notes: Also class here: The Psalms, Septuagint, Pentateuch. Use with: QRVC for critiques or examination of books of the Old Testament

QRMF13.label: New Testaments
QRMF13.notes: Also class here: Gospels, Epistles. Use with: QRVC for critiques or examination of some or all of the books the New Testament

QRMF3.label: Writings of the Early Church Fathers
QRMF3.notes: Also class here: Patristics or patrology. Use for: the works of early Christian Writers and with QRVC for critiques of the texts or on its own when just the text

QRPB3.label: Islamic groups: Shi’ah, Shi’ite
QRPB3.notes: Also class here: Isma’ilism, Nizari Isma’ilism, Tayyibi Isma’ilism, Twelver Shi’ism, Imāmiyya, Zaydism

QRPF.label: Islam: sacred texts and revered writings
QRPF.notes: Use all QRPF* codes with: QRVC for tafsir, critiques or examinations of sacred texts

QRR.label: Further religions and spiritual beliefs
QRR.notes: Use for: works about living religions and their belief systems, worldviews, sacred histories and traditions, mythologies, practices, stories, rituals, etc that do not have a more specific code. Use with: other Q* codes and PLACE 1* Qualifiers as appropriate

QRRL.label: East Asian religions and spiritual beliefs
QRRL.notes: Also class here: Chinese salvationist religions, Japanese new religions. Use for: Taoic or East Asian religions, belief systems, or spiritual traditions that do not have a more specific code

QRRL6.label: Chinese folk religion / Chinese Mythology
QRRL6.notes: Also class here: Chinese folk belief, spiritual beliefs, sacred histories and traditions. Use with: FNM* for fantasy fiction inspired by Chinese mythology and Chinese traditions

QRRM.label: Afro-American / African diaspora religions
QRRM.notes: Also class here: Candomblé, Umbanda, Quimbanda, Voodoo, Voudou, Spiritual Baptist, Espiritismo, Hoodoo, Rastafari. Use for: Variations of African Religions in the Americas or syncretic religions and spiritual traditions of the Americas and Caribbean

QRRN.label: Traditional African religions and spiritual beliefs
QRRN.notes: Use for: works on the living and traditional belief systems of African peoples including their mythologies, pantheons, gods and spirits, creation or origin myths, stories, legends, practices, rituals, traditional healers, etc. Use with: PLACE 1* or LANGUAGE 2* or 5P* INTEREST Qualifiers to indicate a particular tradition

QRRT.label: Indigenous peoples: religions, belief systems, cultural worldviews and spiritual beliefs
QRRT.notes: Use for: works, when there is no more specific code, on religions and spiritual beliefs, including their living beliefs, cultural worldviews, sacred histories, sacred stories, Oral Traditions, mythologies, pantheons, gods and spirits, creation or origin stories, legends, practices, rituals etc. Use with: PLACE 1* or LANGUAGE 2* or 5P* INTEREST Qualifiers to indicate a particular tradition, e.g. for a work about the spiritual beliefs or traditions of Australian Aboriginal people use with 5PB-AU-AD

QRRT1.label: Indigenous peoples in the Americas: religions, belief systems, cultural worldviews and spiritual beliefs
QRRT1.notes: Also class here: religions, traditions and sacred histories and worldviews of the Aztec, Mayan, Olmec, Inca, Inuit or any of the other diverse Indigenous peoples, groups or nations in the Americas. Use for: works about living and traditional spiritual beliefs, worldviews including Oral Traditions, mythologies, religions, ceremonial practices, rituals and observances associated with the diverse Indigenous peoples, groups or nations in the Americas either now or that existed prior to first contact with Europeans or other non-indigenous cultures and beliefs. Use with: PLACE 1K* or LANGUAGE 2* or 5P* INTEREST Qualifiers to indicate a particular tradition

QRRV.label: Animism / Shamanism
QRRV.notes: Also class here: Shamans, animists, natural religion, nature worship, Fetishism, totemism. Use for: studies of these spiritual beliefs, associated rituals, practices, sacred stories, mythologies etc. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers to indicate a particular tradition. Prefer: VXWS for more popular approaches

QRS.label: Ancient religions and Mythologies
QRS.notes: Also class here: Paganism, pagan beliefs and practices, polytheism and ancient polytheistic religions, Comparative mythology, general studies of Mythology, studies of particular regional mythologies with no specific category. Use all QRS* codes for: works that study or examine these spiritual beliefs, sacred histories, ancient worldviews, their mythologies, pantheons, gods and spirits, creation or origin myths, stories, legends, practices, rituals etc. Use all QRS* codes with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers, especially 1QB* codes for historic entities, to indicate a particular tradition, other QR* codes for studies of mythologies associated with other living religions, and use with FN* codes if these are retellings in modern form of a traditional story from these religions

QRST.label: Celtic religion and mythology
QRST.notes: Also class here: Druids in Celtic beliefs. Use for: works about Celtic mythologies and beliefs. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers to indicate a particular tradition

QRSV.label: Slavic religion and mythology
QRSV.notes: Use for: works about pre-Christian Slavic mythologies and spiritual beliefs

QRSW.label: Norse religion and mythology
QRSW.notes: Use for: works about pre-Christian Nordic and Germanic (including Anglo-Saxon and Viking) mythologies and beliefs

QRV.label: Aspects of religion
QRV.notes: Use all QRV* codes with: other QR* code indicating religion concerned. Prefer: religion-specific codes where available, e.g. for Buddhist sacred texts, use QRFF, not QRF with QRVA

QRVA.label: Sacred texts, scriptures and revered writings
QRVA.notes: Use all QRVA* codes for: works about the texts as well as copies of the texts themselves. Use with: an appropriate code such as QRVC for studies, analysis, histories etc

QRVA2.label: Readings, selections and meditations from sacred texts
QRVA2.notes: Use for: general collections or with other QR* codes for selections from specific texts, or works that explore meditation in different religious and spiritual traditions, aids to meditation, religious contemplation and similar spiritual practices taken from or inspired by sacred texts. Use with: DNT for anthologies of readings from different texts

QRVB.label: Sacred stories / sacred histories
QRVB.notes: Also class here: Sacred stories that reflect a particular community’s sacred or religious worldview, that helps explain the fundamentals of human existence, explain where everything we know comes from, why we are here, where we are going, and even our existential purpose as seen in that particular worldview, including narratives of origin or creation, stories of individuals, tales of place, people, animals, beings that help explain the particular worldview. Use for: Modern retellings, or older versions of particular narratives or studies of these histories

QRVC.label: Criticism and exegesis of sacred texts
QRVC.notes: Also class here: concordances, commentaries. Use for: Studies of scriptures or religious texts. Use with: other QR* code indicating religion or text concerned, e.g. QRMF1 for studies and exegesis of the Bible, or QRPF1 for studies of the Koran (Qur’an)

QRVD.label: Religious doctrines
QRVD.notes: Also class here: Doctrinal studies. Use for: codification of beliefs or bodies of teachings or instructions, taught principles or positions, as the essence of teachings in a belief system

QRVG.label: Theology
QRVG.notes: Also class here: Pneumatology, Paterology, Patriology, Angelology, Theological thought, Soteriology, Theological anthropology, Hamartiology, Historical theology, Hierology, Intercultural Theology, Diaconia, Caritas Science, Mariology, Christology

QRVG2.label: Systematic theology / Dogmatics
QRVG2.notes: Also class here: systematics, dogmatic theology, articles of faith

QRVG3.label: Practical theology / Pastoral Theology
QRVG3.notes: Also class here: works on applied theology (such as missions, evangelism, religious education, pastoral psychology or the psychology of religion), church growth, administration, homiletics, spiritual formation, pastoral theology, spiritual direction, spiritual theology (or ascetical theology), political theology, theology of justice and peace and similar areas

QRVH.label: Sermons
QRVH.notes: Also class here: preaching. Use for: collections and analysis of sermons, for preaching techniques etc

QRVJ1.label: Worship, rites, ceremonies and rituals
QRVJ1.notes: Also class here: Hymnals, Psalters, ceremonial or sacred objects. Use for: works about ceremonial practices, rituals or observances, or works containing words, music and actions used in religious ceremonies, or works about religious ceremonial or sacred objects associated with different religious or spiritual traditions or types of worship

QRVJ2.label: Prayer and prayer books
QRVJ2.notes: Use for: collections of prayers as well as how to pray or aspects of prayer

QRVJ3.label: Devotional material
QRVJ3.notes: Use for: works that address ideas, themes, stories, and questions found in sacred texts and that is religious writing which is neither doctrinal nor theological, but designed for individuals to read for their personal edification and spiritual formation

QRVK.label: Spirituality and religious experience
QRVK.notes: Also class here: Spiritual awakening, development and personal religious growth, religious and spiritual meditations, prophecy and prophecies, popular accounts of spirituality or religious experiences

QRVK2.label: Mysticism
QRVK2.notes: Also class here: mystics, religious mystical and visionary experiences. Use with: other QR* codes for mystic traditions and practices in different religions

QRVL.label: Religion: death and dying
QRVL.notes: Use for: works that explore death and associated religious and spiritual beliefs, including ceremonies around death, grief, veneration of the dead, ancestor worship, the afterlife, spiritual near-death experiences, etc

QRVP.label: Religious life and practice
QRVP.notes: Also class here: nature of faith and religious belief, confession or statements of faith. Use for: general works, works that deal with religious faith or beliefs as part of everyday life, living by the tenets of a belief or faith system on a day to day basis, practices associated with religious creeds, or works about aspects of religious life, practices, beliefs in different spiritual traditions. Use with: QRVX for accounts by individuals about their own faith or personal beliefs in their religion, etc

QRVP1.label: Pilgrimage
QRVP1.notes: Also class here: Pilgrims. Use for: the act of pilgrimage, pilgrim routes and sites or accounts by pilgrims. Use with: PLACE1* Qualifiers for sites or routes associated with particular pilgrimages

QRVP2.label: Religious Festivals
QRVP2.notes: Use with: other QR* codes to denote religion and 5HP* values from INTEREST 5* Qualifiers as appropriate

QRVP5.label: Religious counselling
QRVP5.notes: Also class here: pastoral care, faith-based counsel, religious guidance, faith-based emotional, social and spiritual support, etc

QRVP7.label: Religious aspects of sexuality, gender and relationships
QRVP7.notes: Use for: works about religious teaching on, or attitudes towards, sex and relationships including marriage, family life, gender roles, sexual orientation, sexuality, gender identity, celibacy, sexual abstinence, gender and sex equality, or the role of women in the clergy and religious authorities, or works reinterpreting patriarchal (male-dominated) imagery and language about God, studying images of women in the religions’ sacred texts, and matriarchal religion, etc. Use with: other QR* codes and codes from J* for particular topics, such as, JBSF1 for religion and attitudes to women, JBSJ for religion and LGBTQ+ topics, JHBK for religion and relationships or family, JBSF3 for feminist theology or impetrations of religion, etc

QRVQ.label: Religious sites / Holy or sacred places
QRVQ.notes: Also class here: sacred spaces, sacred grounds, holy cities, sanctuaries, shrines, altars, places of worship, natural sites or physical features, such as mountains or rivers associated with a sacred tradition, religious buildings or structures, etc. Use for: general works that look at places or locations associated with religious traditions or beliefs, or works that examine particular sacred places, sites or locations from a religious or spiritual perspective. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers as appropriate, with QRVP1 for sites of pilgrimages and other QR* codes as appropriate

QRVS1.label: Religious and spiritual figures
QRVS1.notes: Also class here: religious or spiritual leaders and influential or inspirational figures such as saints, gurus, mystics, prophets, theologians, hermits, martyrs, venerated persons, popes, etc

QRVS2.label: Religious social and pastoral thought and activity
QRVS2.notes: Also class here: almsgiving, charity, Sadaqah, Zakat, Dāna, Tzedakah, Agape, Diaconia, Caritas, Charity as a Christian virtue, works or acts of mercy. Use for: works about concepts of almsgiving, charity or similar concepts in different religions, religious practices or spiritual traditions, or notions and discussion on benevolence, compassion, generosity in religious practices

QRVS3.label: Religious ministry and clergy
QRVS3.notes: Also class here: ministers, clerics, priests, pastors, bishops, popes, rabbis, hazzans, imams, muftis, mullahs etc. Use for: works about aspects of the work of people who have specific roles in a religion, or practical works aimed at clergy about carrying out their role

QRVS4.label: Religious mission and Religious Conversion
QRVS4.notes: Also class here: missionaries, evangelism. Use for: works on or about the concept of mission, or works about religious conversion in any form

QRVX.label: Personal religious testimony and popular inspirational works
QRVX.notes: Also class here: personal narratives about peoples beliefs or faith, sacred stories by individuals, stories that witness to personal faith or belief or spirituality. Use with: ‘life and practice’ or other QR* codes or the different religions as appropriate

QRY.label: Alternative belief systems and spiritual worldviews
QRY.notes: Also class here: new religious movements, new religions, alternative spirituality, the Goddess movement or worship, Neopaganism, New Thought movement, Pantheism, Pandeism, Contemporary paganism, Pagan studies, Modern Pagan movements, Neodruidism or Druidry, Rodnovery, Slavic Native Faith, Polytheistic reconstructionism. Prefer: VX* codes for more popular approaches

QRYA.label: Humanist and secular alternatives to religion
QRYA.notes: Also class here: Humanism, secularism, Nontheism, Ignosticism, Ietsism, religious scepticism, irreligion, antireligion, Freethought, Apatheism, antitheism, post-theism, spiritual but not religious, secular humanism or parody religions, such as, the Church of the Flying Spaghetti Monster, Pastafarianism, the Invisible Pink Unicorn

QRYC.label: Eclectic and esoteric religions and belief systems

QRYM.label: Contemporary non-Christian and para-Christian cults and sects
QRYM.notes: Also class here: Scientology, apocalyptic cults, etc

QRYX.label: Occult studies / Supernatural studies
QRYX.notes: Also class here: studies of Western esotericism, Western mystery tradition. Use for: serious and academic works about esoteric supernatural beliefs and practices which generally fall outside the scope of organized religion and science, encompassing phenomena involving otherworldly agency, such as magic and mysticism and their varied spells, or works about supernatural ideas

QRYX2.label: Magic, alchemy and hermetic thought
QRYX2.notes: Also class here: Hermeticism, hermetic Qabalah, Rosicrucianism, alchemists, users of magic, ideas of magic use in different historical periods or in different belief systems. Use with: PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate, as well as other subject codes to indicate context, for example NH* codes for historical studies

QRYX5.label: Witchcraft / Witches
QRYX5.notes: Use for: studies of both contemporary and historical witchcraft or witches, the associated practices, those who practised it, societal attitudes towards witches and witchcraft, Witchcraft as a spirituality, etc. Use with: PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate, as well as other subject codes to indicate context, for example NHTX for the historical persecution of witches, witch trials, witch purges, the European Witch craze, with J* or L* codes for modern witch-hunts, witchcraft accusations, etc. Prefer: VXWT for more popular approaches

QRYX9.label: Satanism / demonology
QRYX9.notes: Use for: works about ideological and philosophical beliefs based on interpretations of Satan, on satanic cults, the Church of Satan, the Satanic Temple, Modern Satanism, Compassionate Satanism, LaVeyan satanism, Theistic satanism, Religious satanism, Spiritual satanism, Traditional satanism or other alternative religious movements that include Satan, or works that look at studies of demons or beliefs about demons in different religious traditions. Use with: other QR* codes as appropriate, for example with QRYA for works about Satanism as an alternative to organised religions

R.label: Earth Sciences, Geography, Environment, Planning
R.notes: Use all R* codes for: academic, technical, specialist and general adult titles. DO NOT USE: code ‘R’ itself, but select specific categories from section R*. Use all R* codes with: other subject categories and qualifiers where appropriate, in particular PLACE 1* Qualifiers

RB.label: Earth sciences
RB.notes: Use all RB* codes for: academic, specialist and professional level works. Prefer: WN* codes for the general reader

RBC.label: Volcanology and seismology
RBC.notes: Use for: works about earthquakes, volcanoes, etc from an earth sciences perspective

RBGD.label: Geomorphology and geological surface processes
RBGD.notes: Also class here: erosion, deposition, glaciology, fluvial and aeolian processes, etc

RBGF.label: Historical geology and palaeogeology
RBGF.notes: Also class here: plate tectonics, continental drift, past supercontinents, such as Pangaea, Gondwana, Laurasia, the geological history of the Earth, etc

RBGL.label: Economic geology
RBGL.notes: Also class here: petroleum and mining geology

RBKF.label: Limnology (inland waters)
RBKF.notes: Also class here: rivers, lakes (including saline lakes), etc

RBP.label: Meteorology and climatology
RBP.notes: Also class here: Atmospheric sciences, terrestrial aeronomy. Use for: general works on atmospheric phenomenon

RBPC.label: Climatology and climate modelling
RBPC.notes: Also class here: palaeoclimatology, climate forecasting, climate science, climate variability, mechanisms of climate changes, modern climate change, climate models, climatological processes, climate classification, urban climatology

RBPM.label: Meteorology
RBPM.notes: Also class here: meteorological phenomena, short term weather systems, nephology (study of clouds), weather forecasting, marine and other specialist weather forecasting, aviation and maritime meteorology, meteorological instrumentation, micrometeorology, mesoscale meteorology, synoptic scale meteorology, global scale meteorology, hydrometeorology, environmental meteorology, agricultural meteorology, surface weather analysis, weather maps or charts

RBX.label: Palaeontology
RBX.notes: Also class here: study of fossils, the study of ancient life, Vertebrate palaeontology, Invertebrate palaeontology, Palaeobotany, Palynology, Micropaleontology, Paleoecology, Biostratigraphy. Use for: Palaeontology and all its specialities. Use with: other subject codes for specialist domains

RG.label: Geography
RG.notes: Use all RG* codes with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers as appropriate

RGB.label: Physical geography and topography
RGB.notes: Use all RGB* codes with: other subject codes when works are about particular types of landscape or topography, for example with WN* or WT* codes

RGBC.label: Plains and grasslands
RGBC.notes: Also class here: steppes, pampas, shrubland, scrubland

RGBF.label: Wetlands, swamps, fens
RGBF.notes: Also class here: marshes and marshland, bogs and bogland, peat bogs, peatlands, mires and quagmires, freshwater swamps, fens and fenlands, wetland restoration

RGBP.label: Coasts and Coastlines
RGBP.notes: Also class here: deltas, estuaries, fjords, beaches, spits, shorelines, cliffs, coastal erosion, bays, coasts, littoral zones, nearshore, coastal regions, coastal routes, seashores, etc

RGBP1.label: Coastal wetlands / tidal flats / mudflats
RGBP1.notes: Also class here: salt marsh, tidal marshes, saltwater swamps, tidal wetlands

RGBQ.label: Islands
RGBQ.notes: Also class here: isles, cays, archipelagos

RGBS.label: Mountains and uplands
RGBS.notes: Also class here: mountain ranges or chains, upland plateaux, highlands, hills, moorlands and heathlands

RGCG.label: Population and migration geography
RGCG.notes: Use with: N* codes or PSXE for works about early human migrations, palaeolithic migration, proto-historical and early historical migrations, pre-modern human migration, etc

RGV.label: Cartography, map-making and projections
RGV.notes: Also class here: works about map-reading or using maps, different types of map projections, types of cartography. Use for: books about maps and mapping but not the maps themselves

RGW.label: Geographical information systems, geodata and remote sensing
RGW.notes: Also class here: geomatics, quantitative and qualitative methods, geostatistics, spatial analysis, GPS, geographic data and information, geographic information science, geoinformatics, geovisualization, geodesy, photogrammetry, etc

RGXB.label: World / regional atlases or maps
RGXB.notes: Also class here: globes and small scale global or continental maps, national and regional atlases or maps, small scale regional maps, specialised or thematic atlases with a global or regional scope. Use with: 1* PLACE qualifiers and with other R* codes for particular types of map, for example RGCP for political / administrative maps or atlases, with other RGC* codes for subjects like economic or resource maps , with RGB for physical or topographical maps, with RBK for a world atlas of water resources, with QRP for an atlas of Islam, etc

RGXH.label: Topographic / thematic / specialist maps
RGXH.notes: Use for: all types of specialist / topographical and other large scale maps or charts, including those produced by national mapping agencies, in map series and scale series. Use with: another code indicating specific subject or application where appropriate, for example, with RBG* for geological, mineral deposit, soil maps, etc, RBP* for climate maps, GPH, RGW or UYZF for thematic maps that present data or geovisualization maps, JHBD for demographics maps, MBN for public health maps, RP* for planning maps, etc and with the most appropriate 1*PLACE Qualifier

RGXM.label: Naval, nautical and marine charts
RGXM.notes: Also class here: maritime charts, navigational charts, tide tables, tidal stream atlases. Use for: detailed charts, maps or atlases of inland waterways, coastal waters and maritime shipping routes, charts or maps for sailors or seafarers. Use with: 1* PLACE qualifiers

RNA.label: Environmentalist thought and ideology
RNA.notes: Also class here: ecocentrism, technocentrism, deep ecology, ecofeminism, environmentalism, anthropocentric or human-centred philosophies, biocentric or life-centred schools of thought, Apocalyptic environmentalism, Emancipatory environmentalism, Social ecology, philosophies around the rights of animals

RNC.label: Applied ecology
RNC.notes: Use for: works taking a wide-ranging or ‘issues’-based approach

RNCB.label: Biodiversity / Ecosystems
RNCB.notes: Also class here: General studies of biodiversity, of ecosystems. Use with: RNKH* for works on Biodiversity loss, Biodiversity crisis, Biodiversity or Ecosystem collapse, Mass extinctions

RND.label: Environmental policy and protocols
RND.notes: Use with: JPQB or JPRB codes as appropriate

RNF.label: Environmental management
RNF.notes: Also class here: Natural resource management, stewardship of the environment and nature. Use for: works that look at the management of all natural resources, such as air, land, water, soil, plants and animals together. Use with: code from RBK* or RGB* to indicate specific environment or habitat

RNFD.label: Drought and water supply
RNFD.notes: Also class here: Soil degradation, surface runoff, erosion, irrigation, water poverty, water wars or conflicts, flooding, aquatic pollution, stormwater, water resources, access to water, water shortages, water crisis, water stress, sustainable water cycles

RNH.label: Waste management
RNH.notes: Also class here: recycling, biodegradability, landfill, incineration of waste, plastic waste management, food and bio-waste management, commercial and domestic waste, waste linked to overconsumption, etc. Use with: other subject codes for works about waste management in specific sectors, such as managing fast fashion and textile waste, technology and electronic waste, industrial and commercial waste management

RNK.label: Conservation of the environment
RNK.notes: Also class here: countryside management, environmental preservation, biospheres, closed ecological systems, seed banks and human-curated repositories of seeds, zoological parks, works about conservation projects or structures. Use with: RBK* or RGB* codes to indicate specific types of environment or habitat

RNKH.label: Conservation of wildlife and habitats
RNKH.notes: Also class here: conservation biology, preservation of ecosystems, wilderness areas, wildlands or other natural environments, trans-national, national or regional parks, marine conservation areas, protected landscapes, designated wilderness or conservation areas, debates about conservation or preservation versus human uses or exploitation, etc

RNKH1.label: Endangered species and extinction of species
RNKH1.notes: Also class here: works about biodiversity collapse

RNP.label: Pollution and threats to the environment
RNP.notes: Also class here: plastic waste, air pollution, water pollution, over-consumption, etc. Use with: other codes for works on pollution or environmental threats from specific sectors, such as textile and fashion pollution, pollution from transport and industry, pollution from technology and electronics, from leisure and tourism, from agriculture and food industry, etc

RNPG.label: Climate change
RNPG.notes: Also class here: global warming, greenhouse effect, ozone depletion, the climate emergency, emissions of greenhouse gases, human impact on Earths weather patterns. Use for: works that examine climate change, its effects and possible actions to limit or mitigate the consequences, geoengineering or climate engineering aspects of climate change, mitigation strategies, climate change adaptation. Use with: other codes for works examining aspects of climate change linked to other topics, such as politics, economics, technology, fiction, etc

RNQ.label: Nuclear issues
RNQ.notes: Also class here: nuclear disasters, radioactive incidents, nuclear accidents, disposal of radioactive waste

RNR.label: Natural disasters
RNR.notes: Also class here: Earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, floods, mudslides, hurricanes and cyclones, tornadoes, tsunamis, droughts, wildfires, etc

RNT.label: Social impact of environmental issues
RNT.notes: Also class here: works on the consequences on people and society of environmental issues (such as extreme weather events, droughts, heatwaves, wildfires, flooding, sea level rises, climate change, pollution events, loss of biodiversity, biodiversity collapse, deforestation, desertification) and the impacts (such as mass migration, health effects, soil erosion, loss of agricultural land, food security, hunger, famine, water security, livelihood security, poverty and precarity, global economic inequality, civic unrest, conflict, loss of homes, destruction of infrastructure, threats to urban areas, loss of cultural identity, etc)

RNU.label: Sustainability
RNU.notes: Also class here: Sustainable or regenerative approaches to the environment, sustainable development. Use with: other subject categories to indicate works on sustainability in particular areas

RP.label: Regional and area planning

RPC.label: Urban and municipal planning and policy

RPG.label: Rural planning and policy

S.label: Sports and Active outdoor recreation
S.notes: Use all S* codes for: general adult and specialist titles. Use all S* codes with: other subject categories and qualifiers where appropriate, in particular PLACE 1* Qualifiers, for example with WT* for adventure holidays, or VFM for a sport as part of a fitness regime

SCB.label: Sporting events and management
SCB.notes: Use all SCB* codes with: other S* codes denoting a specific sport as appropriate

SCBC.label: World Cups and World championships
SCBC.notes: Use with: other S* codes to indicate which type of sport this applies to

SCG.label: Sports training and coaching
SCG.notes: Also class here: advice on nutrition and diet, strength and conditioning training, officiating sports events, works for sports professionals, trainers, instructors or coaches, skills acquisition in sports, or advice for improving performance or fitness of athletes. Use with: VFM* or WB* codes as appropriate

SCGF.label: Sport science, physical education
SCGF.notes: Also class here: exercise physiology or kinesiology for sports and fitness professionals, movement education

SF.label: Ball sports / ball games
SF.notes: Also class here: Basque Pelota, jai alai, croquet, ulama, hand-pelota, Xare, rounders, Pesäpallo. Use for: ball games that do not have their own code as well as general works

SFG.label: Floorball and other hockey variants
SFG.notes: Also class here: salibandy, innebandy, unihockey, streetbandy, Swiss floorball, wheelchair floorball, rink or roller hockey, street hockey, inline hockey, floor hockey, bandy

SFJ.label: Field hockey

SFQ.label: Handball and its variants
SFQ.notes: Also class here: Gaelic handball, American Handball, Australian handball, Valencian pilota, Pelota mixteca

SFT.label: Racket games
SFT.notes: Also class here: Real tennis, Padel, paddleball, paddle tennis, frontenis. Use for: racket or racquet games and sports that do not have their own code as well as general works

SFV.label: Bowls, bowling, petanque
SFV.notes: Also class here: boules, bocce, lawn bowls, Pin bowling

SHBM.label: Multidiscipline sports
SHBM.notes: Also class here: triathlon, pentathlon, heptathlon, etc

SHG.label: Gymnastics
SHG.notes: Also class here: baton twirling, rhythmic gymnastics, color guard, cheerleading, tumbling, vault, bars, beams, rings, trampoline, pole sports, etc. Prefer: ATXC for acrobatics and aerial disciplines as performance

SKL.label: Riding, showjumping and horsemanship
SKL.notes: Also class here: eventing, dressage etc

SMC.label: Air sports and recreations
SMC.notes: Also class here: ballooning, paragliding, skydiving, gliding, etc

SMF.label: Motor sports
SMF.notes: Also class here: karting, go-karts, truck racing, any motorised sports not listed below

SMFA.label: Car racing
SMFA.notes: Also class here: Formula 1, Grand Prix, Indianapolis 500, 24 Hours at Le Mans, etc

SMFF.label: Stock car and hot rod racing
SMFF.notes: Also class here: NASCAR, Daytona 500, drag racing, etc

SMFK.label: Motorcycle racing
SMFK.notes: Also class here: road and track motorcycle racing; TT, Speedway, etc

SMQ.label: Cycle racing
SMQ.notes: Also class here: road and velodrome (track) cycling racing; Tour de France, etc

SP.label: Water sports and recreations

SPCD.label: Diving
SPCD.notes: Also class here: platform and springboard diving, etc

SPCS.label: Swimming
SPCS.notes: Also class here: open water, pool swimming and wild swimming

SPG.label: Surfing, windsurfing, water skiing
SPG.notes: Also class here: Water based board sports, surfboarding, sailboarding, boardsailing, wind foiling, kiteboarding, kitesurfing, wing foiling, wing surfing, foil boards, wakeboarding, surfboarding, bodyboarding, bodysurfing, river boarding

SPNG.label: Sailing / yachting
SPNG.notes: Also class here: learning to sail, knots, splices and rope work for sailors, certification, navigation skills, seamanship, racing yachts, cruising yachts and sailboats, small yachts, near-shore yachts, offshore yachts etc. Use with: WTHX for guides to cruising on a sailboat or yachts, or WGGB for works that are about the boats themselves or WGGP for works about official certification or licences for sailing

SPNK.label: Canoeing, kayaking and other paddle sports
SPNK.notes: Also class here: rafting, paddle boarding, stand-up paddleboarding, white water and wild water canoeing, slalom, Canadian canoes, sea kayaking, Dragon boating

SPNL.label: Rowing and sculling
SPNL.notes: Also class here: Crew, sweep rowing, coastal and ocean rowing

SRM.label: Martial arts
SRM.notes: Also class here: Krav Maga, Historical European martial arts, (HEMA or WMA), etc. Use for: general works or for martial arts that do not have their own code

SRMN1.label: Tai Chi
SRMN1.notes: Use with: VFMG for titles specifically about fitness aspects, or VXH for health aspects

SRMN2.label: Qigong
SRMN2.notes: Use with: VFMG for titles specifically about fitness aspects, or VXH for health aspects

ST.label: Winter sports / activities
ST.notes: Use for: general works on sports or activities that take place in the winter, on snow or ice. Use with: WT* for guides to places to do winter activities, use with other SZ* codes for works about a particular activity in winter, for example hiking or camping or mountaineering in winter and 5HRD as appropriate

STAT.label: Freestyle skiing
STAT.notes: Also class here: free skiing, jibbing, ski acrobatics, aerial skiing, mogul skiing, ski ballet, acroski, ski cross, half-pipe skiing, slopestyle

STL.label: Sledding
STL.notes: Also class here: luge, skeleton and bobsledding

STS.label: Snowshoeing
STS.notes: Also class here: Snowshoes, hiking on snow. Use with: WTHE or WTHW and 1* PLACE qualifiers for snowshoe trails, guides to snowshoeing in particular areas, and with STAN1 for guides to both cross-country skiing and snowshoeing

SVB.label: Falconry and hawking
SVB.notes: Also class here: trained birds of prey

SVFS.label: Sea fishing
SVFS.notes: Also class here: big game fishing

SVH.label: Hunting or shooting animals and game

SVHH.label: Professional qualifications for hunting / shooting
SVHH.notes: Use for: works for licences, exams, certificates, vocational courses linked to hunting or shooting

SVS.label: Small firearms, guns and other equipment

SXE.label: eSports / Professional video gaming
SXE.notes: Use for: competitions, usually professional, using video games

SXQ.label: Extreme sports
SXQ.notes: Also class here: bungee jumping, etc

SZ.label: Active outdoor pursuits and activities
SZ.notes: Also class here: canyoning, free running and parkour, obstacle courses, general outdoor games and activities, outdoor family or group activities, or any work about an active outdoor pursuit that does not have a more precise code. Use all SZ* codes for: indoor analogues or training for outdoor activities. Use all SZ* codes with: WTH* codes for guidebooks to places to do the particular activity, WTR* for maps linked to a particular activity, VFM* for fitness aspects, with ST* for winter sports versions, or 5HR* codes for seasonal guides to a particular activity

SZC.label: Walking, hiking, trekking
SZC.notes: Also class here: Hillwalking, backpacking, Nordic walking, fell walking, rambling, scrambling. Use for: any works about walking including walking for recreation, for fitness or as a specialised outdoor activity. Use with: PLACE 1* qualifiers and WTHE for general guidebooks for walkers in an area or WTHW for guidebooks to specific or named walking, hiking or trekking routes or trails, or WTRM for maps

SZD.label: Cycling: general and touring
SZD.notes: Use with: WTHE for general guidebooks for cyclists or WTHW for guidebooks to specific cycling routes

SZE.label: Running and jogging
SZE.notes: Also class here: Trail and Mountain running, running for fitness, fell or hill running. Use with: WTH* codes and PLACE 1* qualifiers for guidebooks for runners in specific areas

SZG.label: Climbing and mountaineering
SZG.notes: Also class here: Indoor wall, Via ferrata, bouldering, free, rock, rope, solo and ice climbing, abseiling, belaying. Use with: WTH* codes and PLACE 1* qualifiers for guidebooks for climbers or climbing routes

SZK.label: Orienteering
SZK.notes: Also class here: Foot orienteering, trail orienteering, map and compass skills for orienteering. SZN.label: Caving and potholing
SZN.notes: Also class here: Spelunking and speleology. Use with: WTHE and PLACE 1* qualifiers for guidebooks to specific caving sites

SZR.label: Camping
SZR.notes: Also class here: all forms of camping, survival camping, glamping, backpacking, wild camping. Use with: WTHH1 and PLACE 1* qualifiers for guidebooks to camping in specific areas

SZV.label: Outdoor survival skills
SZV.notes: Also class here: bushcraft, woodcraft (skills for living in the open air, close to nature), navigation skills

T.label: Technology, Engineering, Agriculture, Industrial processes
T.notes: Also class here: associated skills, trades and professions. Use all T* codes for: academic, technical, specialist and general adult titles. DO NOT USE: code ‘T’ itself, but select specific categories from section T*. Use all T* codes with: other subject categories and qualifiers where appropriate, in particular EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* qualifiers for vocational, professional or apprenticeship style education titles, 4TM for revision and study guides, 4CP for vocational or professional qualifications, 4Z* for specific national qualifications

TBG.label: Engineering graphics and draughting / technical drawing
TBG.notes: Use for: computer aided draughting. Use with: other codes such as architecture, design or engineering as appropriate

TBN.label: Nanotechnology
TBN.notes: Use with: other T* codes for applications of nanotechnology in different fields, with M* codes for applications in medical technology, P* codes for applications in sciences

TCB.label: Biotechnology
TCB.notes: Also class here: biological engineering, bio-engineering, biomanufacturing, biofabrication. Use with: other M*, P* or T* codes for use of biotechnologies in different areas

TCBG.label: Genetic engineering
TCBG.notes: Also class here: cloning; stem cell technology, genome editing, gene editing, genetic modification

TDC.label: Industrial chemistry and chemical engineering
TDC.notes: Also class here: technology of detergents, rubber, biocides etc

TDCJ.label: Dyestuffs, pigments and paint technology
TDCJ.notes: Also class here: cosmetics technology, colour chemistry

TDCP.label: Plastics and polymers
TDCP.notes: Use for: all aspects of the professional manufacturing of plastics

TDCT.label: Food and beverage technology
TDCT.notes: Also class here: food sciences, technology linked to brewing and distilling, nutritional science, nutraceuticals and food supplement technologies

TDCT1.label: Food and beverage safety
TDCT1.notes: Also class here: food quality, impact of food regulation and policy

TDCT2.label: Food and beverage processing and engineering
TDCT2.notes: Also class here: food processing by ingredient

TDP.label: Other manufacturing technologies
TDP.notes: Use for: manufacturing processes or technologies that do not have their own code

TDPF.label: Textiles and fibres
TDPF.notes: Also class here: fibre processing, spinning and weaving, leatherworking. Use for: technical and vocational works aimed at professionals or students in textile manufacture and related sectors, including both human-made and natural materials

TDPF1.label: Apparel and fashion: technology and techniques
TDPF1.notes: Also class here: patternmaking, pattern cutting, tailoring, shoemaking, millinery, bagmaking. Use for: technical and vocational works aimed at professionals or students in the garment, fashion or related sectors including accessories

TDPJ.label: Timber and wood processing
TDPJ.notes: Use for: all aspects of the professional processing of wood and wood products

TDPJ1.label: Paper and pulp manufacture and processing

TGH.label: Precision engineering and manufacturing
TGH.notes: Use for: works on the design, engineering and manufacture of scientific, technical, medical, chemical and optical devices, precision tools and equipment

TGMD.label: Engineering: Mechanics of solids
TGMD.notes: Also class here: dynamics, vibration, stress, fracture etc

TGMF.label: Engineering: Mechanics of fluids
TGMF.notes: Also class here: flow, turbulence, rheology etc. Use for: the application of fluid dynamics in technology

TGMM.label: Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

TGMP.label: Engineering applications of polymers and composites
TGMP.notes: Also class here: Engineering applications of carbon materials

TGMS.label: Engineering applications of surface coatings and films

TGMT.label: Testing of materials
TGMT.notes: Use for: destructive and non-destructive testing

TGX.label: Engineering skills and trades
TGX.notes: Also class here: tool-making, welding, machinist, metalwork skills and trades etc

THN.label: Heat transfer processes
THN.notes: Also class here: refrigeration, industrial air conditioning, heat pumps

THV.label: Alternative and renewable energy sources and technology
THV.notes: Also class here: tidal and wave energy, osmotic power, marine current power, marine energy technologies, ocean thermal energy, air source heat pump technologies, salinity gradient technology

THVB.label: Biofuels
THVB.notes: Also class here: energy from biomass, biogas

THVG.label: Geothermal energy and power
THVG.notes: Also class here: ground source heat pump technology

THVH.label: Hydropower / waterpower
THVH.notes: Also class here: hydroelectricity and hydropower, dams, watermills, waterwheels

THVS.label: Solar power
THVS.notes: Also class here: solar energy, solar panels, photovoltaic panels, solar energy technologies, solar power systems, floating solar energy technologies

THVW.label: Wind power
THVW.notes: Also class here: windmills, wind farms, wind turbines, onshore and offshore wind power and energy, wind energy technologies, wind power systems

THY.label: Energy, power generation, distribution and storage
THY.notes: Also class here: power networks and plants; power utilisation and applications; energy conversion and storage, power distribution grids and networks, power cables, distribution pipelines, storage facilities. Use with: other TH* codes for storage, distribution etc in different sectors

THYB.label: Battery technology / fuel cell technology
THYB.notes: Also class here: battery storage technology, battery engineering

TJ.label: Electronics and communications engineering
TJ.notes: Use all TJ* codes with: 4TM for revision and study guides, 4CP for vocational or professional qualifications, 4Z* for specific national qualifications

TJD.label: Haptic and other tactile technologies
TJD.notes: Also class here: kinaesthetic communication, 3D touch, active touch sensing technology, tactile surfaces on flat screens. Use for: general works on haptics in new technologies. Use with: other subject codes for uses in specific area

TJFD.label: Electronic devices and materials
TJFD.notes: Also class here: microprocessors, chips, transistors, semi-conductors, super-conductors etc

TJFM1.label: Robotics
TJFM1.notes: Also class here: works on the design, construction, operation and use of different types of robots, the applications of robotic and automation technologies in different areas

TJKH.label: Signal processing
TJKH.notes: Also class here: analogue, continuous time, discrete time, nonlinear and statistical signal processing

TJKS.label: Satellite communication technology
TJKS.notes: Also class here: radionavigation-satellite service, satellite navigation, global navigation satellite systems, fixed or mobile satellite systems, satellite transponders, works on satellite communications in different sectors, such as telephony, television, internet access, data collection, military, radio communications etc

TN.label: Civil engineering, surveying and building
TN.notes: Use all TN* codes with: 4TM for revision and study guides, 4CP for vocational or professional qualifications, 4Z* for specific national qualifications

TNCC.label: Soil and rock mechanics
TNCC.notes: Also class here: geotechnical engineering, geotechnics, foundation engineering, ground engineering

TNF.label: Hydraulic engineering
TNF.notes: Also class here: engineering of dams, reservoirs, harbours etc; also land reclamation and drainage

TNFD.notes: Use for: works on the design, building and maintenance of coastal structures, or integrated coastal zone management, or engineering topics relating to port development, coastal defence, protection against sea-level rises, coastal flooding, land reclamation, coastal dredging, etc

TNKD.label: Building and construction regulations, rules and codes
TNKD.notes: Use for: works that explain all the rules and regulations for building construction or design, rules for specific elements of building work, restoration, repair etc, often works aimed at professionals, but not specifically for legal professionals. TNKX.label: Conservation of buildings and building materials
TNKX.notes: Use for: practical and technical guides to the preservation or restoration of buildings and structures, including historic buildings and the associated skills and trades

TNT.label: Building skills and trades

TNTB.label: Masonry, bricklaying, plastering, tiling, cementing skills and techniques
TNTB.notes: Use with: 4CP* EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE qualifiers if appropriate

TNTC.label: Carpentry and joinery skills and techniques
TNTC.notes: Use with: 4CP* EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE qualifiers if appropriate

TNTP.label: Plumbing skills and techniques
TNTP.notes: Also class here: skills for gas installation, manuals for plumbers. Use with: 4CP* EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE qualifiers if appropriate

TNTR.label: Roofing skills and techniques
TNTR.notes: Use with: 4CP* EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE qualifiers if appropriate

TQ.label: Environmental science, engineering and technology
TQ.notes: Use all TQ* codes for: technical and practical aspects of environment, pollution, waste disposal, etc. Prefer: PNC for study and research

TQP.label: Greenhouse gas emissions technologies
TQP.notes: Also class here: works about methods and technologies associated with carbon dioxide removal (CDR), negative emissions technology (NET), greenhouse gas removal (GGR), carbon capture and storage (CCS), carbon sequestration, carbon capture and utilization, carbon separation technologies, decarbonisation, methane capture technologies, nitrous oxide removal

TQSR.label: Waste treatment and disposal
TQSR.notes: Also class here: sewage and hazardous waste disposal

TQSW.label: Water supply and treatment
TQSW.notes: Also class here: water purification and desalination, water resource management and policy, drinking water quality, water reuse, management of greywater and wastewater, integrated urban water management, water-sensitive urban design, use of reclaimed and treated water, use of rainwater, rainwater harvesting, water cycle management, watercourses and management of water supply infrastructure, aqueducts, pipelines. Use for: works that look at planning, developing, distributing and managing the optimum use of water resources

TRP.label: Aerospace and aviation technology
TRP.notes: Also class here: unmanned aerial vehicles and drone technology, aeronautical and aerospace engineering, aircraft avionics

TRPS.label: Aviation skills and piloting
TRPS.notes: Also class here: learning to fly, practical manuals, pilot’s licence

TRT.label: Intelligent and automated transport system technology
TRT.notes: Also class here: autonomous vehicle technology, vehicular automation, smart mass transit, self-driving, unmanned or uncrewed vehicle technology, advanced driver-assistance systems, vehicle telematics. Use with: other TR* codes for particular modes of transport

TRV.label: Electric vehicles / alternative fuel vehicles
TRV.notes: Also class here: human–electric hybrid vehicle, hybrid electric vehicle, hydrogen vehicle, fuel cell vehicles, new vehicle technologies, ammonia as a fuel, liquefied natural gas (LNG) fuelled vehicles. Use for: any technology of powering an engine that does not involve solely petroleum fuels. Use with: other TR* codes for particular modes of transport, for example TRL* for alternative marine fuels for shipping

TTA.label: Acoustic and sound engineering
TTA.notes: Also class here: sound design techniques, sound and audio effects, audio engineering, recording engineer

TTB.label: Applied optics
TTB.notes: Also class here: applied photonics, optoelectronics, optomechanics, optical computing or other uses of optics in technology

TTDS.label: Astronautics
TTDS.notes: Also class here: technical aspects of space exploration e.g. spacecraft design and technology

TTDX.label: Space exploration
TTDX.notes: Also class here: manned and unmanned space missions and programs, Apollo, Vostok, Sputnik, Voyager etc

TTG.label: Mechatronics
TTG.notes: Also class here: interdisciplinary engineering works that that focus on the integration of combinations of mechanical, electrical, electronics, robotics, computer science and information technology systems and principles

TTS.label: Marine engineering
TTS.notes: Also class here: offshore engineering and construction, sonar, ocean engineering or nautical engineering, maritime engineering etc. Use for: works on the engineering of marine vessels, or other ocean systems and structures. Use with: THVW for offshore wind engineering, THFP for oil rigs, offshore drilling, etc

TTVC2.label: Catering and food preparation skills and trades
TTVC2.notes: Use for: any work aimed at professionals in the food and drinks industries

TTVH.label: Hairdressing, salon and beauty therapy skills
TTVH.notes: Also class here: professional makeup, cosmetology, barbering, hair design and haircare, skin care, spa, massage and body therapy, manicures, pedicures and any work aimed at professionals in these industries. Use with: 4CP* and other EDUCATIONAL 4* qualifiers for vocational education titles as appropriate, and with YPWC5 for works aimed at secondary level education

TTVR.label: Traditional trades, crafts and skills
TTVR.notes: Also class here: blacksmithing, thatching, dry stone walling, carpentry and cabinetry, musical instrument making etc. Use for: technical, vocational or professional works that cover these pre-industrial, low technology, artisanal, often rural, crafts. Prefer: WF* for more amateur approaches

TTVS.label: Security, safety and protection skills / professions
TTVS.notes: Use for: professional / vocational works for security and safety professionals, personal protection and related skills

TTVT.label: Caretakers, janitors, housekeepers, cleaners and related skills
TTVT.notes: Use for: vocational works for professionals looking after buildings, domestic workers, caretaking, custodian skills

TTW.label: Assistive technology
TTW.notes: Also class here: Adaptive technology, use of technology to assist and enable people with disabilities or impairments to live independent lives

TV.label: Agriculture and farming
TV.notes: Use for: academic, practical or vocational titles about the practice and techniques of agriculture, farming, food production and rural land use and associated occupations, agricultural workers, land-based studies, industrial agriculture, intensive farming, subsistence agriculture, etc. Use all TV* codes with: other T* or U* codes for works about use of new technologies in agriculture, agriculture as a business, diversification of agriculture units, such as agritourism or agrotourism, and with 4TM for revision and study guides, 4CP for vocational or professional qualifications, 4Z* for specific national qualifications

TVB.label: Agricultural science
TVB.notes: Also class here: agroecosystems, agroecology, Agritech, agricultural biotechnology. Use for: works that look at the scientific study of agriculture and associated processes, such as ecological processes applied to agricultural production systems, studies of the relation of agriculture crops and environment, plant breeding. Use with: PST* for works about agricultural botany, with other T* codes for use of technologies in agriculture, for example TCB for Agricultural biotechnology

TVBP.label: Soil science and management
TVBP.notes: Also class here: edaphology, agricultural soil science and environmental soil science, soil health, soil fertility and nutrient management, soil depletion, soil erosion control, soil loss, soil conservation, soil and carbon sequestration, etc

TVBT.label: Agricultural land management
TVBT.notes: Also class here: managed use of rural land, management of agricultural grassland and other types of grazing land used for livestock, mixed land use, managing rural land for agricultural use, degradation of agricultural land and techniques for improvement, fodder production, land rotation, sustainable land management practices, etc. Use with: RGB* codes for particular land types

TVDR.label: Irrigation and water management
TVDR.notes: Use for: works that look at techniques and use of water resources in agriculture and managed rural land use, drainage techniques

TVF.label: Sustainable agriculture

Use for: works that examine sustainable methods of agriculture, food production and rural land use, or look at environmentally-friendly ways of using rural land and producing food, or farming techniques that improve carbon sequestration, etc

TVG.label: Organic farming
TVG.notes: Use for: works that look specifically at the type of farming labelled organic and that usually uses fertilizers of organic origin and techniques such as crop rotation and companion planting, and is often regulated by rules by national or international bodies about what exactly constitutes ‘organic’ agriculture or horticulture. TVH.label: Animal husbandry
TVH.notes: Also class here: animal care, livestock farming and management

TVHE.label: Equine Management
TVHE.notes: Also class here: horse breeding, equine sciences

TVHF.label: Dairy farming
TVHF.notes: Also class here: techniques for milking, dairy cows, goats, sheep, water buffalo, camels or other mammals that are kept for commercial production of milk or of dairy products. Use with: TQSR for dealing with waste

TVHH.label: Apiculture (beekeeping)

TVHP.notes: Also class here: farming of chickens, ducks, geese, turkeys, quails, peafowl, guinea fowl, pheasants, pigeons, game birds, ostrich, etc. Use for: works about the farming or rearing of domesticated birds for their eggs, meat or feathers; or works about techniques, technology, welfare, production, products, diseases, issues associated with farming of birds

TVK.label: Agronomy and crop production
TVK.notes: Also class here: cereals or crop sciences, crop cultivation systems, cropping and intercropping techniques, weed sciences, vegetation management, genetic modification of crops, plant breeding in agriculture, conservation biology of crop plants, precision agriculture in crop management

TVP.label: Pest control / plant diseases
TVP.notes: Also class here: agricultural use of pesticides and herbicides, managing insects and other types of pests, biopesticides, disease resistance in crops

TVQ.label: Tropical agriculture
TVQ.notes: Use for: academic, practical or vocational titles about the practices and techniques of agriculture, farming, food production and rural land use in tropical areas; tropical crops and ecosystems

TVR.label: Forestry and silviculture
TVR.notes: Also class here: arboriculture, tree-planting, tree surgery. Use for: academic, practical or vocational titles about the practices and techniques of creating, managing, using, conserving, and repairing forest and related resources, land management for forests and woodlands, afforestation, reforestation and tree planting techniques, agroforestry, plantation forestry, urban forestry, bamboo forestry, logging practices, clearcutting, seed tree harvests, shelterwood cutting, etc

WBXD2.label: Beers and ciders

WFB.label: Needlework, textile and fabric crafts

WFBQ.label: Quiltmaking, patchwork and appliqué

WFL.label: Bamboo, reed and wicker crafts

WFQ.label: Decorative woodwork

WFS.label: Carving and modelling, moulding and casting

WFT.label: Book and paper crafts
WFT.notes: Also class here: paper-making, bookbinding, greeting card-making, scrapbooking, paper planes, paper models, papercraft, paper cutting, decoupage, papier mâché, paper layering, Jianzhi, Kirigami, papel picado, silhouette, stencils, etc

WFW.label: Flower arranging and floral crafts

WFX.label: Adult colouring, interactive and activity books or kits

WGC.label: Road and motor vehicles: general interest

WGCF.label: Buses, trams and commercial vehicles: general interest
WGCF.notes: Also class here: HGVs, lorries, trucks, vans, coaches, etc

WGCG.label: Construction vehicles and heavy equipment

WGCK.label: Motorcycles: general interest

WGCQ.label: Road and motor vehicles: Camper vans, Recreational vehicles

WGGB.label: Boats

WGGV.label: Boatbuilding and maintenance

WJK.label: Interior design, decor and style guides

WJXF.label: Table settings and arts of the table

WKR.label: Home renovation and extension / self-build

WKU.label: Outdoor and recreational areas: design and maintenance

WMQW.label: Water gardens, pools

WNCS1.label: Sea life and the seashore: general interest

WND.label: The countryside, country life: general interest

WNF.label: Farm and working animals: general interest

WNGK.label: Birds, including cage birds, as pets

WNGR.label: Rabbits and rodents as pets

WNGS.label: Reptiles and amphibians as pets

WNW.label: The Earth: natural history: general interest

WTHF.label: Travel guides: holidays with children / family holidays

WTHG.label: Travel guides: budget travel / independent travel

WTHH.label: Travel guides: hotel and holiday accommodation guides

WTHH1.label: Travel guides: caravan and camp-site guides / camping
