WTHK.label: Travel guides: beaches and coastal areas / islands
WTHK.notes: Also class here: Guides or maps to seaside holidays, coastal resorts, coastlines, islands, etc. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifier codes as appropriate, WTHW for guides to coastal footpaths or trails, WTHX for guides exploring a coast by boat

WTHL.label: Travel guides: cities / towns
WTHL.notes: Also class here: City break guides, guides to walks in a city, tours of a city, thematic guides to a city or town, etc. Use for: guides to specific cities, towns or any urban area. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifier codes as appropriate and other WTH* codes if appropriate

WTHM.label: Travel guides: museums, historic sites, galleries etc
WTHM.notes: Also class here: guides or maps to heritage sites, individual buildings, monuments, culturally significant sites, historic and archaeological sites, interesting landmarks, places of interest, roadside attractions, cultural tourism, heritage tourism, archaeological tourism, places of burial, historic cemeteries, burial grounds, gravesites, graveyards, memorials to the dead, catacombs, tombs, mausoleums, etc. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifier codes as appropriate

WTHN.label: Travel guides: accessible and inclusive tourism
WTHN.notes: Use for: guides or guides to holidays and destinations which focus on accessibility and inclusivity of all people, for example, those travellers with physical or intellectual limitations or disabilities, women travellers, LGBTQ+ travellers, etc. Use with: 5* INTEREST qualifiers as appropriate

WTHR.label: Travel guides: restaurants and cafes
WTHR.notes: Also class here: Inns, bars, pubs, bistros for food / drink. Use for: ‘where to eat / drink’ guides, recommendations of specific establishments

WTHT.label: Travel guides: theme parks and funfairs

WTHV.label: Travel guides: rail travel / railway journeys
WTHV.notes: Also class here: railway timetables for travellers, railway maps, travelling by train, railway journeys, guides to getting around by train, ideas for days out, excursions, or travel by rail, etc

WTHW.label: Travel guides: routes and ways, tracks and trails
WTHW.notes: Also class here: guides or maps to long distance routes, such as footpaths, cycleways, waterways, highways, bridleways, pilgrim routes and trails or other routes meant for walking, hiking, cycling, etc. Use for: guides for walkers, cyclists, horse riders, pilgrims, hikers, trekkers, cross-country skiers, snowshoeing, etc. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifier codes plus subject codes, such as SZ*, where appropriate, for example, with SZD for guides to cycle ways, SZC for footpaths or trails, with WTRM for maps for walkers or maps showing overviews of long-distance routes, QRVP1 for guides to pilgrim routes, etc

WTHX.label: Travel guides: cruises and cruising on water
WTHX.notes: Also class here: guides or maps to commercial or leisure river and sea cruising, guides to cruise ships, to cruise routes, guides to cruising on canals and other waterways, guides for cruising on yachts, or sailboats, Blue-water cruising and coastal cruising, maritime cruising. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifier codes as appropriate, with SPN* codes for guides to specific types of cruising by sailboat or motor boats or with WGGD for guides about the cruise liners, with RGXM for guides to specific areas with detailed marine charts or nautical maps

WTHY.label: Travel guides: road travel / road trips
WTHY.notes: Also class here: guides or maps to travelling by bus or coach. Use for: guides or maps to travel by motorised vehicles, such as car, motorbike, camper van, motorhome, recreational vehicles, RVS, buses, or guides that follow specific roads or routes suitable for motor vehicles, tourist and scenic routes, theme and promoted touring routes for vehicles, tourist highways or byways and holiday routes, guides to getting around using buses, vanlife or van-dwelling trips etc

WTK.label: Language phrasebooks
WTK.notes: Use with: LANGUAGE Qualifier 2* as appropriate

WTL.label: Travel writing
WTL.notes: Also class here: modern and contemporary travel writing, travelogues, published travel journals, travel literature, outdoor literature, travel memoirs. Use for: works that give personal accounts of a place, an area, a country, and often including personal anecdotes or impressions, and may include some history, some contemporary culture and society, some geography; or works where the writer(s) tries to explore the sense of a place, or explores a place through personal accounts of their travels or journeys. Use all WTL* codes with: PLACE 1* Qualifier codes as appropriate

WTLC.label: Classic travel writing
WTLC.notes: Use for: travel writing widely regarded or presented as ‘classic’ and typically, but not necessarily, published and in print for several decades

WTLP.label: Expeditions: popular accounts
WTLP.notes: Also class here: popular accounts of expeditions and exploration

WTM.label: Places and peoples: general and pictorial works
WTM.notes: Use for: illustrated and inspirational travel books, books about places to visit, etc, that are NOT primarily guidebooks. Use with: the most specific PLACE 1* Qualifiers available plus INTEREST 5* qualifier or another subject code when the title has a specialised theme

WTR.label: Travel maps and atlases
WTR.notes: Also class here: any type of map or atlas of places, countries or regions designed for general travel or leisure. Use all WTR* codes with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers and other codes for specific types of travel maps or atlases, for example, use with WTHV for rail travel, with WTHX for cruising maps or atlases aimed at tourists, etc. Prefer: WTR* codes on their own with PLACE qualifiers when the product is just a map of a place with no other speciality or theme

WTRD.label: Road atlases and maps
WTRD.notes: Also class here: Road maps, Touring maps. Use for: Individual maps, or collections of maps in an atlas, specifically designed for travellers using road systems to get around, for example, for motorists, drivers taking long distance routes, or for those touring by car or other motorised transport. Often published in forms that make it easier for users in a vehicle. Use with: WTHY for collections of maps specifically for touring by motorised vehicles

WTRM.label: Travel and Leisure maps
WTRM.notes: Also class here: detailed maps, or collections of maps or atlases, including topographic maps, for walking, hiking, cycling, riding, holidays or any outdoor leisure activities. Use for: all maps, other than city street maps and motorists’ road maps, for general leisure and travel use. Use with: PLACE 1* qualifiers to indicate what area the map covers and if the map is specialised for a particular type of travel , use with relevant WTH* codes, for example, WTHW for maps of long-distance paths, WTHD for maps of wine or food regions or trails, and with SZ* or S* codes for maps for specific outdoor activities, such as SZC for maps specifically for walking, SZD for maps or atlases specifically for cyclists, STA for maps for Skiing

WTRS.label: Street maps and city plans or atlases
WTRS.notes: Also class here: maps and books of maps of cities, towns and streets for general use, street atlases, guides with A to Z guides to streets in an urban area. Use with: other codes , especially WTH* codes for specialised or thematic city maps

WZ.label: Stationery and miscellaneous items
WZ.notes: Also class here: any non-book product that has no particular theme or topic and is clearly content free but still needs to be classified as something. Use all WZ* codes for: products such as stationery and non-book articles that would not be categorised using another subject category as a primary or main subject. Use with: other subject codes as appropriate but WZ* should be the main or principal code if used. NB: Details of formats are conveyed in other product metadata

WZG.label: Gift and novelty books / items
WZG.notes: Use for: novelty merchandise, products or books typically small format and of a decorative, humorous or inspirational nature, often with illustrations and small amounts of text, intended to be given as gifts by the purchaser, usually used for books that do NOT easily fit into other sections and are often displayed at point of sale. Use with: other subject codes as appropriate but WZG should always be the main or principal code. DO NOT USE: for marketing purposes indicating a title would make a good gift (all books make good gifts!)

WZP.label: Miscellaneous non-book items: Games, puzzles and toys
WZP.notes: Also class here: Board games, travel-games, strategy games, jigsaw puzzles, 3-D puzzles classic games, family games, card games, educational games and toys, book related toys, figurines and action figures, soft toys, etc. Use for: any type of non-book game or puzzle sold separately from books. Use with: other codes to indicate the subject or theme of the game or puzzle. NB: Details of formats and types of games are conveyed in other product metadata

WZS.label: Stationery items
WZS.notes: Use for: any printed stationery item, posters, kits, postcard packs, bookmarks, greetings cards, postcards, gift wrap, school supplies, office supplies, etc. Use with: another code indicating subject where possible

WZSD.label: Printed stationery items: Calendars / diaries
WZSD.notes: Also class here: printed agendas, annual planners, academic year diaries and planners. Use with: other codes to indicate the subject or theme of the calendar or diary. NB: Details of formats and types of calendars or diaries are conveyed in other product metadata

WZSJ.label: Printed stationery items: Thematic / guided journals and notebooks
WZSJ.notes: Also class here: creative journals, planners, journals or albums to record information about special events, such as a wedding, a new baby, pregnancy journal, baby record books. Use for: journals that you fill in, which have some pre-printed text or images to inspire what to write or note down, or entries with a prompt or prompts to write about a particular aspect of your life, but are not linked to a particular year. Use with: another secondary code indicating a subject as appropriate, and 5H* qualifiers if for a particular event or holiday

WZSN.label: Blank stationery items
WZSN.notes: Also class here: blank notebooks, autograph book, scrapbooks, photo albums, artists pads, blank drawing or painting books, blank cards, writing paper, blank sheet paper, musical score paper, and other content-free items

WZSP.label: Stationery items: art and craft supplies
WZSP.notes: Also class here: paints, crayons, crafting kits, stamp kits, painting sets, pens, pencils, brushes or other similar non-book products used for arts or crafts

X.label: Graphic novels, Comic books, Manga, Cartoons
X.notes: Use all X* codes for: general adult, teenage or children’s comic book titles in any form and from any style or tradition. DO NOT USE: code ‘X’ itself, but select specific categories from section X*. Use all X* codes with: other subject A* – W* OR Y* categories (but not both) and qualifiers where appropriate, in particular with PLACE 1*, TIME PERIOD 3* and INTEREST 5* Qualifiers. Use an XA* code to indicate the tradition, an XQ* to indicate genre plus other codes to give greater detail. NB: INTEREST AGE 5A* Qualifiers MUST be used with comic books, graphic novels or manga titles aimed at children or teenagers

XA.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: styles / traditions
XA.notes: Use for: any style, tradition or form when the content is presented as sequential art, any form of comic book. Use all XA* codes for: indicating the tradition or style which the title is from. Use XA itself only where specific tradition or type style is not known, is a mixture of different traditions or is not listed in XA* codes below. Use all XA* codes with: XQ* code(s) to indicate a genre as applicable

XAB.label: Graphic novels
XAB.notes: Use for: comic-strip publications, that are published as stand-alone works and that use illustration to tell a complete story (or narrate a work of non-fiction) in a single work rather than being part of a sequential series of stories or comic-book story-arc. A graphic novel can be fiction or non-fiction, and will usually offer a resolution of its story or narrative within the single work, even if it is part of a wider collection of works

XAD.label: European style / tradition comic books
XAD.notes: Also class here: ‘comic albums’, bandes dessinées (BDs), fumetti, euro-comics, Franco-Belgian comics. Use for: comic-strip and graphic narratives that are part of or have been inspired by the styles associated with the different European comic book traditions and that are typically published in ongoing series, often featuring the same characters, as distinct from ‘one-off’ graphic novels

XADC.label: Classic European style / tradition comic books
XADC.notes: Also class here: classic comic books which can usually be read and enjoyed by everyone from children to adults, and which are widely regarded or presented as ‘classic’ and typically but not necessarily published and in print for several decades

XAK.label: American style / tradition comic books
XAK.notes: Use for: comic-strip narratives that are part of or have been inspired by the styles associated with the comic book traditions that originated in the United States. These often feature super-hero style characters or heightened realities and were originally published in the traditional 32 page comic. They are usually part of a larger, serialised narrative, universe or story-arc that may have been published over a long period of time. This style has inspired many comics around the world and use of this code does not mean the comic is published or created in the USA, only that the work is seen as being an example of that style of comic book

XAKC.label: Classic American style / tradition comic books
XAKC.notes: Also class here: early and classic comic book characters, including from the so-called ‘Golden Age’ or ‘Silver age’ of American style comics and which can usually be read and enjoyed by everyone from children to adults, and which are widely regarded or presented as ‘classic’ and typically but not necessarily published and in print for several decades

XAM.label: Manga and other East Asian style / tradition comic books (Manhwa, Manhua, International Manga, etc)
XAM.notes: Also class here: OEL manga, Original English-language manga (and similar concepts in other languages), Manga-influenced comics, World manga, Global manga, La nouvelle manga, Manfra, Amerimanga, etc. Use for: XAM* codes includes all Japanese style comic books (Manga) plus those from other East Asian countries including Korean style (Manhwa) and Chinese style (Manhua) and from non-Asian countries, but designed according the ‘Manga or East Asian styles’. Use with: XQ* codes to give detail of subject or genre and other subject A*– W* OR Y* categories and qualifiers where appropriate

XAMA.label: Manga - (Japanese) style / tradition comics
XAMA.notes: Use with: XQ* codes to give detail of subject or genre and other subject A*– W* OR Y* categories and qualifiers where appropriate

XAMB.label: Classic East Asian style / tradition comic books
XAMB.notes: Also class here: classic East Asian style comics (Manga, Manhwa, Manhua, etc) which can usually be read and enjoyed by everyone from children to adults, and which are widely regarded or presented as ‘classic’ and typically but not necessarily published and in print for several decades

XAMC.label: Manga: Kodomo (for children)
XAMC.notes: Use for: Manga or other East Asian style comics for children, boys and girls, of an interest age from around 6 to 10. Use with: 5A* qualifiers to indicate interest age

XAMD.label: Manhwa - (Korean) style / tradition comics
XAMD.notes: Use with: XQ* codes to give detail of subject or genre and other subject A*– W* OR Y* categories and qualifiers where appropriate

XAME.label: Manhua - (Chinese) style / tradition comics
XAME.notes: Use with: XQ* codes to give detail of subject or genre and other subject A*– W* OR Y* categories and qualifiers where appropriate

XAMF.label: Manga: Shōjo (for teenage girls)
XAMF.notes: Use for: Manga or other East Asian comics designed for primarily younger teenage girls, adolescent females, of an interest age from around 10 to 15. Use with: 5A* qualifiers to indicate interest age

XAMG.label: Manga: Shōnen (for teenage boys)
XAMG.notes: Use for: Manga or other East Asian style comics designed primarily for younger teenage boys, adolescent males, of an interest age from around 10 to 15. Use with: 5A* qualifiers to indicate interest age

XAML.label: Manga: Seinen (for men)
XAML.notes: Use for: Manga or other East Asian style comics designed primarily for older teenage boys, young adult and adult men, from about 15 years old and up

XAMR.label: Manga: Josei (for women)
XAMR.notes: Use for: Manga designed primarily for older teenage girls, young adult and adult women, from about 15 years old and up

XAMT.label: Manga: Yaoi (BL / boys’ love)
XAMT.notes: Also class here: danmei, shounen-ai. Use for: Manga or other East Asian style comics featuring male same-sex relationships, created principally, but not exclusively, for a female readership. Use with: 5PSG as appropriate

XAMV.label: Manga: Bara (gay manga / Gei Komi)
XAMV.notes: Also class here: Men’s Love (ML) manga. Use for: manga or other East Asian style comics focusing on male same-sex love, usually created by gay men for a gay male audience. Use with: 5PSG and 5X as appropriate

XAMX.label: Manga: Adult (erotic, extreme violence)
XAMX.notes: Use for: Manga or other East Asian style comics designed for adults featuring scenes of an overtly adult nature only suitable for an aware and mature audience. Use with: other XAM* codes as appropriate and Qualifier 5X as appropriate

XAMX2.label: Manga: Hentai manga
XAMX2.notes: Use for: Manga or other East Asian style comics designed for adults (over about 18 years), of an extreme erotic or pornographic nature. Use with: Qualifier 5X as appropriate

XAMY.label: Manga: Yuri (GL / girls’ love)
XAMY.notes: Also class here: shoujo-ai, baihe. Use for: Manga or other East Asian style comics featuring young female same-sex relationships often (but not exclusively) for a young female readership. Use with: 5PSL as appropriate

XAX.label: Alternative comic styles / traditions
XAX.notes: Also class here: post-underground comics, independent comics, indie comics, auteur comics, small press comics, new wave comics, creator-owned comics, art comics, underground comix, etc

XQ.label: Comics (Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga etc): genres
XQ.notes: Use all XQ* codes with: F* or YF* codes, as applicable, to give further extra level of details of fiction genres where required, or, for non-fiction, with A*–W* or relevant Y* codes, as applicable, to indicate the key subject of narrative, for example a comic about an action war story use with FJM*, but one where war or conflict is the background, use with FXF

XQA.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Memoirs, true stories and non-fiction
XQA.notes: Also class here: biographies, politics, travel or other non-fiction subjects that do not have a more precise XQ* code. Use with: Non-fiction A*–W* categories to indicate the subject or Y* codes for comics aimed at children or teenagers, as appropriate

XQAY.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Educational
XQAY.notes: Use for: titles published as comics or manga where the content is primarily non-fiction and aimed at educating people about the subject. Use with: YN* codes if for young people or other relevant non-fiction A*– W* codes for titles aimed at adults, and use with relevant XA* code to indicate type. If created for use in educational institutions use with YP* codes and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate, for graphic medicine or other comics about health or medical or public health topics use with VF* codes or YPJJ6 for educational works for schools, or educational titles about science or technology, use with P* or T* codes or YPM* codes

XQB.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Literary adaptations
XQB.notes: Use for: adaptations of pre-existing literary works into graphic form. Use with: DB*, DC*, DD*, F*, YF*, YND* or YPC* codes as appropriate

XQC.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Inspired by or adapted from other media
XQC.notes: Use for: stories that were published as spin-offs or companions to pre-existing non-book media or merchandise, for example story books based on a popular film franchise, an online game or a TV series. DO NOT USE: for titles that were subsequently made into films etc

XQD.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Crime, mystery and thrillers
XQD.notes: Use with: FF* or FH* YFC* codes to give further details of crime or thriller genres where required

XQE.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Society / culture
XQE.notes: Also class here: chroniques sociales, contemporary cultural, political or social topics or issues, comics that present aspects of the arts, culture, food, cuisine, music or society either as a story or as a work of non-fiction, etc. Use with: codes from A*– W* for works of non-fiction aimed adults to give more specific details about the topic covered or Y* codes for works aimed at children or teenagers, to give further details where required

XQED.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Idol / celebrity
XQED.notes: Also class here: Idol manga, Idol manhwa. Use for: comics where the main theme of the story is about idols or celebrities, or the search to become an idol, sometimes linked to famous singers, entertainers or multimedia stars, such as stars of K-pop, as well as fictional idols or groups

XQF.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Modern and contemporary fiction / literature
XQF.notes: Use for: comic books that are works of fiction or original stories, that do not fall into another fiction genre. Use with: F* or YF* codes to give further details of fiction genres where required. Prefer: XQB for novels or other works of literature that were adapted into comics

XQG.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Action and adventure
XQG.notes: Use with: FJ* or YF* codes to indicate genre as appropriate, for example for war stories use with FJM* codes, for martial arts stories, use with FJD, or with YFC* codes for comics aimed at children or teenagers

XQGW.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Westerns

XQH.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Horror / ghost stories / supernatural
XQH.notes: Use with: FK* or other F* or YFD codes to indicate specific genres, plus VXQ* or YNX* codes as appropriate

XQJ.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Sports
XQJ.notes: Also class here: comic books featuring sports, athletic and competitive pursuits. Use with: FG or YFR for works of fiction and S* or YNW* codes for non-fiction works to give more specific details of which sport as appropriate

XQK.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Superheroes and super-villains
XQK.notes: Use with: other XQ* codes as appropriate

XQL.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Science fiction
XQL.notes: Use with: FL* or YFG* codes to give further details of science fiction genres where required

XQLM.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Science fiction: Mecha and robots
XQLM.notes: Also class here: Super-robots, real robots, transforming robots, armour, machines, AI technology

XQM.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Fantasy, esoteric
XQM.notes: Use for: comic books featuring traditions of mythical, secret or esoteric knowledge, or particular fantasy genres. Use with: FM* or YFH*codes to give further details of fantasy genres where required, plus VXQ* or YNX* codes, as appropriate

XQMM.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Fantasy: Magical Girl / Magical Boy / Magical Creature
XQMM.notes: Also class here: maho shojo, majokko. Use for: comics featuring characters with magical abilities

XQMP.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Fantasy: Portal fantasy / Isekai / Other worlds
XQMP.notes: Also class here: travel to parallel universes or other worlds, crossing to other worlds, otherworld‘s, world hopping, alternate realities

XQN.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Anthropomorphic / animal stories
XQN.notes: Use with: other XQ* codes as appropriate

XQP.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Cultural heritage and Traditional stories, myths, legends
XQP.notes: Also class here: mythic fiction, retellings. Use for: stories that often have a long and continuous existence through multiple generations, stories that get told and retold, traditional local folktales, tall tales, folklore, folk literature, wisdom tales, cautionary stories, teaching stories, origin tales, or any form of traditional story told or retold, or modern retellings or works inspired by traditional stories, mythology, legends, fairy tales or folklore in comic book or any sequential art form. Use with: FN* or YFJ or YFH codes to indicate specific genres or QR* or YNRU codes for non-fiction works plus PLACE1* qualifiers, to indicate a particular tradition, as appropriate

XQQ.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Slice of life
XQQ.notes: Also class here: Iyashikei. Use for: stories that are based on ordinary, everyday life, or parts of a character’s life, or a sequence of events in a characters life or mundane experiences in a characters life

XQR.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Romance
XQR.notes: Use with: FR* or YFM codes to give further details of romance genres where required

XQS.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: School / college life
XQS.notes: Use with: other XQ* codes or F* or YF* codes to indicate genre plus 5L* code as appropriate

XQT.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Humorous / Funny stories
XQT.notes: Use with: other XQ* codes as appropriate or WH* codes or YFQ as appropriate

XQV.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Historical / History
XQV.notes: Use with: F* codes for specific genres of historical fiction aimed at adults or YFT for historical fiction aimed at children or teenagers, OR with specific N* codes for adults or YNH* codes for works aimed at children or teenagers that are non-fiction history titles about particular periods or topics in history, and use with PLACE * plus TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

XQW.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Religious, spiritual, inspirational
XQW.notes: Use with: INTEREST 5PG* qualifiers, F* or YF* for specific genres of fiction, or QR*, VX* or YNR* codes for non-fiction titles

XQX.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Adult only content
XQX.notes: Use for: comic books designed for adults featuring scenes of an overtly adult nature or dealing with graphic themes only suitable for an aware, mature audience. Use with: Qualifier 5X plus other X* codes as appropriate

XQXE.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Adult – erotic
XQXE.notes: Use for: comic books designed for adults featuring scenes of an overtly erotic nature or dealing with graphic sexual themes only suitable for an aware mature audience. Use with: Qualifier 5X plus other X* codes as appropriate

XQXV.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Adult – extreme violence / gore
XQXV.notes: Use for: comic books designed for adults featuring scenes of an overtly violent or gory nature or dealing with graphic or disturbingly violent themes only suitable for an aware mature audience. Use with: Qualifier 5X plus other X* codes as appropriate

XR.label: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Reference, guides and reviews
XR.notes: Also class here: History of Comics, comic studies. Use with: other subject codes as appropriate, for example, with FZ for Companion works or DSB* for histories of comic books or GB* codes for reference works, or DS* for works that analyse, study, critique comic books or Graphic narrative studies, AKLC* for works about comic book art or Sequential art studies, or other subject codes for titles about comics

XRM.label: Manga and East Asian style / tradition: Reference, guides and reviews
XRM.notes: Use with: other subject codes as appropriate, for example, with FZ for Companion works or DSB* for histories of manga or GB* codes for reference works, or DS* for works that analyse, study, critique manga

XY.label: Funny cartoons and comic strips
XY.notes: Also class here: Strip cartoons, humorous comic strips or funnies. Use for: collections of typically humorous cartoons, usually originally published in newspapers or magazines or online

Y.label: Children’s, Teenage and Educational
Y.notes: Use all Y* codes for: material aimed at, or purposefully written or created for a juvenile or adolescent audience (except for graphic novels, comic books, manga in X*). DO NOT USE: code ‘Y’ itself, but select specific categories from section Y*. Use all Y* codes with: only one INTEREST AGE 5A* Qualifier to indicate a guideline starting interest age (detailed age ranges should be included in other metadata) – or for YP* use EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* qualifiers. All other qualifiers can be used as appropriate with Y* codes. DO NOT USE for: material intended primarily for adults that may also appeal to older teenagers. For ‘new adult’ content see note at 5LKE, for ‘Young Adult’ use the most appropriate 5A* Qualifier according to local usage of the term. NB: Y* codes should be used along with X* codes for graphic novels, comic books, manga. Y* codes may be used in combination with A*– W* codes but always prefer Y* codes and if mixing Y* codes with A*– W* codes, the Y* code must ALWAYS be designated as the Main Subject and sent with one 5A* qualifier. If sending A*– W* codes as Main Subject, then Y* codes should NOT be included except for JNU / JNUM with YP* or DSYC for reviews or critiques

YB.label: Children’s: picture books, activity books, early learning concepts
YB.notes: Use all YB* codes for: physical or digital items – the headings relate purely to the content, not the format (Format information is described in other metadata). Use all YB* codes with: only one INTEREST AGE 5A* Qualifier to indicate a guideline starting interest age

YBC.label: Children’s picture books
YBC.notes: Use all YBC* codes for: highly illustrated books (typically colour throughout) for children in which the content (either fiction or non-fiction) is conveyed through the use of words and pictures in combination or through pictures alone. A ‘picture book’ differs from a ‘book with illustrations’, in that the pictures it contains are at least as important as the text (if any) and form an essential component of the book. Use all YBC* codes with: other codes from Y* sections as appropriate, for example, YNB for Picture book biographies, or YPCA21 for picture books that are part of a structured reading scheme

YBCB.label: Baby books
YBCB.notes: Use for: usually small format, board, bath, cloth or rag books, picture books with little or no text, and no explicitly educational early learning content, and usually very little story. Use with: YBG* codes for baby books which involve interactivity, or with YBL* codes if there is a significant theme or topic and with one 5AB* INTEREST AGE qualifier

YBCH.label: Picture books: character books
YBCH.notes: Use for: all books based on TV or film characters, and all books featuring established pictorially-represented characters used in several books and or other products

YBCS.label: Picture storybooks
YBCS.notes: Also class here: wordless or almost-wordless picture stories. Use for: fully illustrated storybooks for children where the narrative is told mostly or entirely through pictures and where any text is totally dependent on the illustrations. Use with: relevant YF* codes to indicate the genre of story, as appropriate, or YN* or YX* categories as secondary codes for stories with specific themes. YBCS should usually be the primary or main subject when used with YF*, YN* or YX* categories. Prefer: X* codes for stories told in comic book or manga form

YBCS1.label: Picture storybooks: bedtime stories, sleep and dreams
YBCS1.notes: Use for: works that are collections or individual stories to be read out loud or listened to by children at bedtime or works about getting ready for bed, going to sleep and bedtime routines, preparing children for bedtime or works that are purposefully created to help soothe or calm a child down and prepare them for sleep or help them to sleep, or are stories about dreaming or dreams

YBCS2.label: Picture storybooks: imagination and play
YBCS2.notes: Use for: picture books featuring use of imagination and/or play, for example with toys, often to create an imaginary world

YBD.label: Children’s / Teenage: Chapter books (transitional storybooks)
YBD.notes: Use for: children’s storybooks that are primarily text, but still contain plentiful illustrations. Usually of a relatively short length and low complexity, divided into very short chapters, and intended for transitioning readers – those moving on from picture storybooks. Use with: relevant YF* codes to indicate the genre of story, as appropriate, or YN* or YX* categories as secondary codes for stories with specific themes. Prefer: X* codes for stories told in comic book or manga form

YBG.label: Children’s interactive and activity books and kits
YBG.notes: Use all YBG* codes for: children’s (of any age group) activity and interactive products; works where the primary purpose and main content of the product is an activity that requires participation and interaction, i.e. something to do or make, whether single use (e.g. press out and make, sticker books) or repeatable (e.g. touch and feel, making noises or sounds, etc). Use all YBG* codes with: other Y* codes as appropriate, and with 5H* qualifiers for activities linked to a specific holiday or season. Prefer: other Y* codes as the main category when the primary content (story or the subject) is more important than the interactivity. NB: Detailed format information is always described in other metadata

YBGC.label: Children’s interactive and activity: drawing, colouring and painting
YBGC.notes: Also class here: books to colour in, magic painting books, books and painting sets, fingerprinting, rubber stamps, connect the dots, dot to dot, paint-by-numbers, stencil books, doodles, finger painting, learning to draw or paint, books to draw in, etc

YBGH.label: Children’s interactive and activity: hidden object / search and discover
YBGH.notes: Also class here: ‘magic eye’ or ‘3D’ books, optical illusions, wimmelbooks. Use for: material where aim is to look for and find item or character in pictures, or which have illustrations packed with details to find, but do not necessarily tell a story

YBGS.label: Children’s interactive and activity: papercrafts
YBGS.notes: Also class here: origami, books of paper dolls to dress, paper models to make or assemble, things to cut out or punch-out, dioramas, paper folding, or other activities for children using paper or card

YBL.label: Early years / early learning concepts
YBL.notes: Use all YBL* codes for: pre-school material only. Use all YBL* codes with: other YN* or YX*codes to give extra detail of a significant theme or topic if appropriate and one 5AB* INTEREST AGE qualifier

YBLA.label: Early years: letters and words
YBLA.notes: Also class here: ABC and alphabet books, first word books etc

YBLB.label: Early years: verse, rhymes and wordplay
YBLB.notes: Also class here: nursery rhymes and simple verse for very young children, tongue-twisters etc

YBLG.label: Early years: prewriting skills
YBLG.notes: Also class here: Pre-handwriting skills, pregraphism or pre-graphics skills and activities, writing readiness skills, activities for learning to hold a pen or pen or pencil control and skills, tracing exercises and activities, tracing different types of lines, patterns and shapes. Use for: works that help children acquire the fundamental skills children need to develop before they are able to write or draw

YBLH.label: Early years: size, shapes and patterns

YBLJ.label: Early years: time and seasons
YBLJ.notes: Also class here: telling the time, day and night, days of the week, seasons of the year, etc

YBLM.label: Early years: daily routine
YBLM.notes: Also class here: elements of daily life for very young children: bath time and washing, meals and eating, getting up, getting dressed, brushing teeth, looking after hair, etc

YBLM1.label: Early years: potty and toilet training
YBLM1.notes: Also class here: titles that talk about poo, wee and farts. Use for: works that explain bodily functions linked to going to the toilet, as well as titles for teaching children how to use a potty or toilet

YBLN1.label: Early years: the body and the senses
YBLN1.notes: Also class here: sounds and noises, touch and feel, tastes and smells, fingers and toes, smiles and laughter, faces, peek-a-boo, hide-and-seek, etc

YBLP.label: Early years: people who help us

YBLQ.label: Early years: family
YBLQ.notes: Use with: YXF* codes as appropriate

YBLT.label: Early years: things that go
YBLT.notes: Also class here: books on ships, planes, trains, trucks, cars, bikes, buses, diggers, tractors, and other moving vehicles for the very young

YD.label: Children’s / Teenage poetry, anthologies, annuals
YD.notes: Use all YD* codes with: INTEREST AGE 5A* Qualifiers as appropriate

YDA.label: Children’s / Teenage: Annuals / yearbooks / almanacs
YDA.notes: Also class here: all annuals, yearly publications, periodicals or similar aimed at children or teenagers. Use for: material published every year, usually dated and thematic. Use with: second Y* code indicating type or subject area where possible

YDC.label: Children’s / Teenage: Anthologies
YDC.notes: Use with: other code denoting literary form where appropriate, e.g. with a YF* code for fiction anthologies, with YDP for poetry anthologies. Use alone for anthologies of various literary forms

YF.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction and true stories
YF.notes: Use all YF* codes with: one 5A* INTEREST AGE Qualifier; with PLACE 1*, TIME PERIOD 3* or INTEREST 5* Qualifiers where these aspects are particularly pertinent and significant; with appropriate non-fiction categories YN* or YX* to indicate key settings or topics of the narrative, but NOTE for ALL Children’s and teenage fiction the primary category MUST be an YF* code; with 5H*, 5J*, 5L* or 5P* qualifiers when these represent a significant topic or part of the appeal of the narrative; with 5X, where appropriate, to indicate material that may have themes or topics only be suitable for older or mature teenagers; with YB* to indicate the genre of a picture or chapter book; with YDC for fiction anthologies; YFZ* codes may be used to indicate special features of a fiction title. Prefer: X* codes for fiction told in comic book or manga form

YFA.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Classic fiction
YFA.notes: Use for: children’s and teenage fiction widely regarded or presented as ‘classic’ and typically but not necessarily published and in print for several decades

YFB.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: General, modern and contemporary fiction
YFB.notes: Use for: all contemporary non-genre fiction for children and teenagers. Use with: YX* or YN* codes to highlight the main theme of the story, for example, social issues, realistic or gritty fiction can be indicated using appropriate YX* codes, when the major theme is growing up or coming of age, use YXW, a story about illness use with YXL*, etc

YFC.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Action and adventure stories

YFCA.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Interactive adventure stories
YFCA.notes: Use for: books, physical or digital, where the reader can select from options to alter the narrative outcome. Use with: other YF* code indicating genre

YFCF.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Crime and mystery fiction

YFCW.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Military and war fiction

YFD.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Horror and ghost stories, chillers, or other scary supernatural stories
YFD.notes: Also class here: scary stories of the paranormal, gothic ghost stories, contemporary and realistic horror stories. Use for: any story that is written to be scary or to give an age appropriate feeling of fear, including stories that turn out not to be scary, stories that feature ghosts (friendly or scary), monsters (frightening or misunderstood), witches (wicked or misrepresented), creepy settings, characters or beings, haunted houses or is any form of supernatural chilling, spooky or scary story. Use with: YNX* codes for stories about specific supernatural or paranormal beings, such as YNXB3 for ghost stories, or other YF* codes, such as YFQ for funny or comedy ghost or horror stories, YFJM for cautionary tales, YFH* for fantasy scary stories, YFHG for horror stories based on myths, YFHT for Dark fantasy horror stories, YFA for classic ghost or horror stories, etc

YFE.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Speculative, dystopian and utopian fiction
YFE.notes: Also class here: fiction set in dystopian or utopian societies, alternative history fiction. Use with: YFG or other YF* codes if possible

YFEB.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic stories
YFEB.notes: Also class here: end of the world stories, dying earth, collapsing or collapsed civilizations. Use for: stories set in worlds trying to prevent, or experiencing or that have already been affected by an apocalypse event, such as runaway climate change, an impact event, resource depletion, nuclear holocaust, pandemics, end times, zombie apocalypse, cybernetic revolts, technological singularity, invasion from space, dysgenics, etc

YFF.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Superhero stories
YFF.notes: Use for: stories for children or teenagers with a superhero character or where the main characters are depicted as superheroes

YFG.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Science fiction
YFG.notes: Use with: YNTT for Time travel, time slip, or time loop sci-fi stories, YNXF for stories about extra-terrestrials or UFOs, YNNZ for stories about space travel, YNTC for stories about AI, Mecha, robots or new technology, etc

YFGR.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Space opera
YFGR.notes: Also class here: Galactic empires, interstellar or intergalactic wars. Use for: science fiction stories set in space, in imagined galaxies or universes, or on different planets, often with advanced cultures and sophisticated technology and usually featuring main characters who are children or teenagers

YFGS.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Steampunk
YFGS.notes: Also class here: dieselpunk, cyberpunk, retrofuturism. Use for: science fiction based on an alternative world where, for example in the case of steampunk, 19th century steam power has emerged as the dominant technology

YFH.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Fantasy
YFH.notes: Also class here: paranormal fantasy, enchanted journeys, alternative worlds, accidental travel, portal fantasy, Isekai. Use all YFH* codes with: YNX* codes as appropriate, with YNXB* codes for stories featuring the paranormal or particular supernatural beings

YFHB.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Epic fantasy / heroic fantasy
YFHB.notes: Also class here: sword and sorcery fantasy, quest fantasy, high fantasy

YFHD.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Magical realism / Magical fantasy
YFHD.notes: Also class here: Magical girl. Use for: works that incorporates fantastic, magical, mythical or supernatural elements into an otherwise real-world or mundane setting, or works where the magic itself – whether a magical object or a character with magical powers – is the subject of the story, rather than simply a means to an end. Use with: YNXW for stories about witches, wizards or magicians or YNXB* codes for other magical creatures

YFHG.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Mythic fantasy / Myths and Legends fiction
YFHG.notes: Also class here: Myths or legends from any culture told or retold as fiction or in story form, mythological fiction, Arthurian fantasy, Classical fantasy (based on Greek and Roman myths), Shenmo (Gods and Demons), etc. Use for: fiction that is inspired by, or a retelling of, or that in some way draws from the characters, stories or themes of myth, legend, for example, a story based on a popular myth or character from a classic work in a modern setting or a story based on a minor character’s perspective, or that takes a ‘what if’ approach or create a mashup of different genres, for example, legendary character or hero meets dystopian future, or mythology crossed with contemporary adventure story. Use with: PLACE 1*, LANGUAGE 2*, INTEREST 5* Qualifiers to indicate if the story is taken from a particular tradition

YFHH.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Historical fantasy
YFHH.notes: Also class here: Medieval, Dark Age, Arabian, Celtic, Gunpowder, Prehistoric, Wuxia fantasy. Use for: fantasy that incorporates fantastic elements, such as magic or supernatural beings, into recognisable historic settings, periods, cultures etc. Use with: PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers to indicate setting as appropriate

YFHR.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Fantasy romance
YFHR.notes: Also class here: Romantasy, romantic fantasy, vampire romance, paranormal romance etc. Use for: Fantasy stories using many of the elements and conventions of romance but that is primarily a fantasy novel. Use with: YNXB* codes for romance stories featuring the paranormal, supernatural or particular supernatural beings, 5X code if content is more explicit and INTEREST AGE 5A* Qualifiers as appropriate

YFHT.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Dark fantasy
YFHT.notes: Use for: fantasy stories with darker and frightening themes, often incorporating elements of horror or that have a gloomy and threatening atmosphere or a sense of horror and dread

YFHW.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Contemporary and urban fantasy
YFHW.notes: Use for: fantasy set in the present day or recognisably contemporary settings (according to the time period of its creator)

YFJ.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction and true stories: Cultural heritage / traditional stories
YFJ.notes: Also class here: Fables, stories that have a long and continuous existence through multiple generations, stories that get told and retold, stories from particular cultural traditions, stories written down from oral traditions, tall tales, myths or legends retold in a story form. Use all YFJ* codes for: modern retellings in story form or collections of these type of traditional stories aimed at children / teenagers. Use with: PLACE 1*, LANGUAGE 2*, INTEREST 5* Qualifiers as appropriate

YFJB.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Folk and Fairy tales
YFJB.notes: Also class here: Fairy tale retellings, fractured fairy tales. Use for: folk and fairy tales from any culture told in a story form, or retellings of these stories, stories inspired by fairy tales

YFJH.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Trickster tales
YFJH.notes: Use for: stories that feature a trickster character such as a spirit, a deity, a human or an animal

YFJK.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Creation, founding, origin stories
YFJK.notes: Use for: stories about the origins or beginnings of peoples, worlds, places, traditions, etc

YFJM.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Teaching stories
YFJM.notes: Also class here: Cautionary tales, Wisdom tales. Use for: stories that were created for the transmission of wisdom, knowledge, cultural traditions, oral transmission of stories, or stories that warn or caution young people about specific dangers, to teach a lesson or a general moral issue

YFK.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Religious and spiritual stories
YFK.notes: Also class here: Faith-inspired or inspirational stories. Use for: fiction that promotes a particular religious, spiritual or visionary message or viewpoint. Use with: 5PG* values from INTEREST 5* Qualifiers or YNR* codes, to indicate the religious tradition, as appropriate

YFM.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Relationship stories
YFM.notes: Use for: stories that deal with all kinds of relationships with others; for stories where interpersonal relationships are the main theme; or explore the relationship of the main characters, stories that explore relationships within groups, relationships between young people. Use with: YX* to give details of kinds of relationships as appropriate, for example, YXH for stories about relationships in peer groups or relationships with adults from a young persons perspective, 5PHG for stories about found or chosen family

YFMF.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Friendship stories
YFMF.notes: Use for: stories where the main or primary topic or theme of the narrative is the friendship between different child or teenage main characters

YFMR.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Romance and love stories
YFMR.notes: Also class here: contemporary romance, romantic comedy, romantic drama, stories of first or young love, teenage romances, teenage love-triangles, lost love, unrequited love, high school romance, etc. Use for: stories that are clearly of the romance genre and feature a romantic relationship as the core theme, that are specifically written for teenagers and deal with romance or love stories from a teenage point of view. Use with: YX* codes as appropriate, with YFT and TIME PERIOD 3* qualifiers for Historical romance, with YFQ for comic romance, etc

YFN.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Family and home stories
YFN.notes: Use for: titles where families, family members or home is the main theme of a story or for stories about topics to do with any kind of family. Use with: codes from YXF* sequence for fiction specifically designed to address family issues, or with 5PH* for stories about particular relationships within a family or types of family

YFP.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Nature and animal stories
YFP.notes: Use for: stories featuring animals, or the natural world, or stories about human interaction or relationships with animals and the natural world, stories about the bond between a child and an animal or pet. Use with: YNN* codes to indicate what type of animal or nature story, for example YNNJ24 for Horse stories or YNN21 for stories about Dogs, YNNH* codes for stories about pets, YNNT for stories about plants or trees

YFQ.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Humorous stories
YFQ.notes: Also class here: Comical fiction, Stories that make you giggle or laugh, laugh out loud funny books. Use with: other YF* code indicating genre if possible

YFR.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Sporting stories
YFR.notes: Use with: YNW* codes to indicate the sport in the story

YFS.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: School stories
YFS.notes: Also class here: back to school, going to a new school, school life, stories principally taking place in and around school, etc. Use with: values from 5L* to indicate what school level as appropriate

YFT.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Historical fiction
YFT.notes: Use for: stories set in the past (usually before the writer’s lifetime), where the time period is a significant or essential part of the story and that portray the spirit, manners, and social conditions of that time with realistic detail. Use with: other YF* codes as appropriate, and PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers to indicate setting as appropriate

YFU.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Short stories
YFU.notes: Use with: other YF* code indicating genre if possible

YFV.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Stories in verse
YFV.notes: Use for: stories for children or teenagers written entirely in verse form rather than prose. Use with: other YF* or YBC* codes indicating genre if possible. Prefer: YDP for poems or collections of poetry

YFX.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Biographical fiction / autobiographical stories
YFX.notes: Also class here: fictional life writing, autobiographical stories, autofiction. Use for: highly fictionalised biographies or autobiographies of real people or where an author is using fictionalised versions of real life memories or experiences from their own life as an integral and major part of the narrative or story

YFY.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: True stories told as fiction
YFY.notes: Also class here: true events or true stories, e.g. of survival, discovery, conflict etc, told in strong narrative from, as if fiction. Use with: other Y Codes to give details of the topic and PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3*, INTEREST 5* qualifiers as appropriate

YFZ.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction / Literature / Comics / Graphic novels: Special features and related items
YFZ.notes: Use all YFZ* codes with: other YF* code indicating genre or type, YDP for poems, YNDS for plays, or YBCS for picture storybooks or XQ* codes for graphic novels, comic books or manga aimed at children or teenagers. NB: YFZ* codes should not usually be the primary or main subject code. DO NOT USE: YFZ itself - always use YFZ* codes

YFZC.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Advent calendar stories
YFZC.notes: Use for: stories aimed at children or teenagers, usually in 24 or 25 chapters or stories, meant to be read, heard or seen as a countdown to Christmas through the Advent season. Use with: 5HPDA

YFZD.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: stories as diaries / journals / letters
YFZD.notes: Also class here: Epistolary fiction. Use for: fiction, often with illustrations, written or drawn in a series of documents, letters, diaries, emails, blogs, social media posts, doodles, etc. Use with: other YF* or XQ* code indicating genre or type

YFZH.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: retellings
YFZH.notes: Use for: stories that are reworkings, reimagining’s or retellings of stories, histories or tales. Use with: other YF* or XQ* code indicating genre or type

YFZR.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: category / serialised stories
YFZR.notes: Use for: genre fiction, or comic books usually published on a monthly basis, short, in clearly delineated lines and with a certain number published every month. Use with: other YF* or XQ* code indicating genre or type. YFZR codes should never be the main subject code

YFZS.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Ranobe (‘light novels’)
YFZS.notes: Also class here: Illustrated novellas. Use for: short fiction for children or teenagers, usually driven primarily by dialogue and character, and generally accompanied by illustrations in manga/anime or similar styles. Use with: other YF* codes to indicate the genre

YFZT.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Stories in translation
YFZT.notes: Use for: fiction in translation from another language. Use with: YF*, YBCS, YDP, YNDS, or XQ* codes to ensure classification is meaningful beyond the translation of the work itself and with 5T* - Literature of Place Qualifiers as appropriate. DO NOT USE: PLACE 1* or LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers to describe the detail of the original language, this would be described elsewhere and not using Thema. You may still use a PLACE Qualifier if it is relevant to the plot or setting of the book. DO NOT USE: YFZT as the main or primary subject or the only code

YFZV.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Stories Inspired by or adapted from other media
YFZV.notes: Use for: stories that were published as spin-offs or companions to pre-existing non-book media or merchandise, for example story books based on a popular film franchise, toy, an online game or a TV series. DO NOT USE: for titles that were subsequently made into films etc. Use with: other YF*, YBCS, YDP, YNDS, or XQ* codes indicating genre or type. NB: YFZV codes should never be the main subject code

YFZW.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Game-related / LitRPG stories
YFZW.notes: Also class here: Literary Role Playing Game, GameLit, RoLit. Use for: fiction that is structured like a videogame, or features the same kind of challenges as would be found in a game, or is about or set in a videogame. Use with: other YF* or XQ* codes as appropriate

YFZZ.label: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Companion works
YFZZ.notes: Use for: companion works to popular children’s or teenage fiction series or titles, typically uncritical, such as an atlas or map of a mythical world or fictional universe, a compendium of characters or objects, a guide to the series, art inspired by or taken from the series etc. Use with: other Y* codes or on its own as appropriate, or with X* codes for companion works to graphic novels, comics, manga aimed at children or teenagers

YN.label: Children’s / Teenage: General interest
YN.notes: Use for: all general interest material not covered elsewhere and not designed specifically for school use. Use all YN* codes for: non-fiction works. Use all YN* codes with: INTEREST AGE 5A* Qualifiers, with relevant YF* code for fiction on specific topics, as appropriate. NB: YN may be used with A* – W* codes to indicate the topic when there is no more specific Y* code or qualifier but if mixing YN codes with A* – W* codes, the YN code or another Y* code MUST be designated as the Main Subject and sent with a 5A* qualifier

YNA.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Art and artists
YNA.notes: Also class here: painters, paintings, photography and photographers, etc. Use with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate, YNB for biographies, YNP for practical, how to titles

YNB.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Biography and autobiography
YNB.notes: Also class here: biographies of people from the past and present. Use for: both individual biographies and works that have multiple biographies of different people, titles about heroes or heroines, inspirational figures, famous and everyday people, diaries or journals of individuals. Use with: other YN* codes for particular genres of biography

YNC.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Music and musicians
YNC.notes: Also class here: titles about music, or particular musicians, pop groups, etc. Use with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate, YNB for biographies of singers, musicians or groups

YNCB.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Musical instruments
YNCB.notes: Also class here: musical instruction, learning to play the piano, the recorder, the guitar, musical scores, etc. Use with: AVR* codes to indicate specific instruments if more detail is appropriate. NB: if mixing Y* codes with AVR* codes, the Y* code MUST be designated as the Main Subject and sent with a 5A* qualifier

YNCS.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Songbooks / singing
YNCS.notes: Also class here: song scores, sing along, learning to sing. Use with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate

YND.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Drama and performing arts
YND.notes: Also class here: circus, acting techniques, stagecraft, theatre, auditions, etc. Use with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate, or with YNB for biographies of performers

YNDB.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Dance, ballet
YNDB.notes: Also class here: learning to dance. Use with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate, or with YNB for biographies of dancers or dance groups

YNF.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Television, video and film
YNF.notes: Also class here: titles about making of a film, TV, series, streaming, digital filmmaking, animation, radio, podcasting, etc. Use with: STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate, or with YNB for biographies of actors, TV, film or video stars, personalities or celebrities

YNG.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: General knowledge and interesting facts

YNGL.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Information resources
YNGL.notes: Also class here: titles about libraries, museums, schools, using and finding information, guides to using information resources, etc. Use for: informative books about museums, galleries, libraries other cultural centres, and their content

YNH.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: History and the past
YNH.notes: Also class here: archaeology, histories of countries, places, peoples, cultures, groups, etc. Use with: PLACE 1*, LANGUAGE 2*, TIME PERIOD 3*, INTEREST 5* or STYLE 6* Qualifiers as appropriate, for histories of particular civilizations, places, peoples, groups, styles or periods of human prehistory and history and with YNB for biographies of specific people from the past, YR* codes for encyclopaedias, timelines of history, or other Y* codes for histories of particular topics for children or teenagers

YNHA.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Adventurers and outlaws
YNHA.notes: Also class here: treasure hunters, seafarers, famous individual or groups of heroes or villains from history, stories of people from the past who were adventurers or heroes, etc. Use with: with YNB for biographies and PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

YNHD.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Discovery and exploration
YNHD.notes: Also class here: explorers, travellers, expedition, first contacts with other continents and peoples, exploring interiors, the seas, or stories of people who were travellers, voyagers, pioneers or explorers etc. Use with: with YNB for biographies and PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

YNHP.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Lives of children in the past
YNHP.notes: Use with: PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

YNJ.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Warfare, battles, armed forces
YNJ.notes: Also class here: soldiers, gladiators, warriors, wars, uniforms, military vehicles. Use with: other YN* codes and PLACE 1* and TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

YNJC.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Castles and knights

YNK.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Work, politics and society
YNK.notes: Also class here: business, the world of work, working or different jobs, specific professions, daily life, everyday occurrences, first jobs, aspects of society or contemporary culture, cultural phenomenon, entrepreneurs, everyday happenings, etc. Use with: YNH for history titles, YXZ* for social issues

YNKA.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Politics and government
YNKA.notes: Use for: titles about politicians, politics, political activity, political institutions, government, human rights, political debates, geopolitics explain different political concepts, ideologies, political strategies, political parties or movements, single issues politics, to young people. Use with: YNB and YNH, as appropriate, for biographies of political figures or history titles. NB: YNKA may be used with JP* codes to give extra detail if there is no specific Y* code or qualifier but if mixing YNKA with JP* codes, a Y* code MUST be designated as the Main Subject and sent with a 5A* code

YNKC.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Law, police and crime
YNKC.notes: Use for: works that look at topics around crime, legal matter, law enforcement or are about those that work in these roles, police officers, judges, lawyers, etc or look at criminals or criminality. Use with: YNB for biographies of people in this domain or YNH for history titles

YNKG.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Medical and emergency services
YNKG.notes: Also class here: doctors, nurses, health workers, carers, ambulances, paramedics, fire and rescue services, lifeboat services, mountain rescue, a visit to the hospital, the doctor, the dentist, the fire station, etc. Use for: works about the medical, health care and emergency sectors or the people who work in these sectors. Use with: YNB for biographies of people in this domain

YNL.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Literature, books and writers
YNL.notes: Use with: YNB for biographies of writers

YNM.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Communities, places and peoples

YNXB4.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Fairies, elves, or similar magic-like beings or folk

YNXB5.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Unicorns
YNXB5.notes: Use with: YB* or YF* codes for stories about or featuring, or encounters with unicorns or similar creatures or animals

YNXB6.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Mermaids / mermen / merfolk
YNXB6.notes: Also class here: sirens, water spirits, kelpies, selkies, seal folk. Use with: YB* or YF* codes for stories about or featuring any of these beings or similar water folk, beings or spirits

YNXB7.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Giants, trolls and other mythical humanoids
YNXB7.notes: Also class here: dwarves, ogres, gnomes, bigfoot, yetis. Use for: legendary, folkloric, or mythological creatures that are part human, or that resemble humans or encounters with them. Use with: YB* or YF* codes for stories about or featuring any of these beings

YNXF.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: UFOs and extraterrestrial beings

YNXW.label: Children’s / Teenage general interest: Witches, wizards and magicians

YPCK91.label: Educational: Modern (non-native or second) languages: School editions of literature texts

YXAB.label: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: Fitness, exercise and healthy eating
